9	## Ledger authority and commits
10	- Mutations enter Host authority and commit one durable operation. Projections, Inbox, tools, commands, Remote responses, and UI derive from committed operations; Client code never interprets ledger records or creates parallel authority.
11	
12	- Replay re-derives each record's expected Inbox delta and compares it exactly, so a release that changes how an existing kind is validated first records `team/rules-version-adopted` (Host actor, `{ version }`). Each record validates under the newest marker before it; a ledger with none is version 1. `initialize` appends the marker inside its own queued commit, so it precedes every later write, startup recovery included. Markers only ascend, at most one per version, and a build refuses a ledger adopted at a version above its own.
13	- Current builds implement version 2: mounting a ledger whose newest marker is lower appends the version 2 marker, and a fresh ledger records it right after `team/initialized`.
14	- Behind version 2 the Host also commits `team/main-message-posted`, `team/main-stream-read` and `team/thread-started`, which a version-1 segment rejects, while `team/message-sent` is rejected in a version-2 segment. The Host no longer writes `team/message-sent` (a Thread starts with `startThread`); it replays only inside version-1 segments.
15	- An inbox delta may carry an optional `mainMarkers` list with its own marker shape (`projectRef` plus a `messageRef` or `activityRef`). It appears only when it changes something, so version-1 records keep their stored bytes, and a departing Member's Main stream markers clear in the same operation as its other inbox state.
16	- An inbox delta may also carry an optional `mainAttention` list (`set` of Main stream Attention rows, `removed` of their keys), with the same "only when it changes something" rule, so every delta written before Main stream Attention existed keeps its stored bytes. `team/main-attention-changed` is the kind that writes it; its row is keyed by Member × Project and never enters a Thread index.
17	- An Attention row carries the `source` that established it: `thread-author`, `claim`, `accountable`, `project-owner`, `mention`, or `self`. It is optional in storage, so rows written before it existed keep their bytes.
18	- On load, a missing cause is derived from the operation that wrote the row: an ownership grant reads as `project-owner`, a Claim as `claim`, a Thread start as `thread-author`, a transfer or reopen as `accountable`, and a legacy read inherits the existing Attention row's cause. The repaired row then participates in strict replay validation, so old records keep their stored shape without weakening the comparison.
19	- An Agent is woken from its Main stream markers through the same direct-notification path as a Thread marker, and an ordinary Main stream update its Attention covers is delivered immediately. Every unread fact interrupts, so an ordinary Thread update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread: no identity — owner or accountable — sits in a slower class, and nothing accumulates a count first. `covered` is the process-memory signature that stops an unchanged rederivation spending a second attempt; a queued but unread notice is replaced, not stacked.
20	- A reply records the Message it answers as `replyToMessageRef` on the Message itself, and the Host resolves that ref against the ledger before committing: an unknown ref, or one belonging to another Thread, is refused rather than stored.
21	- The parent's author joins the recipients at commit and takes a direct marker exactly as a mention does — the same resolution, the same markers, no invitation step. Under rules version 2 `undeliveredMentions` is never populated: every addressable recipient is delivered, whether or not the Thread ever carried it, and nothing follows as a side effect. Reporting an undelivered remainder is the version-1 compatibility path alone.
22	- The quoted picture — the parent's author and one line of its body — is a read-time derivation (`replyTo`), never a second stored copy. It therefore cannot disagree with the parent and still fills in when the parent sits outside the page being read. A ref that no longer resolves stays a bare ref. Quoting is not optional: the parameter is part of the reply contract, and a reply carrying a ref is accepted or refused on the ref alone.
23	
24	## Lifecycle and notifications
25	- Agent lifecycle, JSON/SQLite replay, authorization, idempotency, and revision checks stay on Host. Durable unread changes may produce one bounded coalesced Agent context notification through the public safe boundary: direct mentions carry their Message and source, Task/Claim Activities carry a concise transition, and ordinary unread carries only a body-free Thread-first route. Promotion is a Task activity and reaches followers through Activity markers. Notifications are not a second authority and do not promise exactly-once model processing.
26	- A committed Session transition (`team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-rolled-over`, `team/member-session-recycled`) records the desired binding, not a completed one: retiring the old generation and activating the target are Host effects outside the ledger write. Startup and the explicit Member recovery action both finish an interrupted transition from the recorded previous Session, and each effect derives its own completion — a live handle never proves the archive half ran. A repeated request answers with the recorded receipt and an honest status, never a second binding.
27	- Every durable Member state has one desired external effect set — the [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.md#member-lifecycle) table. Each lifecycle operation re-runs that set right after its commit, and startup re-runs it for every non-enabled Member, so an archive, suspension, or removal interrupted by a crash or a failed Workspace/Session/filesystem call converges by repeating the same derivation rather than by a second durable write.
28	- Startup never activates a non-enabled Member: an effect that fails during startup is logged and retried at the next boot instead of failing the boot. Lifecycle operations for one Member stay serialized in submission order, while different Members never queue behind each other's waits.
29	- Task reminders are Host-owned `team/reminder-raised` operations evaluated after Team events, never timers. Their optional `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta is private to one recipient; replay retains the complete episode for deduplication after its marker is consumed.
30	- Reminder operations invalidate the Task Thread change scope so the Human Inbox refreshes, but add no public fact or revision. Acceptance, close, and lifecycle cleanup remove obsolete unread markers while retaining episode history. Agent idle observations are process-local, retained across generation replacement and discarded on Host restart; unknown idle never satisfies a time condition.
31	
32	- After the ledger append, delivery effects follow — commit listeners, Client change invalidation, the participation notice, and one wake per affected Member. Each runs in a boundary that logs a failure instead of failing the operation, so a failed listener or wake still answers with the committed result, not a false rollback; only invariant divergence still rejects. A failed Inbox wake clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable Inbox facts and retries without a second append. DM keeps its explicit recorded-but-not-delivered error.
33	
34	## Which operations wake a Member, and how recovery is chosen
35	
36	A wake is one bounded coalesced notice the Host delivers over one of four causes, each carrying the durable fact that produced it:
37	
38	| Cause | What produced it |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| `commit` | any committed operation touching the Member: a mention, a DM, a Task activity, a promotion, an accepted answer |
41	| `transition` | a recorded `team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-recycled`, or legacy `team/member-session-rolled-over` whose retire and activation effects complete out of order; the rederived Inbox is sequenced after any carried input |
42	| `activation` | a fresh activation, carrying the previous Session id when input was carried forward |
43	| `running` | the Member's own `agent/status` going `running` — one wake per transition, not per step |
44	
45	Waking is not a second authority and never promises exactly-once model processing. A wake that fails delivery clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable facts and retries without a second append.
46	
47	`recoverMember` is the manual path and picks exactly one of these, in order:
48	
49	| Condition | Action | Use it when |
50	| --- | --- | --- |
51	| handle absent, or the live handle's Session id is not the recorded binding, and a recorded transition exists | finish the recorded transition | a crash or a failed effect left a Session transition half-applied |
52	| durable state is not `enabled` but a live handle survives | finish that state's effects | a suspend, archive, or removal committed but its disposal failed |
53	| a live handle whose preset composition is gone | reactivate in place | a reload lost the preset composition, so the Member's tools are unavailable |
54	| no live handle at all | reactivate | the activation itself failed |
55	| otherwise | steer a resume prompt | the Member is alive, composed, and bound — every other state has already been handled |
56	
57	An error-state Member with a live handle is the last row: `recoverMember` steers it, and a cause that is still present makes the next turn fail again. Distinguish the two before choosing: a broken model route or a rejecting gateway is fixed by changing the route, not by recovering the Member, and steering recovers nothing until the route answers. Recovery never resets a context generation: a stranded Member whose binding already moved finishes that recorded transition, and nothing in the Remote surface renews or rolls a Session over.
58	
59	A Member's current failure reason is carried on its status as a `diagnostic` and rendered by the Client. It is derived from the live surface, not persisted: after a Host restart it is re-derived only if something wakes the Member, so an un-woken Member shows no reason until the next operation touches it.
60	
61	## Projections and the change stream
62	- The `contextContinuity` unit folds live Session events through the Harness projection registry. It retains only the legacy intent, checkpoint, continuation and unanswered-input facts needed for recovery; activation and retired-Session recovery can also fold an inspected log in full.
63	- The Member clock baseline uses `session-event-cursor.ts` to consume only appended events. The cursor restarts when the Session identity, inherited prefix, length or anchor event changes. Its guard relies on the append-only log contract; an in-place replacement with the same sequence and event type is not detected.
64	- `changes()` is a streaming Remote with one optional scope (workspace/project/thread/presence); an omitted scope observes shared Team projection changes, not presence. Host registers the listener before emitting the current baseline, then emits matching invalidations, retaining only the latest pending version while a consumer pauses. Cancellation or Host disposal closes the subscription.
65	- Thread reads and `team/dm-sent` change no shared projection, so neither advances its version nor wakes subscribers. A private reminder does invalidate its Task Thread scope: that is how an open Human Inbox learns about it, without turning it into public Thread history.
66	
67	  Presence uses a process-local epoch; other scopes report the latest shared-projection ledger sequence. Versions are meaningful only within their scope and Host lifetime. Host recomputes Inbox hints only for Members affected by an operation.
68	- `TeamChangeStream` shares one logical stream per scope within each page through `ctx.remote.$stream()`; Harness owns the shared `/api/remote.mux` WebSocket and connection recovery. Each new baseline, including an unchanged or lower version after reconnection, requests a fresh Host read. This closes the initial-read race and recovers failed reads without a new commit. The last listener leaving disposes that scope; plugin disposal closes all scopes. Carrier failures are reported once until recovery; terminal failures are reported without a Team-owned retry loop.
69	
70	  Team has no long-poll fallback, cross-page leader election, or single-active-page restriction. Concurrent supplemental reads coalesce notifications and retain a trailing read when another notification arrives during a fetch, rather than suppressing reconnect baselines by an old version. The Human Inbox badge subscribes without a scope, debounces Inbox totals, and also refreshes after local Thread reads. Presence subscriptions update Member availability without waking the Inbox. Notifications are invalidation hints, never a second facts store.
71	- Read projections are bounded by purpose. `view` answers the requested fact page plus the Thread it names: its catalog fields carry that page's Tasks, Threads, display ordinals and Claims. Only `includeCatalog` returns the Task/Thread/Claim catalog of the whole request scope — the address-book projection the model-facing `team_view` renders.
72	- A page read walks the fact ledger until one match past its limit; a catalog read adds one directory filter over the Threads in scope plus one live-Claim lookup per Task row. Those are the components to report separately, never as one total: a returned row count alone does not show what a read walked.
73	- Claims are bucketed per Task by a replay-derived index, so a per-Task read — a Claim list, a Thread picture, an Inbox row, the Task board — never walks the ledger's whole Claim set. Every index here is rebuilt by replay, never a second durable authority.
74	
75	## Session persistence and replay
76	- The bundle targets DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` and uses the current DSH Session persistence: the shipped JSONL backend migrates released historical formats itself (v0/v1/v2 → V3 → V4), and old-format Session data needs no manual disposal. Team nevertheless retains a narrow replay normalization for old pre-Message `occurredAt` records, and exactly one record shape still reaches it: the pre-receipt `team/thread-read` snapshot, which froze Message anchors and Thread facts beside the Inbox delta it consumed.
77	
78	  That is the only Thread-read form that stores an instant at all — the receipt every current read writes carries progress and its Inbox delta only — and it is normalized and validated in place, never rewritten. Do not add Team Session migration, broad compatibility reads, or fallback storage paths.
79	
80	## Attention and Inbox authority
81	- Thread Attention is private Member × Thread state. The Host is the only Inbox authority. Session history may retain bounded notification context but never a parallel unread projection.
82	- The Inbox read ranks the reader's whole unread queue, then materializes preview text, the instant's person and live Claim owners only for the rows it returns; its totals stay whole-queue, so a one-row badge still reports every unread Thread. `threadObservations` returns the newest `limit` observations with `hasMore`, and its follower set is always the complete current state.
83	
84	## Sessions, policy, and context pressure
85	- Team-managed Agent sessions use the explicit Team preset and trusted `danger-full-access` policy. An untitled Member session receives its handle as a title; explicit or previous titles win.
86	- Member context is owned by two Host-side mechanisms and no model tool (see Tools and preset): Team controls request budgets through its preset adapter over the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine`, which shortens an oversized Session in place, and the generation coordinator swaps a cold Session at a wake boundary, recording `team/member-session-recycled` as the Host actor. [`memory-and-context.md`](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns the pressure and wake thresholds.
87	- A swapping generation reports unavailable with a `rollover` diagnostic until its successor activates, so a Client following the row never opens a Session that does not exist yet.
88	- A swap carries input, not context: the commit records the retired log's offset and the successor replays only the input at or after it, deduplicated by Message id, using the original durable inbox insertions even for already-claimed input. Nothing is copied through process memory (see [Tools and preset](tools-and-preset.md)).
89	- Pending/error bookkeeping is process-local; only compactions in a transaction add Session history.
90	- Terminal recovery classifies each `agent/error` from structured Harness data before any wording. The stable code decides alone — `RATE_LIMIT` is rate limiting, `TRANSPORT`/`TIMEOUT` a transient network failure, an explicit 429/503 response rate limiting — and any other code (quota, auth, context, request) stays manual whatever its message says. Only a codeless error falls back to the narrow message signatures.
91	- `agent/error` owns terminal recovery with its consecutive-error limit, and the failure keeps its recorded Member diagnostic.
92	- A Team wake discarded before any `turn/start` is the one error diagnostic with no `agent/error` behind it. A Team-owned Inbox or recovery notice that leaves the queue before the turn opens, and that the Host did not replace or dispose, records a `runtime` diagnostic with `source: 'agent/inbox/discarded'`, the `sessionId`, and `occurredAt`. A notice the Host replaces or disposes raises nothing, so ordinary replacement never errors. Like every runtime diagnostic it is process-local, re-derived only on the next wake.
93	
94	## Private memory, archival, and identity effects
95	- Private-memory directories under `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/` are Host-owned effects of Member identity. Activation ensures the directory, `notes/`, and missing `memory.md`; startup does not prune unknown directories. Explicit removal archives the Session and removes that Member's private directory; unrelated entries remain untouched.
96	
97	  Both that removal and the activation-time rename of a pre-fix colon directory are confined to the running process's own members root. The recorded `privateMemoryPath` is a durable absolute fact that names a directory in whichever DSH home added the Member, so a process resolving another home refuses to move or delete it (with a warning) instead of taking the Member's real private memory out of its home.
98	- Member and Project archival is the reversible third state between suspend and remove. `archiveMember` commits `team/member-archived`, disposes the live session (private memory and the Session log stay on disk), archives the Session from grouping surfaces, and releases the Member's active Claims with public `claims_released` Activities plus Attention/marker cleanup. A hidden Member must not leave Tasks stuck in progress or phantom unread counts.
99	
100	  `archiveProject` commits `team/project-archived` with the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads; Memberships survive both archival forms (hidden state, not departure).
101	
102	  Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface — projections (view projects/threads/tasks/members, mention candidates, Project joins, edits), ref resolution (`resolveTaskRefs`/`resolveThreadRefs` skip them so message bodies render plain text), and ref-addressed reads (`readThread`/`threadHistory`/`threadObservations`/`listClaims` reject with an explicit archived error, never an unknown-ref disguise). The facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore, and that boundary is the archival-vs-remove divide.
103	
104	  Removal from archived stays available as the data hygiene path, and there is deliberately no restore entry point this round (mirroring archived dsh sessions). Ledgers written before Project archival omit `project.state`; the record schema normalizes it to `active` at load.
105	
106	## Member capabilities and skills
107	- Member capabilities (`capabilities` on the Member entity: reserved `tools.allow`, `skills.allow`) are durable intent carried verbatim by every lifecycle operation. Committing performs no known-name validation so old ledgers stay replayable across Harness upgrades; divergence is derived at activation as non-persisted `capabilityWarnings`. `tools.allow` is a deliberate interface reservation: it has no UI write path today.
108	
109	  Edits follow the partial-update semantics of `model`: an omitted field keeps the stored value and an explicit `null` clears it, so a caller that does not manage capabilities can leave the field out and any Remote-written override survives.
110	- Activation restricts every Member before preset validation (mount → restrict → validate), even without `tools.allow`. The allow-list can only narrow the preset baseline, retaining the seven Team tools and `working_directory`; names outside that baseline drop with a warning. Tool filtering, execution checks, and their limits are defined in [Tools and preset](tools-and-preset.md).
111	
112	  Editing the allow-list on a live Member swaps the restriction at a turn boundary in the same Session: idle Members apply immediately, and a running Member's edit waits for that Member's turn to end. Each Member owns one lifecycle chain, so the wait holds only that Member's later operations, still in submission order, while managing another Member never queues behind it and the ledger keeps its single ordered writer.
113	
114	  Host shutdown releases every pending wait instead of waiting out a turn that may never end, and a Session disposed outside the chain also releases it. A stop cancels that Member's in-flight turn and then waits for the Agent to quiesce, so a stop queued behind a parked edit reaches the boundary after that edit has applied and then usually finds the Agent idle. A stop never clears or aborts a committed configuration: the edit either applies at the boundary or reports `deferred:no-live-handle`, and either order leaves the stored intent in force at the next activation.
115	
116	  Waits are logged by class with their Member, Session, and duration: `stage 'wait-turn'` for waiting on the Member's own turn, and `stage 'wait-external'` for external execution such as the Agent releasing its Session write path. Restriction failures during activation surface as that Member's activation failure.
117	- A failed live apply never widens the surface: the edit keeps its ledger commit, the previous restriction stays in force (restored when the new one fails to install), the Remote call surfaces the failure, and retrying the same request re-applies the stored configuration without a second commit. The Host compares stored intent against the capability effects the runtime has actually applied, never against the requesting call's own history.
118	- Configuration edits report their effect separately from their commit: `updateMember` returns `effect` as `applied`, `already-applied`, `deferred:no-live-handle`, or `deferred:generation-changed` (saved now, applied at the next activation). A failure never appears as a value — it stays a rejection and is also kept as a routable `capability-apply` diagnostic whose `detail` carries requestId, operationId, stage, and reason with the Session in `sessionId`, logged under the same correlation group.
119	- Every roster row carries `capabilityState` (`applied` | `pending`), derived from the effects the runtime actually applied; states with no live surface report `pending` literally. The field is orthogonal to `availability`/`presence`: those answer whether the Member runs, this answers whether its stored configuration is in effect.
120	- Skills are Member-private. The preset carries no shared skill-filesystem row; instead the Host registers one filesystem provider per Member on that agent's exact scope layer (the traceable-service seam, same shape as the tool restriction). That provider scans exactly two Team-owned roots with default roots excluded: the plugin's bundled read-only core skills (`packages/agent-team/core-skills/`, first — a same-name bundled skill stays stable across upgrades) and the Member's writable `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/<memberId>/skills/`.
121	
122	  A Member catalog therefore starts with the bundled set (the `member-skill-manager` meta skill, which owns all skill craft guidance — the persona itself only states the private-space physical facts). Installing is writing into the Member's own directory (directory form `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional references/scripts, or a flat `.md`), there is deliberately no upload Remote, and the filesystem watcher feeds discovery.
123	
124	  `skills.allow` filters `list()` output through a live selection swap on the mounted provider (edits swap the filter and invalidate the catalog at the same turn boundary as tool edits); filtering is a visibility semantic, not a security boundary — both roots stay scanned and watched. Member removal deletes the private directory with its skills; suspend/resume and Host restart restore the identical catalog.

126	## Host service surface (`ctx.agentTeam`)
127	
128	The Host row publishes one service, `ctx.agentTeam`, consumed in two distinct ways with different stability promises. There is no CLI, no `bin`, and no loopback HTTP entry: the Web Client is the only Human control surface, and every change reaches the Host through the typed Remote.
129	
130	- **Remote methods** (the `@Remote`-decorated ones, e.g. `members`, `view`, `addMember`, `updateMember`, `sendMessage`, `readThread`, `inbox`, `humanProfile`) are the Client contract. They are typed through Typert artefacts generated from the declarations, so the Client, the model-facing tools, and any other consumer compile against the same shape; changing one is a contract change.
131	- **Host-only service methods** (e.g. `memberForAgent`, `membersForClient`, `status`, and the activation/lifecycle internals) exist for in-process Host callers — the preset row, commit listeners, and startup derivation. They carry no compatibility promise and may move between releases.
132	
133	Only the Remote set is a contract. Everything else on `ctx.agentTeam` is internal and may change shape without a migration note.
134	
135	A preset row must resolve `ctx.agentTeam` while it runs, never capture it statically at declaration time: the service is provided when the Host plugin starts, so a row that closed over it at import time sees nothing. The same applies to `ctx.get('agentTeam')` in external code, which is undocumented use of an internal surface rather than a supported integration point.
136	
137	## Composer attachments (cache, not archive)
138	
139	Attachments live in the bounded cache `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/attachments/v1/<attachmentId>/`, with a sanitized original name and `meta.json`; they are never ledger bytes or an archive. `putAttachment` enforces a 10 MB file cap and sanitizes names; `getAttachment` serves Client display. Messages record metadata while the stored body contains machine-facing `[attachment] <absolute path>` lines. The Client strips those lines and renders thumbnails/chips.
140	
141	The request's `requestId` is an upload's idempotency key. Retrying the same payload replays the original result instead of writing a second entry, reusing that key for a different payload is refused as a request collision, and the cache id derives from the request id alone. A retry therefore converges on the same entry after a Host restart without a second durable store or an in-memory map.
142	
143	The Project and Thread composers accept files both through the "+" picker and by pasting into the draft; a paste that carries files is intercepted and joins the same pending-file chips, while plain-text pastes keep their native insertion.
144	
145	Garbage collection runs at startup and every 24 hours: referenced uploads older than 72 hours and orphaned uploads older than 24 hours are removed, while metadata remains. Agent-sent absolute paths are validated as absolute non-empty regular files under 10 MB and rejected atomically if any path fails; each surviving path is copied into an immutable cache entry whose id derives from the message or reply request and the path's position in it. A manually pasted absolute path is simply read by the Agent; Host touches nothing it does not own.
146	
147	That request-derived identity is what makes retries cheap: a repeated send or reply converges on the entry the first attempt prepared instead of writing an orphan, so the stored body — one `[attachment]` line per file — stays identical across retries. A message or reply that fails after preparation removes the entries this attempt prepared which no committed Message references, with the ledger's reference set as the guard; genuinely unreferenced uploads stay GC's to reclaim.
148	
149	On a reused request id the ledger compares the recorded resolved attachment ids with the retry's resolved ids, so a retry carrying a different attachment set is refused as a collision.
150	
151	## Human profile and version footnote
152	
153	The Human's display name and avatar reference live in the Team Host row's own Config, in the settings namespace `wowyuarm-agent-team-host` (user layer); avatar bytes live in the persistent `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/human/v1/` store, never in the TTL-bound attachment cache.
154	
155	The retired `agent-team-human` section is no longer an authority: the rc.1 settings importer carries sections across through a closed built-in mapping, so a third-party section stays behind in the renamed legacy document. A boot that finds the row still pristine — the default name and no avatar — adopts those facts through the same write path the settings page uses, and anything already re-entered wins.
156	
157	Four typed Remotes serve the settings page: `humanProfile` (name, avatar reference, and version footnote facts) and `putHumanAvatar`/`getHumanAvatar`/`removeHumanAvatar` (images only, 10 MB cap shared with attachments; a removed entry throws and the Client falls back to the initial).
158	
159	The footnote carries the version of the bundle this Host runs from — read from the installed package's own manifest, so it states what the profile actually installed rather than a string every release must remember to bump — plus the repository link and an update tip. The tip names the newer version once a background check has observed a newer published release.
160	
161	The check asks the public npm `latest` document at most every 12 hours, refreshes in the background so profile reads never wait on the network, settles every failure as "no update known", and stays off while `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_UPDATE_CHECK=0`.
162	
163	The ledger reads the same profile for `team_view` and @ matching, so a rename reaches every surface at once. `human` stays a permanent alias for the Human and no agent handle may claim the literal, so `@human` keeps delivering across renames while chips render the current display name.

11	- 重放会重算每条记录应有的 Inbox delta 并逐项比较，所以改变既有 kind 校验规则的版本要先写一条 `team/rules-version-adopted`（Host actor，`{ version }`）。每条记录按它之前最新的标记校验；没有标记的 ledger 为版本 1。标记由 `initialize` 在它自己排队的提交里追加，因此早于之后的所有写入，包括启动恢复。标记只升不降，每个版本至多一条；ledger 采用的版本高于本构建实现的版本时拒绝打开。
12	- 当前构建实现版本 2：挂载时若 ledger 的最新标记低于它，就追加版本 2 标记；全新 ledger 在 `team/initialized` 之后立即写入该标记。
13	- 规则版本 2 起，Host 还会提交 `team/main-message-posted`、`team/main-stream-read` 和 `team/thread-started`，它们在版本 1 的记录段内会被拒绝，而 `team/message-sent` 在版本 2 的记录段内被拒绝。Host 不再写 `team/message-sent`（开 Thread 用 `startThread`），它只在版本 1 的记录段内重放。
14	- inbox delta 可带可选的 `mainMarkers` 列表，使用独立的 marker 形状（`projectRef` 加 `messageRef` 或 `activityRef`）。它只在确有变化时出现，所以版本 1 的记录保持存储字节不变；离开的 Member 的 Main stream marker 随同一 operation 与其他 inbox 状态一起清除。
15	- Agent 通过与 Thread marker 相同的 direct 通知路径被 Main stream marker 唤醒；Attention 覆盖的普通 Main stream 更新同样立即投递。每条未读事实都会打断，因此 Thread 的普通更新只因读者 follow 了该 Thread 才到达：没有任何身份——owner 或 accountable——被放进更慢的等级，也没有任何东西在通知发出前先累积计数。`covered` 是保存在进程内的签名，用于阻止同一批 durable facts 的重复派生花掉第二次尝试；已入队但尚未读取的通知会被替换，而不是叠加。
16	- 回复把被回答的 Message 记为自身 Message 上的 `replyToMessageRef`，Host 在提交前用 ledger 解析这个 ref：未知的 ref、或属于别的 Thread 的 ref 一律拒绝，不会被存下。父消息作者在提交时加入收件人，与 mention 走同一套解析、拿同一个 direct marker 被送达——全程没有任何邀请环节。规则版本 2 下 `undeliveredMentions` 永远不会被填上：每个可寻址的收件人都会送达，不论该 Thread 是否曾经承载过它，也不因此开始任何 Attention。报告未送达的残余只属于版本 1 兼容路径。被引用的画面 —— 父消息作者与其正文一行 —— 是读取期派生（`replyTo`），绝不是第二份存储副本。因此它不可能与父消息不一致，父消息不在本次读取这一页里时也照样填得上。ref 不再可解析时只留裸 ref。引用不是可选项：这个参数属于回复契约的一部分，携带 ref 的回复只按 ref 本身被接受或拒绝。
17	- Projections、Inbox results、tools、commands、Remote responses 和 UI 都从已提交的 operations 派生。
18	- Client code 不得解释 ledger records，也不得创建 parallel authority。

20	## Lifecycle 与通知
21	- Agent lifecycle、JSON/SQLite replay、authorization、idempotency 和 revision checks 都留在 Host 侧。durable unread 变化可以通过 public Agent safe-boundary API 产生一条有界、经过合并的 Agent context notification。direct mentions 携带 Message 和 source。Task/Claim Activities 携带简要状态变化。ordinary unread 只携带不含正文的 Thread-first route，存在 Task 时再带 Task overlay。Promotion 与其他 Task transition 一样是 Task activity，通过 Activity markers 到达 followers。这类 notification 不是第二权威，也不保证模型恰好处理一次。
22	- 已提交的 Session transition（`team/member-session-renewed`、`team/member-session-rolled-over`、`team/member-session-recycled`）记录的是 desired binding，而不是已完成的切换。retire 旧代与 activate 目标都是 ledger 写入之外的 Host 效果。startup 与 Member 的显式 recovery 动作都会补完被中断的 transition，依据记录的 previous Session。每个效果各自推导自己是否已完成。live handle 不能证明 archive 那一半跑过。重复请求只返回已记录的 receipt 与诚实状态，不再提交一次绑定。
23	- 每个 durable Member state 只有一组期望的外部 effect，即 [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.zh.md#member-lifecycle) 表。每一次 lifecycle operation 在 commit 之后重跑这组 effect。startup 对每个非 enabled Member 也重跑同一组。archive、suspension、remove 因此走同一条推导重跑收敛，不做第二次 durable 写入。即使 Workspace/Session/filesystem 调用被 crash 或失败打断，也一样收敛。
24	- startup 绝不把非 enabled Member 激活为 enabled。启动阶段失败的 effect 只记日志，下一次 boot 重试，不让 boot 失败。同一 Member 的 lifecycle operation 按提交序串行；不同 Member 从不排在彼此的等待之后。
25	- Task 提醒由 Host 在 Team 事件后评估并写入 `team/reminder-raised`，不使用 timer。其可选 `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta 仅属于一个接收者；marker 被读取消费后，replay 仍保留完整 episode 用于去重。
26	- reminder operation 会使对应 Task Thread 的 change scope 失效，让 Human Inbox 刷新，但不增加公开 fact 或 revision。accept、close 与生命周期清理会移除已经失效的未读 marker，同时保留 episode 历史。Agent idle 是进程内观测，跨 generation 替换保留，Host 重启后丢弃；idle 未知时不满足时间条件。
27	
28	- ledger append 之后剩下的是 delivery 效果：commit listeners、Client change invalidation、participation notice。每个受影响的 Member 还会收到一次 wake。每一项都经过同一条边界：失败只记日志，不让操作本身失败。失败的 listener 或 wake 仍以 committed result 作答，而不是虚假的回滚。只有 invariant divergence 继续 reject。失败的 Inbox wake 清掉这个 wake 记录的 notice state。因此，下一次触及该 Member 的 commit 重新推导同一批 durable Inbox facts 并重试，不追加第二次操作。DM 保留显式的 recorded-but-not-delivered 错误。
29	
30	## 哪些操作会唤醒 Member，以及成员卡住时怎么选
31	
32	唤醒是 Host 经四种 cause 之一投递的一条**有界合并通知**，每条都带上产生它的持久事实：
33	
34	| Cause | 产生它的事实 |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `commit` | 任何触及该 Member 的已提交操作：提及、DM、Task 活动、promotion、被接受的回答 |
37	| `transition` | 一条已记录的 `team/member-session-renewed`、`team/member-session-recycled` 或旧式 `team/member-session-rolled-over`，其 retire 与 activation 效果没有按序完成；重新派生的 Inbox 排在携带输入之后 |
38	| `activation` | 一次新的 activation，有 carried input 时带上旧 Session id |
39	| `running` | Member 自身 `agent/status` 转为 `running`——每次转换一次，不是每步一次 |
40	
41	唤醒不是第二权威，也不承诺恰好一次被模型处理。一次投递失败会清掉它记录的 notice 状态，于是下一条触及该 Member 的提交会重新派生同样持久事实并重试，不会追加第二次通知。
42	
43	`recoverMember` 是人工入口，按顺序且只选一个：
44	
45	| 条件 | 动作 | 适用场景 |
46	| --- | --- | --- |
47	| handle 缺失，或活动 handle 的 Session id 不是记录中的绑定，且存在已记录的 transition | 完成这条已记录的 transition | 崩溃或某个效果失败，使一次 Session transition 只执行了一半 |
48	| 持久状态不是 `enabled`，但仍有活动 handle | 完成该状态的效果 | suspend/archive/removal 已提交，但它的 disposal 失败 |
49	| 活动 handle 的 preset 组合已丢失 | 原地 reactivate | 一次 reload 丢了 preset 组合，Member 的工具不可用 |
50	| 完全没有活动 handle | reactivate | activation 本身就失败了 |
51	| 其余情况 | steer 一条 resume 提示 | Member 活着、组合完成、绑定正常——其余状态都已被上面几行接走 |
52	
53	带活动 handle 的 error 态 Member 落在最后一行：`recoverMember` 会 steer 它，而如果原因仍在，下一轮会再失败一次。选之前先分清两件事：模型路由坏了或网关拒收，要改的是路由而不是恢复 Member，在路由通之前 steer 什么也救不回来。恢复从不会重置上下文世代：绑定已经迁移的滞留 Member 由这条路径补完那条已记录的 transition，而 Remote 面上没有任何东西会 renew 或 rollover 一个 Session。
54	
55	Member 当前的失败原因以 `diagnostic` 挂在 status 上并由 Client 渲染。它由活动 surface 派生、不落盘。Host 重启后只有在有东西唤醒该 Member 时才会重新派生，所以一个没有被唤醒的 Member 在下次被操作触及前不显示原因。
56	
57	## 变更流与 Projection
58	- `changes()` 是流式 Remote，可声明一个 scope（workspace/project/thread/presence）。省略 scope 时观察共享 Team 投影变化，不包含 presence。Host 先注册监听，再发送当前基线，之后只发送匹配的变更通知。消费者暂停期间，只保留最新待发送版本。取消或 Host 释放时关闭订阅。
59	- Thread read 与 `team/dm-sent` 不改变共享投影：既不推进版本，也不唤醒订阅者。私有 reminder 会使其 Task Thread scope 失效，从而让已打开的 Human Inbox 得知提醒；它不会因此成为公开 Thread 历史。Presence 使用进程内 epoch，其他 scope 使用最近一次共享投影提交的 ledger sequence。版本只在同一 scope 和 Host 生命周期内有意义。Host 只为受 operation 影响的 Members 重算 Inbox hints。
60	- `TeamChangeStream` 在每个页面内通过 `ctx.remote.$stream()` 按 scope 共享一个逻辑流。Harness 管理共享的 `/api/remote.mux` WebSocket 和连接恢复。每次开场基线都会触发重新读取 Host，包括重连后的相同或更低版本。开场基线既补上首次读取与订阅之间的变化，也在没有新提交时恢复失败的读取。最后一个 listener 离开时释放这个 scope，插件释放时关闭所有 scope。传输失败在恢复前只报告一次。终止性错误直接报告，不走 Team 自有重试循环。没有长轮询回退、跨页面主从选举或单活跃页面限制。并发的补充读取合并通知。读取期间再收到通知，保留后续一轮读取，不用旧版本过滤重连基线。Human Inbox 徽标订阅无 scope 通知。订阅经 debounce 重拉 Inbox 合计，在本页 Thread read 后刷新。Presence 订阅更新 Member 可用状态，不唤醒 Inbox。通知只是重新读取的提示，不是第二份事实存储。
61	- `contextContinuity` unit 经 Harness projection registry 增量折叠活动 Session 事件，只保留恢复所需的旧 intent、checkpoint、continuation 与未答复输入。激活与退休 Session 恢复也可全量折叠被检视日志。
62	- Member clock baseline 经 `session-event-cursor.ts` 只消费追加事件。Session 身份、继承前缀、日志长度或锚点事件变化时从头重折。守卫依赖日志只追加的契约；同一 sequence、同一事件类型的就地替换不在检测范围内。
63	- 读取投影按用途定界。`view` 只回答它自己那一页 fact 加上请求点名的 Thread：catalog 字段带的是这一页的 Task、Thread、显示序号与 Claim。只有 `includeCatalog` 才返回整个请求 scope 的 Task/Thread/Claim catalog，也就是模型侧 `team_view` 渲染的 address book 投影。
64	- 一页读取沿 fact ledger 走到超出 limit 的第一个匹配为止。catalog 读取再多一次对 scope 内 Thread 的目录过滤，以及每个 Task 行一次活 Claim 查询。这些分量必须分开报告，不合并成一个总数：只报返回行数看不出这次读取走过了什么。
65	- Claim 按 Task 分桶，由重放派生的索引支撑，所以按 Task 的读取（Claim 列表、Thread 画面、Inbox 行、Task board）绝不走账本的全部 Claim。这里每个索引都由重放重建，绝不是第二份 durable 权威。
66	
67	## Session 持久化与重放
68	- Bundle 目标为 DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`。Bundle 的 Session persistence 使用当前 DSH schema。随附的 JSONL backend 会自行迁移已发布的旧格式（v0/v1/v2 → V3 → V4），旧格式 Session 数据无需手动处置。这个 DSH Session-schema 策略不会抹掉 Team operation history。Team 有意保留针对旧版、Message-level `occurredAt` 之前 records 的窄 replay normalization。
69	- 普通存储的 Message operations 在加载时使用包裹 operation 的 instant。旧 `team/thread-read` snapshot anchors 与 Message facts 从来源 Message operation 解析 instant。只在必要时回退到 read operation。而 snapshot 正是唯一仍会走到这条 normalization 的记录形态。snapshot 把 Message anchors 与 Thread facts 连同消费掉的 Inbox delta 一起冻结在记录里。
70	
71	  当前每次读写入的 receipt 只存进度与 Inbox delta，是唯一不存任何 instant 的 Thread-read 形态。旧记录就地 normalize 并校验，绝不改写。不要增加 Team 自有的 Session migration、宽泛 compatibility reads 或 fallback storage paths。可选的 `member.model` inheritance 与可选 Message attachments 都是当前语义，不是 legacy fields。
72	
73	## Attention 与 Inbox 权威
74	- Thread Attention 是 private Member x Thread state。ordinary unread 来自当前 Attention。structured mentions 创建 direct markers。terminal Task changes 在 Attention 结束后仍可能保留稀疏 Activity markers。Host 是唯一 Inbox authority。Session history 可以保留有界 notification context，包括 direct Message bodies 和 Task/Claim transition summaries。但 Session history 不能形成 parallel unread projection。
75	- Inbox 读取先对读者的整条未读队列排序，只为自己返回的行准备 preview 文本、instant 的署名者与活 Claim owner。总计仍针对整条队列，所以只取一行的角标也报告全部未读 Thread。`threadObservations` 返回最新的 `limit` 条 observation 并带 `hasMore`，follower 集合始终是完整当前状态。
76	
77	## Session 策略与上下文压力
78	- Team 管理的 Agent sessions 使用显式 Team preset 和可信的 `danger-full-access` policy。这是面向可信 Workspace 的有意产品边界。
79	- Host 激活 Member 时，通过 session-title service 用这个 Member 的 handle 命名没有标题的 Member session。这样普通 Session list 就会显示 Member identity。显式 rename 或任何已有 title 始终优先。命名失败不会导致 activation 失败。
80	- Member 上下文的两个机制都在 Host 侧，模型没有对应工具（见 Tools and preset）：Team 通过 preset 中的适配层控制请求预算，Harness 的 `BasicCompactionEngine` 把过大的 Session 就地缩短；换代协调器在唤醒边界换掉冷下来的一代，并以 Host actor 记录 `team/member-session-recycled`。压力与唤醒阈值归 [`memory-and-context.zh.md`](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.zh.md)。
81	- 换代窗口内的这一代报告 unavailable，并带 `rollover` diagnostic，直到新代激活。所以跟随该行的 Client 绝不会打开一个尚不存在的 Session。
82	- 换代携带的是输入，不是上下文：commit 记下退役日志的偏移，新代只重放该边界及其之后的输入，并按 Message id 去重；即使输入已被 claim，也使用最初的 durable inbox 插入记录。不经过进程内存拷贝（见 [Tools and preset](tools-and-preset.zh.md)）。
83	- Pending/error bookkeeping 只在进程内维护。只有进入 transaction 的 compactions 才会写入 durable Session history，绝不写入 Team ledger。
84	- 终止回合的恢复先读 Harness 的结构化失败，再看措辞。稳定的 code 单独决定结果。`RATE_LIMIT` 是 rate limiting，`TRANSPORT`/`TIMEOUT` 是 transient network，显式 429/503 响应是 rate limiting。其他任何 code（quota、auth、context、请求状态）无论 message 写什么都保持 manual。只有无 code 可用的错误才回落到窄 message 签名。
85	- `agent/error` 负责终止回合恢复及其连续错误上限。无论走哪条路，失败都保留已记录的 Member diagnostic。
86	- 在任何 `turn/start` 之前被丢弃的 Team 唤醒，是唯一一类背后没有 `agent/error` 的 error diagnostic。当一条 Team 自己的 Inbox 或 recovery 通知在 Agent 开启回合前离开队列、且不是 Host 自己做的替换或 dispose 时，Host 记一条 `runtime` 类 diagnostic，带上 `source: 'agent/inbox/discarded'`、该 Member 的 `sessionId` 和 `occurredAt`。Host 有意替换或拆除的通知不触发任何东西，所以普通的通知替换从不显示 error。被取消的 splice 不带 durable 原因，因此它和所有 runtime diagnostic 一样只在进程内维护。重启后，在下一次唤醒真正运行或再次取消之前什么都不显示。
87	
88	## 私有记忆、归档与身份效应
89	- `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/` 下的 private-memory directories 是 Member identity 的 Host-owned effects，不是第二权威。Member activation 确保 private-memory directory、`notes/` 和缺失的 `memory.md` 存在。startup 不会清理 ledger 不知道的 `member:` directories。显式 Member removal 会归档这个 Member 的 Session，并移除这个 Member 的 private-memory directory。Team removal path 之外的 entries 保持不动。
90	- 这项删除，以及 activation 时对旧式 colon 目录的改名，都限定在当前进程自己的 members root 之内。记录里的 `privateMemoryPath` 是一条 durable 绝对事实，指向「当初添加这个 Member 的那个 DSH home」里的目录。因此解析到另一个 home 的进程会拒绝搬移或删除这个目录（并告警），而不是把 Member 的真实私有记忆搬出 Member 自己的 home。
91	- Member 与 Project 的归档是介于 suspend 与 remove 之间的可逆第三态。`archiveMember` 提交 `team/member-archived`。dispose live session，私有 memory 与 Session log 留在磁盘，并把 Session 从分组 surface 归档。`archiveMember` 再以公开 `claims_released` Activity 加上 Attention/marker 清理，释放这个 Member 的 active Claims。被隐藏的 Member 不得让 Task 卡在 in progress，也不得留下幻影 unread 计数。`archiveProject` 提交 `team/project-archived`，对 Project 上所有 Thread 的 owner 施加同样的释放形态。两种归档形态下 Membership 都保留（隐藏态，非退出）。
92	
93	  Archived 实体从所有 Team API surface 消失：
94	  - projection：view projects/threads/tasks/members、mention 候选、Project join、编辑。
95	  - ref 解析：`resolveTaskRefs`/`resolveThreadRefs` 跳过 Archived 实体，message 正文渲染为纯文本。
96	  - ref-addressed read：`readThread`、`threadHistory`、`threadObservations`、`listClaims` 以明确的 archived 错误拒绝，绝不伪装成 unknown-ref。
97	
98	  事实则完整保留在 ledger 中，供重放与未来恢复。这条边界就是 archival 与 remove 的分界。从 archived 状态 Remove 仍可作为数据清理路径。本轮刻意不提供 restore 入口，与 dsh 的 archived session 对齐。Project 归档之前写入的 ledger 省略 `project.state`。记录 schema 在 load 时把 `project.state` 归一化为 `active`。
99	
100	## Member capabilities 与 skills
101	- Member capabilities 是随全部 lifecycle operation 原样流转的 durable intent。Member capabilities 指 Member 实体上的 `capabilities` 字段，即预留的 `tools.allow` 与 `skills.allow`。commit 时不做已知名白名单校验，保证 Harness 升级后旧 ledger 仍可重放。与已知名的偏差在 activation 时派生为不持久化的 `capabilityWarnings`。`tools.allow` 是有意的接口预留：当前没有 UI 写入路径。编辑语义与 `model` 一致，都是局部更新：字段缺省即保持已存储的值，显式传 `null` 才清除。因此不管理 capabilities 的调用方可以直接省略该字段，其他来源写入的覆盖不会被带掉。

127	## Composer attachments（cache，不是 archive）
128	
129	Composer attachments 是有界 cache，不是 archive，也不是 ledger bytes。cache 目录是 `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/attachments/v1/<attachmentId>/`，存经过清理的原始名称和 `meta.json` sidecar。

131	- `putAttachment` 写入 immutable payload：每个文件上限 10 MB，名称中的 path separators 和 control characters 会被剥离。`getAttachment` 为 Client display 读取它们。两者和其他 Host capabilities 一样都是 typed Remote actions。
132	- `requestId` 是一次 upload 的幂等键。同一 payload 的重试 replay 原结果，而不是写第二份条目。复用该 key 携带不同 payload 的调用被拒为 request collision。cache id 单独由 request id 派生，因此 Host 重启后重试仍收敛到同一条目，不需要第二个 durable store 或进程内 map。

138	- 不需要为手动 path references 增加机制。粘贴到 Message body 的 absolute path 会被 Member agent 像其他文件一样读取，Host 不会触碰不属于自己的内容。

4	
5	The Host capability for one Agent Team in a dshHome. `ctx.agentTeam` owns the append-only operation ledger, reconstructs the current collaboration projection, and is the lifecycle owner for member Agents managed by the same capability. Thread Attention and the Member Inbox are durable Host projections. When unread state changes, this package sends one bounded, coalesced context notification through the Agent's public safe-boundary API; it never interrupts an active request or acts as a Session delivery worker. The [Agent Team architecture note](../../.scratch/archive/2026-08/m1/design/agent-notes/2026-08-15-agent-team-operation-ledger.md) owns the persistence and package-topology decisions.
6	
7	## Service contract
8	
9	The Service owns its SQLite-backed DomainFacility and consumes `ctx.workspaceRegistry`, `ctx.agents`, `ctx.agentDefaultModel`, `ctx.agentPresets`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.tokenMeter`, `ctx.sessionProjections`, and `ctx.sessionPersistence`. It opens the versioned `agent_team` Domain before Cordis publishes `ctx.agentTeam`. The first boot appends one `team/initialized` operation for the stable Human Member; later boots replay the same operation and do not append another record.
10	
11	`status()` returns the current durable sequence, operation count, project count, Agent Member count, and Human Member ref. It performs no model request and no storage write. `validateLedger()` checks the package-owned projection against the durable operation table. The invariant companion re-derives that whole table at mount — an unreplayable ledger fails startup — but adopts the record-level replay the ledger constructor already ran while nothing has committed since, gated on the record count, head sequence, and head operation id, which only the operations table's single writer can change. Any commit in between, and every later validation, replays the durable records again. Afterwards the invariant re-derives once per burst of commits, after the committing call has returned, so a Thread read never waits on an O(ledger) replay; a divergence is logged where it is detected and re-raised on every later commit until a replay comes back clean.
12	
13	Every operation record carries a positive global sequence, unique operation and request ids, an actor snapshot, and the previous operation id. Replay rejects invalid record fields, table-key/id mismatches, sequence gaps, broken previous links, repeated ids, and invalid state transitions. An identical request-id retry returns the original receipt; a changed payload with the same request id rejects.
14	
15	One durable record stores progress instead of the projection it reported. A `team/thread-read` receipt carries the Workspace, Member, Thread ref, optional Task ref, read watermark, and Inbox delta; the Thread, its facts, the anchor, the reader's Attention, and the unread count left behind are re-derived from the projection on every replay. Records written before this form froze that whole picture beside the delta: one strict union accepts both shapes, the legacy record keeps its own full derivation as its expected value, and loading normalizes and validates it without rewriting a stored byte. A record that fits neither shape — a receipt carrying a picture field, a legacy record missing the Task it belongs to or one of its facts — fails the domain open rather than being guessed at. An identical retry of a committed read returns the original receipt with the picture the current projection derives.
16	
17	## Durability and lifecycle
18	
19	`storage-domain` validates every record at the durable read boundary and rejects a backend unit stamped with another version. The Team updates its projection only after `KvTable.put()` resolves. Its Fiber owns the Domain handle; disposal rejects new Service calls through Cordis removal, drains accepted Domain writes, and closes the backend unit before the name can reopen.
20	
21	Member creation commits one stable Member/session/Workspace/preset/private-memory identity before unpublished Agent setup. The creation Workspace is recorded as the Member's creation site; further Workspaces are joined and left through the participation operations (`team/member-workspace-joined`/`team/member-workspace-left`), which grant collaboration immediately without moving the Session. Setup mounts the selected preset and validates its marked `team_message` plus all seven Team tools before publication. Failure leaves only that Member unavailable. Suspend waits for the owned `AgentHandle` to stop; resume and Host remount restore the exact persisted session.
22	
23	Archival is the reversible third state between suspend and remove, for Members and Projects alike. `archiveMember` commits `team/member-archived`, disposes the live session while keeping private memory and the Session log on disk, archives the Session from grouping surfaces, and releases the Member's active Claims with public `claims_released` Activities plus Attention/marker cleanup. `archiveProject` commits `team/project-archived` with the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads. Memberships survive both forms — hidden state, not departure. Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface: projections, ref resolution (their Task refs stop resolving, so message bodies render plain text), and ref-addressed reads (`readThread`/`threadHistory`/`threadObservations`/`listClaims` reject with an explicit archived error) — while the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore; that boundary is the archival-vs-remove divide. Removal from archived stays available as the data hygiene path; there is no restore entry point yet (mirroring archived dsh sessions).
24	
25	Members optionally carry durable capability intent (`capabilities.tools.allow`, `capabilities.skills.allow`). It flows verbatim through every lifecycle operation, replays unchanged after Host restart, and commits without known-name validation so Harness upgrades can never break old ledgers; divergence from known names surfaces at activation as derived, non-persisted `capabilityWarnings`. `tools.allow` is a deliberate interface reservation: it has no UI write path today. Edits are partial like `model`: an omitted field keeps the stored value and an explicit `null` clears it, so a caller that does not manage capabilities can simply leave the field out.
26	
27	Every Member is restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`, even without `tools.allow`. An allow-list only narrows that baseline, retaining the seven Team tools and `working_directory`; out-of-baseline names produce warnings. Late plugin tools are filtered from requests and denied execution; same-name replacements reject request assembly. Other plugins' prompts remain visible and do not block conversation. See [Tools and preset](../../docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md) for the checks and their limits. Live edits swap restrictions at a turn boundary in the same Session; later lifecycle operations wait behind the edit. Activation failures leave only that Member unavailable.
28	
29	Skills are Member-private: the preset has no shared skill-filesystem row, and the Host registers one provider per Member that scans exactly the plugin's bundled read-only core skills (`packages/agent-team/core-skills/` — the `member-skill-manager` meta skill that owns all skill craft guidance) plus that Member's writable `skills/` directory under its private memory path (default roots excluded). Installing is writing into the Member's own directory — directory form `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional references and scripts, or a flat `.md` — and there is deliberately no upload Remote. The persona itself only states the private-space physical facts; the meta skill's description routes skill-management work to it. `skills.allow` filters the catalog through a live selection swap on the mounted provider at the same turn boundary; the filesystem watcher feeds discovery after a self-install.
30	
31	Every team-managed session records `danger-full-access`. Session cwd remains the Workspace path, while private memory lives under `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/<memberId>/`. An untitled Member session is named with its handle through the session-title service, so the ordinary Session list shows the Member identity; an explicit rename or any earlier title always wins. The isolated `team-member` preset also provides coding tools including model-facing web search, Workspace instruction discovery, and Team protocol guidance. The host owns the shared Web service and provider; the preset mounts only the model-facing web tool. Its lowercase `memory.md` is a bounded 16 KiB reference index, injected only for that Member when its content changes, with its current usage (`X.X KiB / 16 KiB`) stated in the block; `notes/` stays on-demand through filesystem tools. Over-budget indexes receive a maintenance warning, not silent truncation. Ordinary sessions and forks receive no Team identity or private-memory context. At Host startup every enabled Member's private memory is provisioned and an `inactive` Member's is removed with its Session archived; directories the replayed ledger does not reference are never pruned, so leftovers from a discarded ledger stay on disk for the operator. Both that removal and the activation-time migration of a pre-fix colon directory act only on paths inside the running process's own `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/`: a recorded path naming a different DSH home (an isolated test home, a second instance) is refused with a warning rather than renamed or deleted, because acting on it would take a Member's real private memory out of its home.
32	
33	Adding a Member to a Project grants future read/send/claim authority but injects no historical Messages into the member session. A Thread is created by `startThread`, never by a Main stream message: a started Thread is a discussion, or a Task when `kind: 'task'` asks for one, and a Human can later promote a taskless Thread by atomically adding its Task overlay and a structured `promote` Task activity. Thread Attention starts when a Thread is created, a Claim is created, or a member follows — never from a mention or a reply, which deliver one direct marker and leave Attention alone. Ordinary unread is derived from Attention; structured mentions create durable direct markers, while terminal Task changes retain sparse Activity markers for affected followers after Attention ends. `team_inbox` and Thread reads are Host projections, not Session inbox contents. A direct mention context includes its Message body and source; Task/Claim changes — including promotion — include concise transition facts; ordinary unread carries a body-free Thread-first route. Pending hints are coalesced, ignored hints do not loop, and resume/error recovery derives a new hint from durable unread state. For recoverable service failures, the Host wakes a Member after each of the first two consecutive `agent/error` occurrences, then leaves the third failure for the operator; only a clean turn resets that run.
34	
35	Member replies require the exact current Thread revision and atomically update Message and Thread facts. `threadRef` is the primary collaboration identity; released task-only Clients may send a Host-resolved `taskRef` alias for taskful Threads, while Task/Claim operations remain Task-ref based. Unread work must be read before a mutation, unless every unread Message is already on the writer's model-visible surface in full — a direct mention or DM notice that carried the body counts as the reading, records nothing, and leaves the durable read state untouched; stale revisions are rejected after that unread gate. A closed Task rejects replies and new Attention; reopening restores the Task without restoring prior Attention. Taskless Threads still support replies, follow, mentions, Inbox, read, and history, but have no Claims or Task-resolution path. Under rules version 2 a mention delivers one direct marker and never starts Attention, and a reply carries the parent's author into the recipient set the same way. Every addressable recipient is delivered — a Member the Thread has never carried included — and nothing follows as a side effect; there is no invitation step and no undelivered remainder to report. Mentions are authored in the Message body as `@Handle` and resolved by the Host against the Project's addressable names; the body is the sole delivery authority, and no recipient list travels with the request. Message facts carry the resolved refs, and the Client renders mention chips only for those Members. Claim/done/release and Task changes are ordered host-authored Activities. Active Claims exclude only the same normalized Direction; different Directions can run concurrently. Task state is derived from Claims unless Human acceptance or closure overrides it. Close releases active Claims and clears Thread Attention atomically. Member removal marks the member inactive, releases owned active Claims, clears its Attention and direct markers, and archives the session after the durable commit. Message and Activity facts share one bounded sequence cursor.
36	
37	`changes({ scope? }, signal?)` returns an `AsyncIterable<{ version: number }>` through a streaming Remote. It emits the current baseline, then matching workspace/project/thread/presence invalidations; omitting scope observes shared projections but not presence. A paused consumer retains only the latest pending version; cancellation or Host disposal closes the stream. The Client must reread projections on every baseline, even when the version is unchanged or lower after a restart. See [architecture](../../docs/architecture/host-authority.md) for scope/version and recovery semantics. Thread reads change only private read state: they wake no scope, and a read with no unread or markers to consume appends no operation. After a commit, Inbox hints are recomputed only for affected Members.
38	
39	M1 supports one Host writer. The ledger is permanent and has no snapshot or compaction path.

41	## Composition
42	
43	The bundle consumes the Host's existing singleton providers; it does not mount replacements for `agents`, default model selection, `tools`, `fs`, `sandboxPolicy`, Session store/persistence, or Workspace registry. Its private SQLite DomainFacility does not replace the Host's global storage service, so toggling the bundle does not rebuild unrelated storage consumers. Load those Host services once, then mount this Service and its invariant companion. The Team Web Client is the only Human control surface.
44	
45	A team-enabled preset registers the seven tools in its own agent scope and marks the `team_message` definition with `markAgentTeamPreset()`. Preset rows must resolve `ctx.agentTeam` when executing, not statically inject it: the Host mounts member presets while it restores Members during its own activation, so a row that declares `agentTeam` as a dependency cannot activate and fails every startup restore. Duplicate scoped tool names fail during unpublished setup and make only that Member unavailable. Duplicate Host service providers remain a composition error and should be removed rather than layered.
46	
47	Member context has two mechanisms and no model tool. The preset's `member-compaction-engine` delegates summaries and durable reduction to the Harness, while Team bounds input and output before each request; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns those numbers. A generation swap is a Host decision at a wake boundary: `team-context-management.ts` waits for true idle, rechecks the owned-jobs guard, commits the idempotent `team/member-session-recycled` operation (Host actor), retires the old Session (dispose and archive, never delete), and activates a fresh one parented at the one it replaces. Identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention survive, and process state is reconstructible from the durable log after a crash. No Remote write renews, rolls over, or otherwise resets a Member's context.

50	
51	### Host collaboration state
52	
53	#### What the model sees
54	
55	An enabled Member may receive one bounded, coalesced context notification after durable unread work appears. Structured direct mentions include their Message body and source; Task/Claim Activities include concise state transitions; ordinary unread includes only a Thread-first route, counts, and revisions, with a Task overlay where present. The notification is queued at the Agent's safe step boundary, so active model requests and tools are not interrupted. It routes the common path directly to `team_thread.read`; the model uses `team_inbox` only when it needs to triage remaining Threads.

58	
59	The ledger, projection, and Human status reads add no model tokens.

61	#### KV Cache effect
62	
63	The Host ledger and Human status reads do not alter model requests or cache reuse.
64	
65	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
66	
67	- **Single Host writer** — concurrent processes over one dshHome are unsupported; operation serialization is process-local.
68	- **Permanent ledger** — M1 provides neither snapshots nor compaction, so storage grows with committed collaboration facts.
69	- **No remote provider seam** — the package combines the capability definition and its only implementation until a real remote Consumer requires another Provider.
70	- **No Session migration of its own** — Member Sessions ride the Host's Session persistence and its released-format migration chain; this package provides no Team ledger or Member Session migration, compatibility read, or fallback.
