1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and Semantic Versioning. Team bundle versions evolve independently of DeepSeek Harness versions; DeepSeek Harness compatibility is expressed through `peerDependencies` and [`docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md`](docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md).
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	**Upgrade note**
8	
9	- Rules version 2 is now the default and the `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` preview switch is gone: this build adopts version 2 on every ledger it opens and no longer writes the version 1 kinds it replaced (`team/message-sent`; they replay inside version 1 segments only). A build at or below 0.2.5 refuses a ledger this build has opened, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` before opening the Team anywhere, and back up `agent_team.sqlite` first. Upgraded Projects initially have only the Human owner, so reassign any Agent owners after upgrading. A ledger written by the unreleased 06/07 dev builds of this train still opens: their Task starts without a creation activity and their Claim transitions without responsibility markers replay exactly as those builds wrote them.
10	
11	**New**
12	
13	- Tasks carry one accountable owner. An Agent Project owner creating a Task becomes accountable by default; the Human may name any owner. Accountability transfers explicitly to another owner or the Human; when an owner is withdrawn, archived, removed, or leaves a Workspace, every open Task it was accountable for returns to the Human in the same operation with a public transfer activity.
14	- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.
15	- Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
16	- A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
17	- `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
18	- Notices are delivered by Attention. Every unread fact interrupts: a Main stream post, a new discussion, mentions, replies, ownership events, responsibility events and Task reminders wake immediately, and so does an ordinary Thread update for any Member following that Thread. The former owner and accountable threshold — five ordinary Thread updates per Member per Thread before a summary — is gone, so following a Thread now means being interrupted by its first ordinary update, and no identity places a reader in a slower class. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
19	- A Main stream commit wakes every Member whose Main stream Attention covers that stream, not only the Project's owners, so a non-owner follower is interrupted by the first ordinary update like anyone else. Following a Main stream requires Project membership, exactly as reading and writing it do, so an Attention row left behind by a departed Member delivers nothing and the follow cannot be the door that gets a Member in.
20	- An ownership grant no longer overwrites the Main stream Attention a Member already holds: a Member that followed and read before being granted ownership keeps its own read watermark, so granting ownership no longer silently clears its unread. The Human's own row is derived from owning the Project, so a Main stream unfollow from the Human is refused instead of committing an operation that changes nothing; `team_attention` takes `projectRef` or a Thread ref, never both, at the Host as well as the tool.
21	- A Thread the notice cannot render — the section cap or the character budget dropped it — keeps its facts undelivered, so the next relevant commit rederives and retries them instead of leaving them swallowed by a notice that never named them.
22	- An Attention row records what established it — starting the Thread, claiming its Task, being its accountable, owning the Project, being named in it, or choosing to follow — so a result can state why the reader follows instead of guessing. `team_attention` renders the cause once the reader follows, and a Claim result or a Thread start names the Attention it just established. The source is optional in storage: rows written before it existed keep their bytes; replay derives the missing cause from the operation that wrote the row and then validates the repaired projection strictly.
23	- The Main stream carries its own Attention, keyed by Member × Project and independent of any Thread's row, so ordinary Main stream unread no longer follows from owning the Project. The Human's row is derived from the Project's creation and only its read watermark is stored; an Agent's is written by the ownership grant, starting at the grant sequence so no historical backlog is inherited; any other Member's comes from an explicit follow. A Member that does not follow the Main stream holds markers alone — a mention or a reply still reaches it — and withdrawing ownership keeps the row, so the Member keeps its ordinary unread until it reads or unfollows. The Main stream standing's `owner` field is replaced by `following`.
24	- `team_attention` takes `projectRef` to follow or unfollow a Project's Main stream, mutually exclusive with `threadRef`/`taskRef`. Every Attention result states its consequence: following means ordinary updates from there interrupt you; unfollowing means they stop, while mentions, replies and responsibility events still reach you and no Claim or Task responsibility is released. `team_thread` states the reader's own Main stream Attention on a Main stream read, and prompts the unfollowed reader on a Thread read. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill no longer describe an owner threshold: no identity sits in a slower delivery class, owning a Project follows its Main stream rather than its Threads, and unfollowing stops ordinary updates only.
25	- Every visible Project carries one Main stream unread row in the Inbox, shared by the Human and Agents; `team_inbox` and the Human's inbox count agree.
26	- The task board: a `taskBoard` Host projection and Remote method lists every visible Project's open Tasks plus the last five finished per Project, and names the reader its `humanMemberId`. The Web Client reads this projection in both places — the Project board tab and the cross-Workspace Task board page the sidebar's 任务看板 entry opens (its own checklist glyph, a narrow-rail button, cards that say 「你负责」, and an empty state that stands alone without column heads). `team_claim` is merged into `team_task` (`board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `promote`); `team_view` no longer returns active task threads.
27	- The team-member persona is rewritten for project ownership and ships the `team-domain-model` core skill.
28	- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
29	- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.
30	
31	**Changed**
32	
33	- The Team settings nav row now carries the Team mark instead of the shell's generic gear. The shell draws nav glyphs by section id and `settings.section` offers no icon, so the row is tagged inside the settings dialog and the mark is painted over the shell glyph with a mask — the same contained workaround installed third-party themes use; it releases itself on dispose.
34	- The Client drops its version 1 paths: the old Project feed, `@all` expansion, and the invitation confirmation flow are gone. The Project page is the Main stream plus the board, and a Thread starts through the owner-only 讨论/任务 control.
35	- Exactly one sidebar row carries `aria-current="page"`: a global face (Inbox, Task board) no longer leaves the marker on the Workspace selector beneath it, and the auto-select no longer pulls the seat back to a Workspace overview while a global face stands.
36	- A Message's row actions stay on the Message they act on. The copy/quote card still floats at its row's top-right corner, but it is anchored to that row instead of to a rise measured upwards out of it: the rise put the card in the band the row above owns, so a Message that opens a run showed its actions over the empty gutter of the Message before it. A run head now hangs its card beside its own author line, clear of the first words by the row's own padding plus that line minus the card's height, and a continuation still rises over its run's own previous line; the Thread timeline no longer reserves the rise, so the first row of a page keeps its inset.
37	- A board card and a discussion's derived Task card answer the pointer on their own surface with the interactive fill the Thread card and the Inbox rows take. The previous hover only lightened the border: it left the fill untouched and made the one edge that reacted grow fainter under the pointer.
38	- The sidebar's unread mark now clears from a Main stream read as well as a Thread read. Both move the same private watermark and the Host derives both Inbox slices from it, but only a Thread read told the badge to re-read, so a Project's unread outlived the read that consumed it: the Inbox emptied while the mark stayed.
39	- An arriving Main stream entry keeps its accent bar for three seconds and then releases it on its own clock, instead of holding it until the reader leaves the page. Durable unread stays in the sidebar count and a Thread card's accessible name, which a read can clear.
40	- The Thread page's follow, transfer, accept, close, and reopen controls render as one action band of two groups separated by a 1px rule, instead of four sibling containers spread across the header. Every control in the band shares one 28px height, one radius, one 10px inline inset, one outlined stroke and one 6px step; widths stay content-sized. The followed state now paints the shipped selected fill (the ghost-active vocabulary `Pill` and `ClockPicker` already use) instead of reading as an unfollowed button with a different word. Visible verbs shorten to 关注/取消关注/转交 while the accessible names keep the full phrases and take the long pending phrase while a write runs, so the shorter word never leaves the write unannounced. That band's failures are one 12px line per refusing control under the band rather than the whole-surface `errorState`, and a committed transfer states the new accountable beside the control, retiring the line once the projection moves on.
41	- Mentions and replies are delivered from the message body alone: the `@Handle` names in a body, plus the quoted Message's author on a reply, are the whole recipient set for both the Web Client and `team_message`. The request no longer carries a separate `recipients` list, so a composer's notice and the Host's delivery read the same set.
42	- Maintained documentation and the shipped `agent-team` README no longer describe rules version 1 as current. Corrected: a Main stream message creates no Thread (`startThread` does); a mention or reply never starts or resumes Attention; `@all` is plain text; the invitation confirmation step is version 1 only; an owner's ordinary Main stream unread is delivered immediately; the request's explicit `recipients` list is stated as the input it is, unioned with the body's mentions, rather than denied; and `changeAttention` is recorded as a Host Remote the Web Client does not yet wire, instead of a control the Human Client is claimed to use. Bilingual pairs moved together.
43	
44	**Fixed**
45	
46	- The follow control reads the Human's own row out of the follower set instead of asking whether the set is non-empty. The set holds every Member whose Attention is on the Thread, so while any Agent still followed, the Human's unfollow left the button pressed with the pressed fill while its word read 「关注」; the same reading also made a press on a Thread only an Agent followed answer "already following". The Human's own Attention and notification gate were never wrong — only the Client's identity test was.
47	- Every whole-surface loading state renders one box in one place. The box centres by taking the free space itself (`min-height: 100%`) instead of relying on its container being a flex column, so the Task board and the discussion panel — plain block scroll boxes, where the vertical half of `margin: auto` resolves to zero — no longer drew their state against the top edge while the reading surfaces drew theirs in the middle; a whole-surface failure takes the same box so one surface never splits its two states. The board's loading frame was also drawn with the empty state's own style and no pulse mark, which read as 「already empty」 rather than 「still reading」. The Main stream no longer loads under the Projects sentence: it has its own key, and `正在读取看板…` joined the 「正在加载…」 verb family.
48	- The follow control's standing now tracks the Host instead of settling once. The Thread page took the observation it read on mount as permanently authoritative and never took the refreshes its own subscription performed, so a follow or unfollow another face or another client made left the button showing the previous standing — and the next press then wrote the opposite action to the one the Host held. The page hands in the one follower set it already re-reads, which is also what ranks the composer's mention candidates, so both read the same answer.
49	- Following a Thread again after unfollowing it now commits. The control cached a request id per action and never released it, so the second follow reused the first one's id and the Host answered from its idempotency cache with the earlier result: the button showed 「已关注」 while the Host's own follower set did not hold the Human. The id is now scoped to the action and the Thread and dropped once the Host has answered it, so only a write whose answer never arrived retries with the same id.
50	- The release snapshot a departing Member, an archived Member, an archived Project, or a Workspace exit writes now hands out a frozen claims array. The shared builder returned the caller's own array, which the archived and removed results also exposed, so a caller could edit the committed Claim records after the commit and leave replay and validation reading something the write never recorded.
51	- Every mention chip renders alike, the reader's own handle included, and no chip ink falls under the 4.5:1 body-text floor. The reader's own chip used to leave the business family for the success alias, which in this UI already means online, passing, or succeeded — so a `@handle` sitting beside those words read as 「this is fine」 rather than 「this is you」, and the same green on its own 14% tint measured 2.02:1 in the light theme, the least legible text on the reading path. Recognising yourself now belongs to the row, which already states it in `data-mentions-me` and the card's 「提到了你」 notice, and the mark follows the identity across a rename there. Chip ink mixes the business alias toward `label-primary` (5.89:1 light, 7.01:1 dark) and the notice's warn ink does the same (4.90:1 light, 7.63:1 dark), stated as a measured ratio over the painted pixels in the browser gate rather than as a token name.
52	- A Task card now says who owns the outcome and who is executing it as two different things instead of two grey phrases. The accountable owner stays text — the reader as 「你负责」 — because one named person has to be read; executors are the avatar stack the Project board already used, under a 「执行者」 caption, so 「负责人 Vera 已有执行者」 no longer leaves the reader guessing whether that boolean is a person. An open Task nobody has claimed says 「待认领」 rather than 「未指派」, which read as though the owner itself was unassigned while sitting right beside a named one; a resolved card drops the executor slot entirely, since nobody is executing finished work. The cross-Workspace board and the Project board now share one foot component (`BoardCardFoot`), so the two surfaces can no longer describe the same Task differently.
53	- Starting a Task from the Project composer now lands the keyboard focus on that Task's own new card instead of the 看板 tab. The composer unmounts with the switch, so focus has to move; parking it on the tab drew that tab's `:focus-visible` ring as a stray blue circle above the board, while the card is the thing the reader just created and Enter opens it. A pointer-driven send focuses the card without a visible ring, and the landing reuses the one `:focus-visible` ring every board card already draws rather than a second focus language.
54	
55	## [0.2.5] - 2026-10-24
56	
57	**Upgrade note**
58	
59	- Channel is now Project. New ledger records use `project:` refs, `projectRef` / `project` / `projectRefs` fields, and `team/project-*` kinds; records written before keep their bytes and still read. Compatibility is one-way: a build older than this release cannot open a ledger this release has written to, because it knows neither the `project:` ref spelling nor the `team/project-*` kinds and rejects the whole table at open. There is no interim release that reads both spellings, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` at the same time, and treat downgrading below it as unavailable.
60	- The generation swap records a new operation kind, `team/member-session-recycled`, in the durable ledger. An older build reading a ledger that contains one rejects the whole table at open, so downgrading below this release with a ledger that already recorded a swap leaves the Team unavailable until the release is restored. The domain version stays at 1: an additive kind never changes what a stored record means, which is the only thing the number is allowed to move for.
61	
62	**New**
63	
64	- A Project has owners once the ledger adopts rules version 2, which is still a preview: only `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES=1` adopts it, and the next release makes it the default. The Human owns every Project without being recorded, and grants or withdraws Agent owners from the Project dialog among Agents that participate in the Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving the Workspace, archival, or removal ends an ownership; suspension does not. Writes are non-optimistic and a Host error stays in the section's alert.
65	
66	**Changed**
67	
68	- Channel is renamed to Project on every surface: the Client (项目 in Chinese), the Remote (`createProject`, `updateProject`, `archiveProject`), tool parameters and output (`projectRef`), change scopes (`kind: 'project'`), and the `start_requires_project` rejection. `channel:` refs still resolve wherever a ref is accepted — a tool argument or a ref cited in a Message body — so Agents and older Messages that cite them keep working. Drafts, sidebar order, and the last open page saved in the browser carry over.
69	- Every Member starts restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`; a capability allow-list can only narrow that set. Later plugin tools are removed from request schemas and denied direct or nested execution. Same-name replacements reject requests and execution.
70	- When other official or custom plugins are enabled, Team mode filters their undeclared tools but does not filter their injected prompts. Current public Harness APIs do not provide complete per-Member prompt isolation: required contexts can be restored after assembly. Those prompts remain visible without blocking conversation; full plugin compatibility is not certified.
71	- A Member no longer manages its own context. The four context tools (`context_rollover`, `context_checkpoint`, `context_status`, `context_compact`) are gone, and so is the acceptance advice that used to ride a Thread read. The preset delegates in-place reduction to the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine` through a thin Team admission adapter; the compaction transaction and summary template stay upstream's. A generation swap is a Host decision: `team-context-management.ts` records `team/member-session-recycled` as the Host actor and activates a fresh Session parented at the one it replaces.
72	- An acceptance that concludes a Member's own work now leaves a boundary behind. The Host appends one `<system-reminder>` telling the Member to move durable conclusions into its `memory.md` index and the notes it names, and at or above 128000 measured tokens it also compacts the generation once the Agent settles. A follower who owns nothing on the Task sees the same accept as unread and is left alone, the reminder never promises a compaction the preset cannot run, and one turn spends at most one boundary however many accepted Tasks it reads.
73	- A Member's proactive input trigger is `floor(min(memberCompaction.tokens, window × 0.8, window − 16384))`, with an absolute default of 256000. A 272K model therefore triggers at 217600 without pre-reserving its maximum output. Pending input is counted; tool-result pruning precedes forced upstream reduction with no proportional retained tail. Summary output has its own 16384 cap. Normal output is limited to remaining window space and the original allowance, with temporary limits recomputed rather than persisted as future intent. An insufficient reduction ends the turn explicitly. A window under 20480 tokens cannot hold both fixed reserves, so the policy declines and that route keeps only the Agent's own limits. Disabling `memberCompaction` restores upstream pressure handling; overflow recovery and ordinary Sessions are unchanged.
74	- The Team settings page configures the in-place compaction threshold under 「上下文」: one capacity field (`256K`, `1M`, or a plain count) that writes `memberCompaction.tokens` through the shared configuration form. A blank field clears the override so the group returns to its 256000 default, and only that child path is written — the sibling `enabled` switch and the rest of the Host row keep the values they had.
75	- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
76	- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
77	- A swapped-in generation is told nothing about the swap. Its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection — identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list — plus the message that woke it; the handoff envelope, the generation announcement and the crash-time `Context handoff:` steer are all gone, because a successor that is told it received a handoff performs a handoff instead of reading its memory.
78	- A Member works in the directory the work is in. Its Session, Team participation, Claims, and write permissions stay bound to the Workspace it was created in, but its working directory moves: `working_directory` enters a Workspace the Member has joined and leaves it again, so relative paths, searches, new shells, `run_code`, and that checkout's `AGENTS.md` all resolve where the work actually is. The multi-Workspace guidance now says so instead of telling Members to reach across checkouts by absolute path, which silently skipped the other checkout's instructions.
79	- A Member's tool allow-list no longer removes `working_directory`. The restriction narrows capability; it does not confine a Member to its creation checkout, so the Host unions the tool over the configured list the way it already unions the Team tools.
80	- The bundle declares `engines.dsh` beside its DSH peers. DSH decides a plugin's compatibility from that field alone when it is present, so an install on an uncertified Harness now reports one unmet requirement instead of listing every peer package.
81	- A stale-revision rejection now says how the writer's token related to the Thread instead of carrying a lone `tokenUnrecognized` flag: `staleTokenKind` is `unrecognized` for a token this Thread's revisions skipped over, `unknown` for one older than its first fact, and absent for a plain insertion race. The model-facing refusal is unchanged in words, but a caller that read the boolean must read the new field.
82	- The Inbox and feed rows name Claim owners as `liveClaimOwners` rather than `claimOwners`, so the field matches the rule that produces it: owners of live Claims only, empty once the Task is resolved.
83	- A discussion panel's width is the reader's. Opening one gives it the larger share of the surface (52% of it, clamped to 420–960px) instead of a fixed 360px column, and a seam between the panel and the feed drags that share either way with arrow keys as well as the pointer. Both surfaces read one variable, so the feed gives up exactly what the panel takes, the band above gives up the same width so a long Project description ellipsizes beside the seam rather than running under it, and the seat is remembered per browser and re-clamped to whatever surface it reopens on. The panel is the surface's own child rather than the feed's, so it spans the band and the feed as one column: its head now shares the band's identity row — the same 10px inset and 30px row as the Project title — instead of starting under the tab strip, and its foot composer stands on the feed composer's line. The two rules that used to close those two rows are gone; the band's own rule already ends the row they framed. Below 600px the panel covers the feed in the surface's single column, so the band above keeps its width and its identity row stays whole.
84	- The discussion panel's Messages carry the row actions the Thread page gives them. Hovering a row opens the same card — copy, and a quote that fills the panel's own composer with the Message as the reply's parent — and a row that answers another leads with its quote line, which scrolls to the original inside the panel instead of walking the reader to another page. The panel was the one surface rendering Thread rows without the reading language, so quoting from it was impossible without leaving it. The first row of any scroll box took its card's rise as headroom: the rule that was meant to pay for it named a row as the box's own child, which a run wrapper never is, so the first row's card was clipped by the scroll edge on both surfaces.
85

1	# dsh-agent-team Domain Vocabulary
2	
3	English | [中文](domain-model.zh.md)
4	
5	## Agent Team
6	
7	The single shared collaboration domain in one DSH home. It stores cross-member collaboration facts, not model context, session transcripts, or private memory.
8	
9	## Member
10	
11	A stable identity authorized to read, speak, claim work, and receive Inbox hints. A Member is identified by an immutable branded ref. Private memory, skills, persona, and model are Member-global facts, not per-Workspace state. The first release has Human and Agent Members.
12	
13	## Workspace Participation
14	
15	A join/leave relation between a Member and a Workspace, committed as ledger operations — the same relation shape as Project participation, one rung above it (Workspace participation → Project participation, derived from Threads → Thread Attention). A Member's `workspaceId` records where it was created and never changes; authorization everywhere reads the current participation set, not the creation field. Joining grants collaboration immediately; it does not move or create the Member's Session. Each Member retains one Session lineage in its creation Workspace.
16	
17	Joining does not create another Session; collaboration in other participated Workspaces uses the same Session, and the Member moves its own working directory into them with `working_directory`. The Human Member participates in every Workspace.
18	
19	## Human Member
20	
21	The special Member corresponding to the current Harness user. It participates in Messages, Claims, and Activities and can manage Projects, Members, acceptance, and Task terminal state.
22	
23	## Agent Member
24	
25	A Member created and managed by Team. Created inside one Workspace (its creation record), it joins further Workspaces through Workspace Participation. It runs one explicit team-enabled preset Session at a time, rooted in its creation Workspace; ordinary Sessions and forks do not gain membership automatically.
26	
27	## Member Capabilities
28	
29	Durable capability intent on the Member entity (optional `capabilities` field: `tools.allow` and `skills.allow`), carried verbatim through every lifecycle operation and restored by Host restart replay. Pure intent: allow-list names are not validated against any known-name set at commit time — a Harness upgrade that renames or removes tools can never make an old ledger unreplayable. Divergence from the names known at activation is derived as a runtime warning (`capabilityWarnings`, a projection-derived state, never persisted — persisted warnings would lie after Host restart or upgrades).
30	
31	## Workspace
32	
33	A shared working directory and authorization domain. An Agent Member's Session header cwd is its creation Workspace's directory and never changes; the directory it works in is the Session's own, movable through `working_directory`. Private memory lives outside the Workspace directory.
34	
35	## Project
36	
37	A persistent collaboration place in a Workspace. A Member takes part in a Project by taking part in one of its Threads — reading, speaking, claiming, or following — and that is what authorizes it everywhere in the Project; there is no separate enrolment to grant. Human Members can view every Workspace Project.
38	
39	Once the ledger adopts rules version 2, a Project has owners: the Human owns every Project without being recorded, and the Human grants or withdraws Agent owners (`team/project-owner-added` / `team/project-owner-removed`) among Agents that participate in the Project's Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving that Workspace, archival, or removal ends an Agent's ownership; suspension does not.
40	
41	From version 2, Project membership also counts owners and every Member ever mentioned in the Project, and drops archived and inactive Members; everything visible under version 1 stays visible.
42	
43	Behind rules version 2 a Project also has a Main stream: a conversation of its own, outside every Thread. Any Project member may post to it (`team/main-message-posted`). A Main stream Message carries `scope: 'main'`, no Thread or Task, and may only answer another Main stream Message of the same Project. Mentioning a Member, or answering their Message (the Human included), gives them one Main stream marker; `@all` is plain text.
44	
45	A reader's ordinary Main stream unread comes from its own Main stream Attention — what other Members wrote after that row's read watermark — plus its markers. The Human's row is derived from the Project's creation and never stored; an Agent's is written by its ownership grant, and any other Member's by an explicit follow. Withdrawing ownership keeps the row, so the Member keeps its ordinary unread until it reads or unfollows; removal and archival end it, while leaving the Workspace and archiving the Project do not.
46	
47	[Attention and messaging](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns the rows.
48	
49	A writer holding Main stream unread reads first (`main_unread_required`). `team/main-stream-read` advances the reader's own Main stream watermark and consumes markers, and writes nothing when it would change neither.
50	
51	Behind rules version 2 only a Project owner starts a Thread (`team/thread-started`, kind `discussion` or `task`) and the top-level `team/message-sent` is no longer written; anyone else gets `project_owner_required`, which points to the Main stream.
52	
53	A Thread appears in the Main stream as a card showing its current state: anchor preview, reply count, writers and newest activity for a discussion; Task number, status and live Claim owners for a Task. Version-1 top-level Threads appear as cards in creation order and are never unread.
54	
55	Behind rules version 2 any Project member may reply in any Thread. A mention or an answer is one direct marker and never starts or resumes Attention, and the Human invitation confirmation no longer exists.
56	
57	## Message
58	
59	Immutable content explicitly sent in a Project or existing Thread. A Thread is created by `startThread`, never by a Main stream message: `postMainMessage` writes a Main stream Message that belongs to no Thread, and `startThread` writes the Thread's anchor. A started Thread is a discussion, or a Task when `kind: 'task'` asks for one; a taskless Thread can later gain a Task through Human promotion. A reply continues an existing Thread. Every Message carries the wall-clock instant of its committing operation; agent-facing surfaces render that instant in the fixed UTC+8 coordination zone.
60	
61	## Task
62	
63	An optional work-tracking overlay attached to an existing Thread, not a prerequisite for a Thread. It can be created by explicit top-level task intent or added by Human promotion. Promotion also appends a public explanation Message. Task status is derived from Claims; acceptance and close are explicit facts. Human-facing `Task #N` is the durable Task creation ordinal within its home Project: taskful starts and promotions participate, while a taskless anchor's original position does not. It is not identity; stable cross-project references use branded `taskRef`.
64	
65	One accountable owner carries responsibility for the Task. An Agent Project owner creating one is accountable by default; the Human chooses the accountable when needed, among enabled Project owners and the Human. Execution stays in Claims, so accountability is not ownership of the work. `sourceThreadRefs` immutably names the same Project's taskless source discussions; sourced Tasks appear as read-only current-state cards there rather than in the Main stream.
66	
67	Acceptance normally waits for every Claim to be done (`in_review`). The Human may also accept early from `in_progress`: the accept operation projects the Claims still active at that moment to done and records them in the activity as `completedClaimRefs`, notifying each owner without fabricating owner claim-done events. A `todo` Task that was never claimed is accepted directly, and its activity carries no claim list.
68	
69	An Agent can accept only in `in_review`, as a Project owner who never held any Claim on that Task, including a released Claim. Otherwise an accountable who executed asks an uninvolved owner or the Human to verify, or transfers accountability. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human or the current accountable; only the Human transfers a finished Task. Transfer keeps the Claims with their executors. Withdrawing, archiving, removing, or withdrawing the Workspace of an accountable Agent returns each open Task to the Human atomically; suspension does not transfer it.
70	
71	## Thread
72	
73	An independent, single-level public collaboration aggregate inside a Project. It always has `threadRef`, an anchor Message, and a revision, but may have no Task. Public Messages increment revision; Taskful Claim and resolution changes do too. Existing-Thread writes require current revision. A taskless Thread still supports replies, follows, structured mentions, Inbox, reads, and history, but has no Claims, Task status, or resolution controls.
74	
75	Collaboration uses `threadRef` first; a released task-only Client may use `taskRef` as a Host compatibility alias only for taskful Threads, while Task/Claim operations use `taskRef` identity. Revision is an internal concurrency token, not citable message content.
76	
77	## Claim
78	
79	A Member's commitment to one Direction in a Task overlay. Taskless Threads have no Claims. States are active, done, and released; after normalization, one Task has at most one active Claim for the same Direction. Multiple Claims intentionally allow different text that may describe duplicate work.
80	
81	## Direction
82	
83	Free-text work direction for a Claim. Comparisons apply Unicode normalization, trim, whitespace compression, and case folding; synonyms are not inferred.
84	
85	## Thread Attention
86	
87	A private persistent attention period for one Member and Thread: the current period's start and a contiguous read watermark. Its presence is what following means, and it is not public revision. What starts and ends a period is in [attention-and-messaging.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md).
88	
89	## Thread Inbox
90	
91	Member-level unread projection derived from Thread Attention and direct mentions. It is not a Session queue, browser state, or per-message read table; its derivation and read semantics are in [attention-and-messaging.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md), and the tool contract in [tools.md](team-collaboration/tools.md).
92	
93	## Follow
94	
95	An operation on Thread Attention, not an independent subscription object. Follow controls whether ordinary updates create Inbox work and does not revoke Project visibility.
96	
97	## Activity
98	
99	A recorded collaboration-state fact. Claim create/done/release, Task accept/close/reopen, and promotion are public revisioned Thread facts; follow/unfollow and read watermarks are private Attention audit facts. Runtime errors may be current Human UI risk but are not ledger Activity or Inbox facts.
100	
101	## Inbox Hint
102	
103	A safe-boundary hint derived from durable Thread Inbox state. A hint is bounded and may wake an idle Agent or arrive at a running Agent's next safe step; it does not mean the model read, handled, replied to, or accepted anything. Durable Inbox is rediscovered after resume.
104	
105	## Operation
106	
107	One immutable atomic business commit in the Team ledger. Each operation has global sequence, stable operation ID, idempotent request ID, actor, one business fact, and a wall-clock `occurredAt`. Sequence — never the instant — is the ordering and concurrency authority; Thread fact envelopes project the committing operation's instant so every reread path sees one value per fact.
108	
109	## Revision
110	
111	The sequence of the latest operation relevant to a Thread. It is an optimistic concurrency fence, not a Message count.
112	
113	## Ref
114	
115	A restart-stable, typed identifier that callers cannot safely construct by concatenation. Member, Project, Task, Thread, Message, Claim, and Operation use distinct branded refs. Attention is identified by Member plus Thread.
116	
117	## Direct Message
118	
119	A private Member-to-Member message, not part of any Thread. The ledger appends one audit-only `team/dm-sent` operation (request-idempotent; sender and recipient must be enabled Agent Members of the same Workspace) while the projection deliberately stays unchanged — no Project, Thread, revision, Attention, or Inbox markers. Delivery is a transient runtime effect: an idle recipient opens a followup turn with the body as a relay-form user message, a busy one is steered into the current turn, and the text carries one bounded line of adjacent context.
120	
121	A failed wake leaves the durable fact intact and the sender gets a structured delivery error instead of a silent loss; there is no automatic redelivery. A DM is for quick clarifications and status syncs; task work belongs in Threads. A possible future private Place with its own participants and visibility would get separate authority and notification design.
122	
123	## Runtime Presence
124	
125	An in-process availability projection, not a ledger fact: available (live idle), working (loop running), error (current loop/tool failure), and unavailable (no usable handle or lifecycle/setup/resume block, including the brief context-rollover window where the ledger binding has moved but the new Session is not live yet). It is separate from Claim state.
126	
127	## Member Diagnostic
128	
129	The structured reason behind a non-normal presence or availability row, never persisted: `session-refused` (a deterministic format refusal of a Session the activation needed; may carry the refused artifact's location and whether a repair attempt proved anything remediable), `session-unreadable` (missing, corrupt, io, or unknown Session read failure), `preset-composition` (preset mount/validation failure, typically an install/runtime split), `rollover` (the transient commit window), `runtime` (live loop or compaction failure), or `activation` (unclassified activation failure).
130	
131	The `class` routes which recovery action actually helps: a non-remediable refusal or a rollover window offers no restart, while everything else may recover through restart.
132	
133	## Context Generation
134	
135	One Member Session's working context between two generation boundaries. A fresh generation starts empty: its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection (identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list) plus whatever message woke it, and it is never told a generation changed. The ledger records the current binding (one per Member at all times) and the previous Session of the latest transition; the Session logs themselves hold the context history. Every generation keeps Member identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention.
136	
137	A swap is the Host's decision alone, taken at a wake boundary. A legacy log may still carry a checkpoint anchor, a rollover pair, or a pending intent written by an earlier build; the fold keeps decoding them so old ledgers and old Session logs still read back, but no current build produces any of them.
138	
139	## Suspend
140	
141	Temporarily stop a Member's live Agent while retaining identity, Session, Claims, Attention, unread state, and private memory. Resume uses the same Session and durable unread to decide whether to hint Inbox.
142	
143	## Withdraw
144	
145	Leaving one Workspace: `team/member-workspace-left` ends the Member's participation there, exits its Project memberships in that Workspace, releases that Workspace's active Claims, and clears its Attention there. Everything else — the Member identity, other participations, the live Session and its cwd, private memory — is untouched; the creation Workspace cannot be left — use global archival instead. The UI presents this as the destructive row action on a non-creation Workspace.
146	
147	## Archive
148	
149	The hidden third state between Suspend and Remove, for Members and Projects. It is reversible in design — the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore — but there is deliberately no restore entry point this round, mirroring archived dsh sessions. `archiveMember` disposes the live session (private memory and the Session log stay on disk) and releases active Claims across every participated Workspace with public `claims_released` Activities; `archiveProject` applies the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads.
150	
151	Memberships survive archival (hidden state, not departure). Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface — projections, mention candidates, ref resolution, and ref-addressed reads reject with an explicit archived error. Removal from archived remains available as the data-hygiene path.
152	
153	## Remove
154	
155	Irreversibly deactivate an Agent Member: release active Claims, end Attention, delete private memory, and archive its Session. Historical Messages, Activities, and identity snapshots remain.
156	
157	## Member Lifecycle
158	
159	The desired external state of each durable Member state, in one table. Every lifecycle operation runs exactly this effect set right after its commit, and Host startup re-runs it for each Member, so a crash or a failed effect between commit and effect converges by repeating the same derivation:
160

# Distill Memory

Save proactively when the conversation produces a durable fact, preference, decision, plan, procedure, learning, event, or important context. Do not wait to be asked.

## When to Suggest (Moment Detection)

**Breakthrough:** Extended debugging resolves, user relief ("Finally!", "Aha!"), root cause found

**Decision:** Compared options, chose with rationale, trade-off resolved

**Research:** Investigated multiple approaches, conclusion reached, optimal path determined

**Twist:** Unexpected cause-effect, counterintuitive solution, assumption challenged

**Lesson:** "Next time do X", preventive measure, pattern recognized

**Skip:** Routine fixes, work in progress, simple Q&A, generic info

## Memory Quality

**Good (atomic + actionable):**

- "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused leaks."
- "PostgreSQL over MongoDB: ACID needed for transactions."

**Poor:** Vague "Fixed bugs", conversation transcript

## Tool Usage

Use `nmem` CLI to create memories:

```bash
nmem m add "Insight + context for future use" \
  -t "Searchable title (50-60 chars)" \
  -i 0.8
```

Add `--unit-type fact|preference|decision|plan|procedure|learning|context|event` when the type is clear.

If an existing memory already captures the same decision, workflow, or preference and the new information refines it, update that memory instead of creating a duplicate:

```bash
nmem m update <id> -t "Updated title"
```

**Content:** Outcome/insight focus, include "why", enough context

**Importance:** 0.8-1.0 major | 0.5-0.7 useful | 0.3-0.4 minor

**Note:** For programmatic use, add `--json` flag to get JSON response

**Examples:**

```bash
# High-value insight
nmem m add "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused memory leaks in event listeners." \
  -t "React Hooks Cleanup Pattern" \
  -i 0.9

# Decision with context
nmem m add "Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for ACID compliance and complex queries" \
  -t "Database: PostgreSQL" \
  -i 0.9
```

## Suggestion

**Timing:** After resolution/decision, when user pauses

**Pattern:** "This [type] seems valuable - [essence]. Distill into memory?"

**Frequency:** 1-3 per session typical, quality over quantity

## Troubleshooting

If `nmem` is not in PATH: `pip install nmem-cli`, or on Arch Linux `yay -S nmem-cli` / `paru -S nmem-cli`

For remote servers: run `nmem config client set url https://...` and `nmem config client set api-key ...` once on this machine.

Run `/status` to check server connection.

[`memory-and-context.md`](../team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) defines the budgets. Generation swaps remain Host decisions, never model ones.

21	The generation swap is owned by `team-context-management.ts`, Team's own coordinator. It starts from a Host wake decision rather than a durable intent, executes through the serialized lifecycle queue, and takes the successor's identity from the retired Session so a crash converges on one successor:
22	
23	1. wait for true idle;
24	2. recheck the owned-jobs guard and the ordinary-input queue at the commit seam — a queued ordinary message defers the swap;
25	3. inside `agent.runMaintenance`, commit the idempotent `team/member-session-recycled` operation as the Host actor, recording `inputFromSeq` (the retired log's offset) when a live generation exists;
26	4. retire the old generation: its pre-step gate rejects the step without a model request, then dispose and archive (never delete); the original inbox insertions remain in the log even if already claimed;
27	5. activate the fresh Session, parented at the one it replaces;
28	6. fold the retired log from `inputFromSeq`, drop every message the successor already holds by id, deliver the rest by followup, then rederive the Inbox from the ledger.
29	
30	Maintenance is what makes the commit safe against input arriving mid-swap: the loop is parked there, so a new message waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired. A failed commit releases maintenance and the old generation continues; a committed one retires it, and startup or recovery finishes a swap interrupted before the replay.
31	
32	The successor's first model-facing context is its ordinary per-step injection — identity, `memory.md`, the workspace list — plus the message that woke it. There is no handoff envelope and no generation announcement: a successor told it received a handoff performs a handoff instead of reading its memory.
33	
34	The fold is Team's own `contextContinuity` projection unit, registered once per host at Team service init. `context-projection.ts` owns the durable checkpoint-ref naming, the Team-notice rule, the fork cut, and the folded state a generation reads back: its checkpoints with their turn-end delivery state, at most one legacy rollover intent, the continuation delivery records, and the unconsumed non-Team input the retired generation never consumed. 35

5	## Mutation fences
6	Existing-Thread public mutations require the current next-write token in `baseRevision` — an opaque copy-through value, not a fact about the Thread. The model copies the latest explicitly rendered value verbatim and never increments, derives, compares, or cites it. The token appears on exactly two surfaces: a `team_thread read` that leaves no unread remaining, and a committed public mutation (`team_message` start/reply, `team_task` mutation) whose result returns the resulting Thread state.
7	
8	It is absent from `team_view`, `team_inbox`, `team_thread status/follow/unfollow/history`, `team_task list`, partial reads, and every typed rejection — a fresh-looking token there would invite a blind retry.
9	
10	Host checks: (1) relevant unread must be read, otherwise `unread_required`; (2) the token must match the current Thread revision, otherwise `stale_revision`; (3) closed Tasks reject replies, Claims, and new Attention. Taskless Threads have no Claim or Task-resolution mutation. These are normal collaboration outcomes, not infrastructure failures; there is no force-send or unread bypass.
11	
12	An exemption sits inside check (1) and only there. When every unread fact is already on the writer's model-visible surface in full, the write is allowed without a read — the notice that carried the body is itself the reading.
13	
14	The exemption persists nothing: no attention watermark advances, no direct marker is consumed, and the durable "has this been read" answer stays exactly what it was. One fact off the surface keeps the write refused, and a Member with no live Session is never exempt. A rejected mutation still renders no bypass: it carries the facts that gated the write and the current revision to retry with, and recovery is read the Thread and reconsider.
15	
16	Close releases active Claims and ends Attention. Reopen restores an open Task, not previous Attention periods; a new reopen restores the accountable's current Thread follow unless the accountable is the actor or already follows. Older reopen records keep their marker-only replay semantics.

6	既有 Thread 上的 public mutation 必须在 `baseRevision` 中携带当前的 next-write token。它是不透明的 copy-through 值，不是关于 Thread 的事实：模型原样复制最近一次显式渲染的值。绝不递增、推导、比较或引用它。令牌只出现在两个位置。第一，一次未读清零的 `team_thread read`。第二，一次结果返回结果 Thread 状态的已提交 public mutation（`team_message` start/reply、`team_task` mutation）。它不出现在 `team_view`、`team_inbox`、`team_thread status/follow/unfollow/history`、`team_task list`、未读完的 read，以及所有类型化拒绝中——这些位置一个看似新鲜的令牌反而会诱导盲重试。
7	
8	Host 按以下顺序检查 fences：
9	
10	1. 相关 unread work 必须先读完；失败返回带当前 unread counts 的 `unread_required`。
11	2. 令牌必须匹配当前 Thread revision；失败返回 `stale_revision`。
12	3. Closed Task 拒绝 replies、Claims 和 new Attention；taskless Threads 没有 Claim 或 Task-resolution mutation path。
13	
14	第 (1) 条内部有一个豁免，且只在这一条内。当每条 unread fact 的正文都已经完整出现在写入者的 model-visible surface 上时，写入可以不经过 read 直接放行——把正文带上去的那条 notice 本身就是这次阅读。该豁免不落任何账：attention 水位不推进、direct marker 不消耗，durable 的「是否已读」答案保持原样。只要有一条 fact 不在 surface 上，写入继续被挡；没有活 Session 的 Member 永远不豁免。被拒的 mutation 同样不提供 bypass：它带回挡住这次写入的 facts 和可用于重试的当前 revision，恢复动作是 read 这个 Thread 再重新考虑。
15	
16	这些结果属于正常协作结果，不是 infrastructure failures。被拒绝的 mutation 仍不提供 bypass：它带回挡住这次写入的事实与重试所用的当前 revision。恢复永远是读取 Thread 并重新考虑。不存在 force-send 或 unread bypass。
17	
18	close 会 release active Claims、结束 Attention 并停止 ordinary delivery。reopen 恢复 open Task，但不恢复旧 Attention periods；新的 reopen 会为 accountable 恢复当前 Thread follow，accountable 是操作者或已经 follow 时除外。旧 reopen 记录保持只加 marker 的回放语义。
19	
20	## Ownership 与 Task 权限
21	Project owner 才能发起或 promotion Thread。accountable 与执行分离，担任 accountable 不等于获得 Project owner 权限；非 owner 的 Project member 也能执行 Task。
22

115	Before pushing, follow [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

129	## Conventions
130	
131	- Packages use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendor is [rescoped](docs/rescope.md) and `private: true`. Harness packages declare `@deepseek-ai/cordis` in `peerDependencies`/`devDependencies`. Workspace dependency sections use DSH `workspace:*`, vendor/native `workspace:~` ([rules](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-10-npm-release-sequences.md)).
132	- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
133	- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
134	- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. `SessionEventMap` members are required-on-read unless the envelope carries `ignorable: true`. Bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` only when existing discriminators cannot prevent unsafe interpretation; same-version changes require safe reader behavior ([review](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-10-08-session-reader-compatibility-review.md)).
135	- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
136	- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
137	- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
138	- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
139	- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
140	- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
141	- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
142	- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
143	- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
144	- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
145	- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
146	- **No new assertions to `unknown`** (`as unknown` or `<unknown>`). Preserve or reduce the exact legacy baseline; use typed values or validation for replacements ([rule](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-19-no-unknown-casts.md)).
147	- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
148	- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** A package with both Host and Client programs exposes face-specific leaf configs and a solution-only root; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
149	- **Error handling:** use typed, structured failures and localized, actionable reports. Define handling ownership, containment, and failure guarantees; stop dependent work and visibly report untrusted state or unknown outcomes. Follow [dsh-error-handling](.agents/skills/dsh-error-handling/SKILL.md).
150	- **An empty `catch` names the error** and why; keep its `try` to one statement.
151	- **Keep comments local.** Do not restate code, expand unrelated comments, or explain distant behavior without local need ([rationale](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md)).
152	- **Ban `prove` + `nance`** ([rule](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-26-ban-ambiguous-origin-label.md)).
153	- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
154	- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
155	- **Create Agent Notes only for durable decision rationale;** mechanical/local edits are exempt, including local UI changes ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
156	- **Official plugin artwork:** use [dsh-official-plugin-artwork](.agents/skills/dsh-official-plugin-artwork/SKILL.md) for official and official experimental plugin icons; obtain designer approval before landing new glyphs.
157	- **Client UI copy is locale-owned.** Route product text through typed dictionaries and `t` or localized primitive props; `verify-client-ui-i18n` rejects hardcoded copy ([decision](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-23-locale-owned-client-ui-copy.md)).
158	- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible change updates a keyless recorded-session snapshot; [snapshot ownership](snapshots/AGENTS.md) reserves the top-level tree for session-driven cases and keeps other expected output owner-local. Fixtures replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
159	- **Design each tool's UI presentation up front.** Host presenters stay pure; Web cards derive from raw events and persisted result metadata ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
160	- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
161	- **Both SDKs project the loop.** Agent-loop, session-lifecycle, and `SessionEventMap` changes update the TypeScript and Python SDK expected outputs in the same PR; `pnpm run test` covers neither ([surfaces](docs/testing.md#when-a-snapshot-test-is-required)).
162	- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes and fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone/stack branches may merge-forward or rebase. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; preserve an in-progress merge-forward checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
163	- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
164	- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
165	- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

167	## Defensive patterns
168	
169	Read [docs/defensive-patterns/README.md](docs/defensive-patterns/README.md) before changing a package surface, remote service, client component or state, conversation or Session behavior, or lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, and teardown code. Its [review principles](docs/defensive-patterns/README.md#why-these-rules) apply per artifact.
170	
171	## Type safety and documentation
172	
173	Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.
174	
175	Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.
176	
177	Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

8	Upkeep craft (what earns a line, the three tiers, compaction and demotion) is owned by the bundled `member-memory-manager` core skill, on the same pattern as skill craft in `member-skill-manager`. The persona carries only the resident rule that the index stays bounded and that detail lives in the note it names, and a Member's first-run `memory.md` scaffold states the same sections.
9	
10	## Member context injection
11	A Member's per-step context is assembled as four classified blocks: identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and private memory. Each block is a separate surface message; a later block of the same class supersedes the earlier one semantically — the earlier message stays in the Session log and surface until compaction — and an unchanged class appends nothing. Ownership and participation are always stated in full, including an empty ownership list and a participation list that shrank from several Workspaces to one.
12	
13	Private memory has two shapes. The complete index is the baseline. After `memory.md` changes, the Member gets one compact notice that the earlier copy is stale, where the file is, and its current budget use. The newest memory event is compared with the file's current state, so an older matching notice cannot hide a later change. A notice is not an index: a compaction that leaves only the notice still triggers the latest complete baseline. A missing, unreadable, or over-budget index states that condition and its path instead of injecting content.
14	
15	## Context lifecycle ownership
16	A Member's context has exactly two mechanisms, and neither is the model's to invoke.
17	
18	**In-place compaction.** The preset mounts `member-compaction-engine`, a thin adapter over the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine`. Team owns proactive request admission; the parent supplies the summary template, tool-pair-safe reduction, durable transaction, and overflow retries. Compaction never changes generation or deletes the original log.
19	
20	The input trigger is `floor(min(B, W × 0.8, W − 16384))`, where `B` is `memberCompaction.tokens` (default 256000) and `W` is the routed window. Without a declared window the absolute budget still applies. A 1M or 2M model triggers at 256000; a 272000 model triggers at 217600. Model maximum output is not subtracted from this trigger. Pending messages, assembled tools, and system-prompt growth are counted before admission.

29	  readonly bodyLength: number
30	}
31	
32	interface RenderedFactSurface {
33	  readonly threadRef: string
34	  readonly messages: readonly RenderedMessageIdentity[]
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * The projected text of every Team-authored notice and every Team tool result on this agent's surface, newest first.
39	 *
40	 * `surface.nodes` holds SessionSeq values while `snapshotEvents` takes SessionLogOffsets; they line up only through the seq = log.length contiguity contract, so the conversion goes through the validating constructor. The content comes from `deriveEventMessage`, which applies message projections (compaction and pruning); reading the raw event would miss a rewrite that removed the body.
41	 */
42	export function visibleTeamSurface(agent: Agent): readonly VisibleTeamSurfaceEntry[] {
43	  const entries: VisibleTeamSurfaceEntry[] = []
44	  for (const sequence of agent.session.surface.nodes.toReversed()) {
45	    const event = agent.session.snapshotEvents(SessionLogOffset(sequence), SessionLogOffset(sequence + 1))[0]
46	    if (event === undefined) continue
47	    const message = agent.session.deriveEventMessage(event)
48	    if (message === null) continue
49	    if (event.type === 'user/message') {
50	      const source = message.source
51	      if (!isAgentTeamSource(source)) continue
52	      if (source.form !== 'notice') continue
53	      entries.push({ kind: 'notice', text: textOf(message.content) })
54	      continue
55	    }
56	    if (event.type !== 'tool/result') continue
57	    const surface = renderedFactSurfaceOf((event.data as { readonly meta?: unknown }).meta)
58	    if (surface === undefined) continue
59	    entries.push({ kind: 'tool-result', text: textOf(message.content), surface })
60	  }
61	  return entries
62	}
63	
64	/** The text blocks of one message, in order; a rendered body always lives inside one block. */
65	function textOf(content: readonly { readonly type: string; readonly text?: string }[]): string {
66	  return content.flatMap(part => part.type === 'text' && part.text !== undefined ? [part.text] : []).join('\n')
67	}
68	
69	/**
70	 * Whether one unread fact's body is on the surface in full, bound to this Thread and Message.
71	 *
72	 * Notification text carries explicit `Thread:` and `Message ref:` lines beside the body. A Team tool result carries the same identity in its private meta, while the body must still be in the projected content; that is what separates a complete result from one whose content a pruner replaced while leaving meta intact.
73	 */
74	export function isFactOnSurface(entries: readonly VisibleTeamSurfaceEntry[], fact: AgentTeamThreadReadFact, threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef): boolean {
75	  if (fact.fact.kind !== 'message') return false
76	  const body = fact.fact.message.body
77	  if (body === '') return false
78	  const messageRef = fact.fact.message.messageRef
79	  return entries.some(entry => entry.kind === 'notice'
80	    ? noticeAttests(entry.text, threadRef, messageRef, body)
81	    : toolResultAttests(entry.text, entry.surface, threadRef, messageRef, body))
82	}
83	
84	/** Whether one direct-mention block names both refs and then carries the body at its own `Message:` position, uncut. */
85	function noticeAttests(text: string, threadRef: string, messageRef: string, body: string): boolean {
86	  const marker = 'Direct Team mention\n'
87	  for (let start = text.indexOf(marker); start !== -1; start = text.indexOf(marker, start + 1)) {
88	    const headerEnd = text.indexOf('\nMessage: ', start)
89	    if (headerEnd === -1) continue
90	    const header = text.slice(start, headerEnd)
91	    if (!hasLine(header, 'Thread', threadRef) || !hasLine(header, 'Message ref', messageRef)) continue
92	    const bodyStart = headerEnd + '\nMessage: '.length
93	    if (!text.startsWith(body, bodyStart)) continue
94	    const rest = text.slice(bodyStart + body.length)
95	    if (rest.startsWith(`\n${NOTIFICATION_TRUNCATION_MARKER}`)) continue
96	    if (rest !== '' && !rest.startsWith('\n')) continue
97	    return true
98	  }
99	  return false
100	}
101	
102	function hasLine(block: string, label: string, value: string): boolean {
103	  return block.split('\n').includes(`${label}: ${value}`)
104	}
105	
106	/** A tool result attests only when its meta names this Thread and Message and the projected content still carries the full body. */
107	function toolResultAttests(text: string, surface: RenderedFactSurface, threadRef: string, messageRef: string, body: string): boolean {
108	  if (surface.threadRef !== threadRef) return false
109	  const identity = surface.messages.find(message => message.messageRef === messageRef)
110	  if (identity === undefined || identity.bodyLength !== body.length) return false
111	  return bodyAtLineBoundary(text, body)
112	}
113	
114	/** Whether the body is present as a whole rendered segment, not as a prefix of a longer body or a fragment inside one. */
115	function bodyAtLineBoundary(text: string, body: string): boolean {
116	  for (let at = text.indexOf(body); at !== -1; at = text.indexOf(body, at + 1)) {
117	    const before = at === 0 ? '\n' : text[at - 1]!
118	    const afterIndex = at + body.length
119	    const after = afterIndex === text.length ? '\n' : text[afterIndex]!
120	    if ((before === '\n' || before === ' ') && after === '\n') return true
121	  }
122	  return false
123	}
124	
125	/** Parse and validate one tool result's private fact binding; malformed or foreign meta binds nothing. */
126	function renderedFactSurfaceOf(meta: unknown): RenderedFactSurface | undefined {
127	  if (typeof meta !== 'object' || meta === null || Array.isArray(meta)) return undefined
128	  const record = meta as Record<string, unknown>
129	  if (record['surface'] !== FACT_SURFACE_META || typeof record['threadRef'] !== 'string' || typeof record['messages'] !== 'string') return undefined
130	  let parsed: unknown
131	  try {
132	    parsed = JSON.parse(record['messages'])
133	  } catch {
134	    return undefined
135	  }
136	  if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) return undefined
137	  const messages: RenderedMessageIdentity[] = []
138	  for (const entry of parsed) {
139	    if (typeof entry !== 'object' || entry === null) return undefined
140	    const message = entry as Record<string, unknown>
141	    if (typeof message['messageRef'] !== 'string' || typeof message['bodyLength'] !== 'number') return undefined
142	    messages.push({ messageRef: message['messageRef'], bodyLength: message['bodyLength'] })
143	  }
144	  return { threadRef: record['threadRef'], messages }
145	}
146	
147	export function surfaceVisibilityProbe(agentFor: (memberId: AgentTeamMemberId) => Agent | undefined) {
148	  return (memberId: AgentTeamMemberId, fact: AgentTeamThreadReadFact, threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef): boolean => {
149	    const agent = agentFor(memberId)
150	    if (agent === undefined) return false
151	    return isFactOnSurface(visibleTeamSurface(agent), fact, threadRef)
152	  }
153	}

      "content": "# Prompt Caching 优先的 Agent 工程设计原则\n\n从 Claude Code 的架构实践中提炼的 Agent 工程设计原则，以 prompt caching 为核心约束。\n\n## Prompt Cache 优先的设计\n\nPrompt caching 基于前缀匹配（prefix match），任何前缀层改变会 invalidate 之后所有缓存。**布局顺序决定一切**：静态内容优先，动态内容靠后。\n\n**标准四层结构**：① Static system prompt & Tools（全局缓存）→ ② Claude.MD（项目级）→ ③ Session context（会话级）→ ④ Conversation messages\n\n**常见破缓存原因**：在 static prompt 放详细时间戳、非确定性排列 tool 顺序、改 tool 参数。\n\n## 核心设计模式\n\n### 1. 用 Message 代替 System Prompt 更新\n更新时间/状态等动态信息时，通过 `<system-reminder>` tag 在下一轮 user message 或 tool result 中传递，不修改 system prompt。\n\n### 2. 模型切换用 subagent handoff，不直接切\nPrompt cache 是模型独有的。100k tokens 后切到小模型反而更贵（重建整个缓存）。正确做法：主模型（Opus）把任务整理成 handoff message 传给子模型（Haiku），子模型从干净上下文开始。[[Claude Code|Claude Code's]] Explore agents 即此模式。\n\n### 3. Plan Mode 作为 tool，不换工具集\n直观方案是切换工具集（只留只读），但会 invalidate 整个对话缓存。实际方案——所有工具始终在请求中，加 EnterPlanMode 和 ExitPlanMode 作为 tool。额外收益：模型可自主调用——当它发现问题复杂时自己进入 plan mode，全程不破缓存。\n\n### 4. Task-Specific Subagent 代替 Tool 膨胀\nClaude Code 约 20 个工具，加新工具门槛高。当需要新能力时（如回答「如何使用 Claude Code」），构建 subagent 而非加工具。这是 progressive disclosure 的另一种实现——在 action space 不变前提下扩展能力范围。\n\n### 5. Defer Load 代替 Remove\n大量 MCP tools 时，发 lightweight stub（名称 + defer_loading:true），模型通过 ToolSearch 按需发现完整 schema，缓存前缀始终稳定。\n\n### 6. 安全 Compaction\n复用父会话完全相同的 system prompt/tools/context，追加父会话 messages + compaction prompt 作为最后一条 user message。从 API 视角「几乎和上一次请求一样」，命中缓存前缀。\n\n### 7. AskUserQuestion 的三次迭代教训\n独立工具优于参数复用（职责清晰），结构化输出优于格式约定（稳定可靠）。最终标准不是设计多优雅，而是模型是否愿意且正确地调用它。\n\n### 8. Agent 自建上下文的三个进化阶段\n- **Phase 1 - RAG**：系统用向量数据库检索上下文喂给 agent。问题：需索引和 setup，跨环境脆弱\n- **Phase 2 - Grep Tool**：给 agent 搜索工具让它自己找文件。关键转变：从「喂上下文」到「给找上下文的工具」\n- **Phase 3 - Progressive Disclosure**：skill 文件可引用其他文件，agent 递归读取。模型越聪明，越应该给它找上下文的工具而不是替它找",

1	# .scratch Work Rules
2	
3	This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.
4	
5	## Work-item structure
6	
7	Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.
8	
9	```
10	active/<work>/
11	├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
12	├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
13	├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
14	│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
15	│   └── 02-<slug>.md
16	├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
17	└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
18	```
19	
20	## Ticket discipline
21	
22	Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):
23	
24	```markdown
25	# NN — title
26	
27	**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
28	**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
29	**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete
30	
31	- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
32	- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
33	```
34	
35	- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
36	- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
37	- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
38	- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).
39	
40	## Lifecycle
41	
42	- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
43	- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
44	- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.
45	
46	## Version control
47	
48	- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
49	- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.
50

52	
53	See [README.md](README.md).
