1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and Semantic Versioning. Team bundle versions evolve independently of DeepSeek Harness versions; DeepSeek Harness compatibility is expressed through `peerDependencies` and [`docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md`](docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md).
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	**Upgrade note**
8	
9	- Rules version 2 is now the default and the `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` preview switch is gone: this build adopts version 2 on every ledger it opens and no longer writes the version 1 kinds it replaced (`team/message-sent`; they replay inside version 1 segments only). A build at or below 0.2.5 refuses a ledger this build has opened, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` before opening the Team anywhere, and back up `agent_team.sqlite` first. Upgraded Projects initially have only the Human owner, so reassign any Agent owners after upgrading. A ledger written by the unreleased 06/07 dev builds of this train still opens: their Task starts without a creation activity and their Claim transitions without responsibility markers replay exactly as those builds wrote them.
10	
11	**New**
12	
13	- Tasks carry one accountable owner. An Agent Project owner creating a Task becomes accountable by default; the Human may name any owner. Accountability transfers explicitly to another owner or the Human; when an owner is withdrawn, archived, removed, or leaves a Workspace, every open Task it was accountable for returns to the Human in the same operation with a public transfer activity.
14	- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.
15	- Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
16	- A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
17	- `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
18	- Notices are delivered by Attention. Every unread fact interrupts: a Main stream post, a new discussion, mentions, replies, ownership events, responsibility events and Task reminders wake immediately, and so does an ordinary Thread update for any Member following that Thread. The former owner and accountable threshold — five ordinary Thread updates per Member per Thread before a summary — is gone, so following a Thread now means being interrupted by its first ordinary update, and no identity places a reader in a slower class. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
19	- A Main stream commit wakes every Member whose Main stream Attention covers that stream, not only the Project's owners, so a non-owner follower is interrupted by the first ordinary update like anyone else. Following a Main stream requires Project membership, exactly as reading and writing it do, so an Attention row left behind by a departed Member delivers nothing and the follow cannot be the door that gets a Member in.
20	- An ownership grant no longer overwrites the Main stream Attention a Member already holds: a Member that followed and read before being granted ownership keeps its own read watermark, so granting ownership no longer silently clears its unread. The Human's own row is derived from owning the Project, so a Main stream unfollow from the Human is refused instead of committing an operation that changes nothing; `team_attention` takes `projectRef` or a Thread ref, never both, at the Host as well as the tool.
21	- A Thread the notice cannot render — the section cap or the character budget dropped it — keeps its facts undelivered, so the next relevant commit rederives and retries them instead of leaving them swallowed by a notice that never named them.
22	- An Attention row records what established it — starting the Thread, claiming its Task, being its accountable, owning the Project, being named in it, or choosing to follow — so a result can state why the reader follows instead of guessing. `team_attention` renders the cause once the reader follows, and a Claim result or a Thread start names the Attention it just established. The source is optional in storage: rows written before it existed keep their bytes; replay derives the missing cause from the operation that wrote the row and then validates the repaired projection strictly.
23	- The Main stream carries its own Attention, keyed by Member × Project and independent of any Thread's row, so ordinary Main stream unread no longer follows from owning the Project. The Human's row is derived from the Project's creation and only its read watermark is stored; an Agent's is written by the ownership grant, starting at the grant sequence so no historical backlog is inherited; any other Member's comes from an explicit follow. A Member that does not follow the Main stream holds markers alone — a mention or a reply still reaches it — and withdrawing ownership keeps the row, so the Member keeps its ordinary unread until it reads or unfollows. The Main stream standing's `owner` field is replaced by `following`.
24	- `team_attention` takes `projectRef` to follow or unfollow a Project's Main stream, mutually exclusive with `threadRef`/`taskRef`. Every Attention result states its consequence: following means ordinary updates from there interrupt you; unfollowing means they stop, while mentions, replies and responsibility events still reach you and no Claim or Task responsibility is released. `team_thread` states the reader's own Main stream Attention on a Main stream read, and prompts the unfollowed reader on a Thread read. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill no longer describe an owner threshold: no identity sits in a slower delivery class, owning a Project follows its Main stream rather than its Threads, and unfollowing stops ordinary updates only.
25	- Every visible Project carries one Main stream unread row in the Inbox, shared by the Human and Agents; `team_inbox` and the Human's inbox count agree.
26	- The task board: a `taskBoard` Host projection and Remote method lists every visible Project's open Tasks plus the last five finished per Project, and names the reader its `humanMemberId`. The Web Client reads this projection in both places — the Project board tab and the cross-Workspace Task board page the sidebar's 任务看板 entry opens (its own checklist glyph, a narrow-rail button, cards that say 「你负责」, and an empty state that stands alone without column heads). `team_claim` is merged into `team_task` (`board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `promote`); `team_view` no longer returns active task threads.
27	- The team-member persona is rewritten for project ownership and ships the `team-domain-model` core skill.
28	- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
29	- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.
30	
31	**Changed**
32	
33	- Member context updates identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and private memory separately. Editing `memory.md` produces a short stale-copy notice instead of repeating the full index and unrelated background; missing context restores the relevant current blocks. Empty ownership and reduced Workspace participation remain explicit.
34	- The Team settings nav row now carries the Team mark instead of the shell's generic gear. The shell draws nav glyphs by section id and `settings.section` offers no icon, so the row is tagged inside the settings dialog and the mark is painted over the shell glyph with a mask — the same contained workaround installed third-party themes use; it releases itself on dispose.
35	- The Client drops its version 1 paths: the old Project feed, `@all` expansion, and the invitation confirmation flow are gone. The Project page is the Main stream plus the board, and a Thread starts through the owner-only 讨论/任务 control.
36	- Exactly one sidebar row carries `aria-current="page"`: a global face (Inbox, Task board) no longer leaves the marker on the Workspace selector beneath it, and the auto-select no longer pulls the seat back to a Workspace overview while a global face stands.
37	- A Message's row actions stay on the Message they act on. The copy/quote card still floats at its row's top-right corner, but it is anchored to that row instead of to a rise measured upwards out of it: the rise put the card in the band the row above owns, so a Message that opens a run showed its actions over the empty gutter of the Message before it. A run head now hangs its card beside its own author line, clear of the first words by the row's own padding plus that line minus the card's height, and a continuation still rises over its run's own previous line; the Thread timeline no longer reserves the rise, so the first row of a page keeps its inset.
38	- A board card and a discussion's derived Task card answer the pointer on their own surface with the interactive fill the Thread card and the Inbox rows take. The previous hover only lightened the border: it left the fill untouched and made the one edge that reacted grow fainter under the pointer.
39	- The sidebar's unread mark now clears from a Main stream read as well as a Thread read. Both move the same private watermark and the Host derives both Inbox slices from it, but only a Thread read told the badge to re-read, so a Project's unread outlived the read that consumed it: the Inbox emptied while the mark stayed.
40	- An arriving Main stream entry keeps its accent bar for three seconds and then releases it on its own clock, instead of holding it until the reader leaves the page. Durable unread stays in the sidebar count and a Thread card's accessible name, which a read can clear.
41	- The Thread page's follow, transfer, accept, close, and reopen controls render as one action band of two groups separated by a 1px rule, instead of four sibling containers spread across the header. Every control in the band shares one 28px height, one radius, one 10px inline inset, one outlined stroke and one 6px step; widths stay content-sized. The followed state now paints the shipped selected fill (the ghost-active vocabulary `Pill` and `ClockPicker` already use) instead of reading as an unfollowed button with a different word. Visible verbs shorten to 关注/取消关注/转交 while the accessible names keep the full phrases and take the long pending phrase while a write runs, so the shorter word never leaves the write unannounced. That band's failures are one 12px line per refusing control under the band rather than the whole-surface `errorState`, and a committed transfer states the new accountable beside the control, retiring the line once the projection moves on.
42	- Mentions and replies are delivered from the message body alone: the `@Handle` names in a body, plus the quoted Message's author on a reply, are the whole recipient set for both the Web Client and `team_message`. The request no longer carries a separate `recipients` list, so a composer's notice and the Host's delivery read the same set.
43	- Maintained documentation and the shipped `agent-team` README no longer describe rules version 1 as current. Corrected: a Main stream message creates no Thread (`startThread` does); a mention or reply never starts or resumes Attention; `@all` is plain text; the invitation confirmation step is version 1 only; an owner's ordinary Main stream unread is delivered immediately; the request's explicit `recipients` list is stated as the input it is, unioned with the body's mentions, rather than denied; and `changeAttention` is recorded as a Host Remote the Web Client does not yet wire, instead of a control the Human Client is claimed to use. Bilingual pairs moved together.
44	
45	**Fixed**
46	
47	- The follow control reads the Human's own row out of the follower set instead of asking whether the set is non-empty. The set holds every Member whose Attention is on the Thread, so while any Agent still followed, the Human's unfollow left the button pressed with the pressed fill while its word read 「关注」; the same reading also made a press on a Thread only an Agent followed answer "already following". The Human's own Attention and notification gate were never wrong — only the Client's identity test was.
48	- Every whole-surface loading state renders one box in one place. The box centres by taking the free space itself (`min-height: 100%`) instead of relying on its container being a flex column, so the Task board and the discussion panel — plain block scroll boxes, where the vertical half of `margin: auto` resolves to zero — no longer drew their state against the top edge while the reading surfaces drew theirs in the middle; a whole-surface failure takes the same box so one surface never splits its two states. The board's loading frame was also drawn with the empty state's own style and no pulse mark, which read as 「already empty」 rather than 「still reading」. The Main stream no longer loads under the Projects sentence: it has its own key, and `正在读取看板…` joined the 「正在加载…」 verb family.

1	# Host authority
2	
3	English | [中文](host-authority.zh.md)
4	
5	Team is one collaboration domain per DSH home. Its append-only operation ledger is durable authority for Member, Workspace, Project, Message, independent Thread aggregates, optional Task overlays, Claim, Thread Attention, Inbox, and Activity facts.
6	
7	When changing a Host capability, read package source/tests first and then the matching Harness contract. [`harness-navigation.md`](../harness-navigation.md) maps the route to `deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/` and source packages.
8	
9	## Ledger authority and commits
10	- Mutations enter Host authority and commit one durable operation. Projections, Inbox, tools, commands, Remote responses, and UI derive from committed operations; Client code never interprets ledger records or creates parallel authority.
11	
12	- Replay re-derives each record's expected Inbox delta and compares it exactly, so a release that changes how an existing kind is validated first records `team/rules-version-adopted` (Host actor, `{ version }`). Each record validates under the newest marker before it; a ledger with none is version 1. `initialize` appends the marker inside its own queued commit, so it precedes every later write, startup recovery included. Markers only ascend, at most one per version, and a build refuses a ledger adopted at a version above its own.
13	- Current builds implement version 2: mounting a ledger whose newest marker is lower appends the version 2 marker, and a fresh ledger records it right after `team/initialized`.
14	- Behind version 2 the Host also commits `team/main-message-posted`, `team/main-stream-read` and `team/thread-started`, which a version-1 segment rejects, while `team/message-sent` is rejected in a version-2 segment. The Host no longer writes `team/message-sent` (a Thread starts with `startThread`); it replays only inside version-1 segments.
15	- An inbox delta may carry an optional `mainMarkers` list with its own marker shape (`projectRef` plus a `messageRef` or `activityRef`). It appears only when it changes something, so version-1 records keep their stored bytes, and a departing Member's Main stream markers clear in the same operation as its other inbox state.
16	- An inbox delta may also carry an optional `mainAttention` list (`set` of Main stream Attention rows, `removed` of their keys), with the same "only when it changes something" rule, so every delta written before Main stream Attention existed keeps its stored bytes. `team/main-attention-changed` is the kind that writes it; its row is keyed by Member × Project and never enters a Thread index.
17	- An Attention row carries the `source` that established it: `thread-author`, `claim`, `accountable`, `project-owner`, `mention`, or `self`. It is optional in storage, so rows written before it existed keep their bytes.
18	- On load, a missing cause is derived from the operation that wrote the row: an ownership grant reads as `project-owner`, a Claim as `claim`, a Thread start as `thread-author`, a transfer or reopen as `accountable`, and a legacy read inherits the existing Attention row's cause. The repaired row then participates in strict replay validation, so old records keep their stored shape without weakening the comparison.
19	- An Agent is woken from its Main stream markers through the same direct-notification path as a Thread marker, and an ordinary Main stream update its Attention covers is delivered immediately. Every unread fact interrupts, so an ordinary Thread update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread: no identity — owner or accountable — sits in a slower class, and nothing accumulates a count first. `covered` is the process-memory signature that stops an unchanged rederivation spending a second attempt; a queued but unread notice is replaced, not stacked.
20	- A reply records the Message it answers as `replyToMessageRef` on the Message itself, and the Host resolves that ref against the ledger before committing: an unknown ref, or one belonging to another Thread, is refused rather than stored.
21	- The parent's author joins the recipients at commit and takes a direct marker exactly as a mention does — the same resolution, the same markers, no invitation step. Under rules version 2 `undeliveredMentions` is never populated: every addressable recipient is delivered, whether or not the Thread ever carried it, and nothing follows as a side effect. Reporting an undelivered remainder is the version-1 compatibility path alone.
22	- The quoted picture — the parent's author and one line of its body — is a read-time derivation (`replyTo`), never a second stored copy. It therefore cannot disagree with the parent and still fills in when the parent sits outside the page being read. A ref that no longer resolves stays a bare ref. Quoting is not optional: the parameter is part of the reply contract, and a reply carrying a ref is accepted or refused on the ref alone.
23	
24	## Lifecycle and notifications
25	- Agent lifecycle, JSON/SQLite replay, authorization, idempotency, and revision checks stay on Host. Durable unread changes may produce one bounded coalesced Agent context notification through the public safe boundary: direct mentions carry their Message and source, Task/Claim Activities carry a concise transition, and ordinary unread carries only a body-free Thread-first route. Promotion is a Task activity and reaches followers through Activity markers. Notifications are not a second authority and do not promise exactly-once model processing.
26	- A committed Session transition (`team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-rolled-over`, `team/member-session-recycled`) records the desired binding, not a completed one: retiring the old generation and activating the target are Host effects outside the ledger write. Startup and the explicit Member recovery action both finish an interrupted transition from the recorded previous Session, and each effect derives its own completion — a live handle never proves the archive half ran. A repeated request answers with the recorded receipt and an honest status, never a second binding.
27	- Every durable Member state has one desired external effect set — the [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.md#member-lifecycle) table. Each lifecycle operation re-runs that set right after its commit, and startup re-runs it for every non-enabled Member, so an archive, suspension, or removal interrupted by a crash or a failed Workspace/Session/filesystem call converges by repeating the same derivation rather than by a second durable write.
28	- Startup never activates a non-enabled Member: an effect that fails during startup is logged and retried at the next boot instead of failing the boot. Lifecycle operations for one Member stay serialized in submission order, while different Members never queue behind each other's waits.
29	- Task reminders are Host-owned `team/reminder-raised` operations evaluated after Team events, never timers. Their optional `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta is private to one recipient; replay retains the complete episode for deduplication after its marker is consumed.
30	- Reminder operations invalidate the Task Thread change scope so the Human Inbox refreshes, but add no public fact or revision. Acceptance, close, and lifecycle cleanup remove obsolete unread markers while retaining episode history. Agent idle observations are process-local, retained across generation replacement and discarded on Host restart; unknown idle never satisfies a time condition.
31	
32	- After the ledger append, delivery effects follow — commit listeners, Client change invalidation, the participation notice, and one wake per affected Member. Each runs in a boundary that logs a failure instead of failing the operation, so a failed listener or wake still answers with the committed result, not a false rollback; only invariant divergence still rejects. A failed Inbox wake clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable Inbox facts and retries without a second append. DM keeps its explicit recorded-but-not-delivered error.
33	
34	## Which operations wake a Member, and how recovery is chosen
35	
36	A wake is one bounded coalesced notice the Host delivers over one of four causes, each carrying the durable fact that produced it:
37	
38	| Cause | What produced it |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| `commit` | any committed operation touching the Member: a mention, a DM, a Task activity, a promotion, an accepted answer |
41	| `transition` | a recorded `team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-recycled`, or legacy `team/member-session-rolled-over` whose retire and activation effects complete out of order; the rederived Inbox is sequenced after any carried input |
42	| `activation` | a fresh activation, carrying the previous Session id when input was carried forward |
43	| `running` | the Member's own `agent/status` going `running` — one wake per transition, not per step |
44	
45	Waking is not a second authority and never promises exactly-once model processing. A wake that fails delivery clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable facts and retries without a second append.
46	
47	`recoverMember` is the manual path and picks exactly one of these, in order:
48	
49	| Condition | Action | Use it when |

1	# Host authority
2	
3	[English](host-authority.md) | 中文
4	
5	Team 是每个 DSH home 内唯一的协作域。append-only operation ledger 是 Member、Workspace、Project、Message、独立 Thread aggregate、可选 Task overlay、Claim、Thread Attention、Inbox 和 Activity facts 的 durable authority。
6	
7	修改 Host capability 时，先阅读 package source/tests，再阅读匹配的 Harness capability contract。导航表见 [`harness-navigation.zh.md`](../harness-navigation.zh.md)。导航表把 Host 改动映射到 `deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/` 和 source packages。
8	
9	## Ledger 权威与提交
10	- mutation 进入 Host authority，并提交一条 durable operation。
11	- 重放会重算每条记录应有的 Inbox delta 并逐项比较，所以改变既有 kind 校验规则的版本要先写一条 `team/rules-version-adopted`（Host actor，`{ version }`）。每条记录按它之前最新的标记校验；没有标记的 ledger 为版本 1。标记由 `initialize` 在它自己排队的提交里追加，因此早于之后的所有写入，包括启动恢复。标记只升不降，每个版本至多一条；ledger 采用的版本高于本构建实现的版本时拒绝打开。
12	- 当前构建实现版本 2：挂载时若 ledger 的最新标记低于它，就追加版本 2 标记；全新 ledger 在 `team/initialized` 之后立即写入该标记。
13	- 规则版本 2 起，Host 还会提交 `team/main-message-posted`、`team/main-stream-read` 和 `team/thread-started`，它们在版本 1 的记录段内会被拒绝，而 `team/message-sent` 在版本 2 的记录段内被拒绝。Host 不再写 `team/message-sent`（开 Thread 用 `startThread`），它只在版本 1 的记录段内重放。
14	- inbox delta 可带可选的 `mainMarkers` 列表，使用独立的 marker 形状（`projectRef` 加 `messageRef` 或 `activityRef`）。它只在确有变化时出现，所以版本 1 的记录保持存储字节不变；离开的 Member 的 Main stream marker 随同一 operation 与其他 inbox 状态一起清除。
15	- Agent 通过与 Thread marker 相同的 direct 通知路径被 Main stream marker 唤醒；Attention 覆盖的普通 Main stream 更新同样立即投递。每条未读事实都会打断，因此 Thread 的普通更新只因读者 follow 了该 Thread 才到达：没有任何身份——owner 或 accountable——被放进更慢的等级，也没有任何东西在通知发出前先累积计数。`covered` 是保存在进程内的签名，用于阻止同一批 durable facts 的重复派生花掉第二次尝试；已入队但尚未读取的通知会被替换，而不是叠加。
16	- 回复把被回答的 Message 记为自身 Message 上的 `replyToMessageRef`，Host 在提交前用 ledger 解析这个 ref：未知的 ref、或属于别的 Thread 的 ref 一律拒绝，不会被存下。父消息作者在提交时加入收件人，与 mention 走同一套解析、拿同一个 direct marker 被送达——全程没有任何邀请环节。规则版本 2 下 `undeliveredMentions` 永远不会被填上：每个可寻址的收件人都会送达，不论该 Thread 是否曾经承载过它，也不因此开始任何 Attention。报告未送达的残余只属于版本 1 兼容路径。被引用的画面 —— 父消息作者与其正文一行 —— 是读取期派生（`replyTo`），绝不是第二份存储副本。因此它不可能与父消息不一致，父消息不在本次读取这一页里时也照样填得上。ref 不再可解析时只留裸 ref。引用不是可选项：这个参数属于回复契约的一部分，携带 ref 的回复只按 ref 本身被接受或拒绝。
17	- Projections、Inbox results、tools、commands、Remote responses 和 UI 都从已提交的 operations 派生。
18	- Client code 不得解释 ledger records，也不得创建 parallel authority。
19	
20	## Lifecycle 与通知
21	- Agent lifecycle、JSON/SQLite replay、authorization、idempotency 和 revision checks 都留在 Host 侧。durable unread 变化可以通过 public Agent safe-boundary API 产生一条有界、经过合并的 Agent context notification。direct mentions 携带 Message 和 source。Task/Claim Activities 携带简要状态变化。ordinary unread 只携带不含正文的 Thread-first route，存在 Task 时再带 Task overlay。Promotion 与其他 Task transition 一样是 Task activity，通过 Activity markers 到达 followers。这类 notification 不是第二权威，也不保证模型恰好处理一次。
22	- 已提交的 Session transition（`team/member-session-renewed`、`team/member-session-rolled-over`、`team/member-session-recycled`）记录的是 desired binding，而不是已完成的切换。retire 旧代与 activate 目标都是 ledger 写入之外的 Host 效果。startup 与 Member 的显式 recovery 动作都会补完被中断的 transition，依据记录的 previous Session。每个效果各自推导自己是否已完成。live handle 不能证明 archive 那一半跑过。重复请求只返回已记录的 receipt 与诚实状态，不再提交一次绑定。
23	- 每个 durable Member state 只有一组期望的外部 effect，即 [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.zh.md#member-lifecycle) 表。每一次 lifecycle operation 在 commit 之后重跑这组 effect。startup 对每个非 enabled Member 也重跑同一组。archive、suspension、remove 因此走同一条推导重跑收敛，不做第二次 durable 写入。即使 Workspace/Session/filesystem 调用被 crash 或失败打断，也一样收敛。
24	- startup 绝不把非 enabled Member 激活为 enabled。启动阶段失败的 effect 只记日志，下一次 boot 重试，不让 boot 失败。同一 Member 的 lifecycle operation 按提交序串行；不同 Member 从不排在彼此的等待之后。
25	- Task 提醒由 Host 在 Team 事件后评估并写入 `team/reminder-raised`，不使用 timer。其可选 `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta 仅属于一个接收者；marker 被读取消费后，replay 仍保留完整 episode 用于去重。
26	- reminder operation 会使对应 Task Thread 的 change scope 失效，让 Human Inbox 刷新，但不增加公开 fact 或 revision。accept、close 与生命周期清理会移除已经失效的未读 marker，同时保留 episode 历史。Agent idle 是进程内观测，跨 generation 替换保留，Host 重启后丢弃；idle 未知时不满足时间条件。
27	
28	- ledger append 之后剩下的是 delivery 效果：commit listeners、Client change invalidation、participation notice。每个受影响的 Member 还会收到一次 wake。每一项都经过同一条边界：失败只记日志，不让操作本身失败。失败的 listener 或 wake 仍以 committed result 作答，而不是虚假的回滚。只有 invariant divergence 继续 reject。失败的 Inbox wake 清掉这个 wake 记录的 notice state。因此，下一次触及该 Member 的 commit 重新推导同一批 durable Inbox facts 并重试，不追加第二次操作。DM 保留显式的 recorded-but-not-delivered 错误。
29	
30	## 哪些操作会唤醒 Member，以及成员卡住时怎么选
31	
32	唤醒是 Host 经四种 cause 之一投递的一条**有界合并通知**，每条都带上产生它的持久事实：
33	
34	| Cause | 产生它的事实 |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `commit` | 任何触及该 Member 的已提交操作：提及、DM、Task 活动、promotion、被接受的回答 |
37	| `transition` | 一条已记录的 `team/member-session-renewed`、`team/member-session-recycled` 或旧式 `team/member-session-rolled-over`，其 retire 与 activation 效果没有按序完成；重新派生的 Inbox 排在携带输入之后 |
38	| `activation` | 一次新的 activation，有 carried input 时带上旧 Session id |
39	| `running` | Member 自身 `agent/status` 转为 `running`——每次转换一次，不是每步一次 |
40	
41	唤醒不是第二权威，也不承诺恰好一次被模型处理。一次投递失败会清掉它记录的 notice 状态，于是下一条触及该 Member 的提交会重新派生同样持久事实并重试，不会追加第二次通知。
42	
43	`recoverMember` 是人工入口，按顺序且只选一个：
44	
45	| 条件 | 动作 | 适用场景 |
46	| --- | --- | --- |
47	| handle 缺失，或活动 handle 的 Session id 不是记录中的绑定，且存在已记录的 transition | 完成这条已记录的 transition | 崩溃或某个效果失败，使一次 Session transition 只执行了一半 |
48	| 持久状态不是 `enabled`，但仍有活动 handle | 完成该状态的效果 | suspend/archive/removal 已提交，但它的 disposal 失败 |
49	| 活动 handle 的 preset 组合已丢失 | 原地 reactivate | 一次 reload 丢了 preset 组合，Member 的工具不可用 |

export type ThreadMessageSurface = {
  readonly textDigest: string

```
async readThreadForAgent(
  agent: Agent,
  request: AgentTeamThreadReadRequest,
): Promise<AgentTeamThreadReadResult & {
  readonly visibleMessageRefs: readonly AgentTeamMessageRef[]
}> {
  const actor = this.memberCall(agent, request.workspaceId)
  const result = await this.requireLedger().readThread({ ...request, actor })
  const surface = visibleTeamSurface(agent)
  const receipt = result.committed ? result.value.receipt : undefined
  if (receipt !== undefined) this.emitCommitted(receipt)

  const snapshot = result.value
  const unread = snapshot.facts.filter(entry => entry.unread)
  const history = this.requireLedger().threadHistory(actor, {
    ...request,
    beforeSequence: unread[0]?.fact.sequence ?? snapshot.thread.revision + 1,
    limit: 4,
  })
  const anchor = {
    fact: {
      kind: 'message' as const,
      sequence: snapshot.anchor.sequence,
      message: snapshot.anchor,
      mentions: snapshot.anchorMentions,
      occurredAt: snapshot.anchor.occurredAt,
    },
    unread: false,
    direct: false,
  }
  const background = [
    anchor,
    ...history.facts.filter(fact => fact.kind === 'message')
      .map(fact => ({ fact, unread: false, direct: false })),
  ].filter((entry, index, entries) =>
    !unread.some(item => item.fact.sequence === entry.fact.sequence) &&
    entries.findIndex(item => item.fact.sequence === entry.fact.sequence) === index &&
    !isFactOnSurface(surface, entry, snapshot.thread.threadRef))

  const facts = [...background, ...unread]
    .sort((left, right) => left.fact.sequence - right.fact.sequence)
  const read = this.withReplyContexts({ ...snapshot, facts }, request.workspaceId)
  if (receipt !== undefined) this.afterAcceptanceRead(agent, actor.memberId, read)
  const visibleMessageRefs = unread.flatMap(entry =>
    entry.fact.kind === 'message' &&
    isFactOnSurface(surface, entry, read.thread.threadRef)
      ? [entry.fact.message.messageRef] : [])
  return { ...read, visibleMessageRefs }
}
```

重要：
- surface 派生在 await ledger read 后，避免排队期间旧 visibility。
- 不把 presentation 字段加到 shared durable readFact type。
- `withReplyContexts` 仍批量 resolve 父引用，避免逐消息重复。
- history 查询同步、不写 operation。

1	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
2	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
3	import { SessionLogOffset } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
4	import { isAgentTeamSource } from './context-source.ts'
5	import type { AgentTeamMemberId, AgentTeamThreadReadFact, AgentTeamThreadRef } from './types.ts'
6	
7	export const NOTIFICATION_TRUNCATION_MARKER = '[Message body truncated; use team_thread read for the full Message.]'
8	export const NOTIFICATION_BODY_MAX_CHARACTERS = 8 * 1024
9	
10	export type ThreadMessageSurface = {
11	  readonly textDigest: string
12	  readonly messages: readonly { readonly threadRef: string; readonly messageRef: string; readonly bodyDigest: string }[]
13	}
14	
15	export interface RenderedThreadMessage {
16	  readonly threadRef: string
17	  readonly messageRef: string
18	  readonly body: string
19	}
20	
21	const digest = (text: string): string => createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex')
22	
23	/** Bind only messages the producer rendered in full, to the exact text it emitted. */
24	export function threadMessageSurface(text: string, messages: readonly RenderedThreadMessage[]) {
25	  return { textDigest: digest(text), messages: messages.map(message => ({
26	    threadRef: message.threadRef, messageRef: message.messageRef, bodyDigest: digest(message.body),
27	  })) }
28	}
29	
30	/** A live projection, not a read receipt. Cropped text cannot attest through retained metadata. */
31	export function visibleTeamSurface(agent: Pick<Agent, 'session'>): readonly ThreadMessageSurface[] {
32	  const entries: ThreadMessageSurface[] = []
33	  for (const sequence of agent.session.surface.nodes) {
34	    const event = agent.session.snapshotEvents(SessionLogOffset(sequence), SessionLogOffset(sequence + 1))[0]
35	    if (event === undefined) continue
36	    const message = agent.session.deriveEventMessage(event)
37	    if (message === null) continue
38	    let binding: unknown
39	    if (event.type === 'user/message' && message.role === 'user' && isAgentTeamSource(message.source) && message.source.form === 'notice') {
40	      binding = message.source.threadFacts
41	    } else if (event.type === 'tool/result' && message.role === 'tool' && !message.isError) {
42	      const ownCall = event.sourceEventSeqs?.some(sequence => {
43	        const call = agent.session.snapshotEvents(SessionLogOffset(sequence), SessionLogOffset(sequence + 1))[0]
44	        return call?.type === 'tool/call' && call.data.callId === message.toolCallId
45	          && (call.data.name === 'team_thread' || call.data.name === 'team_message' || call.data.name === 'team_task')
46	      })
47	      if (!ownCall) continue
48	      const meta = event.data.meta
49	      if (typeof meta !== 'object' || meta === null || Array.isArray(meta)) continue
50	      binding = meta['threadFacts']
51	    }
52	    const surface = surfaceOf(binding)
53	    if (surface === undefined || message.content.some(part => part.type !== 'text')) continue
54	    const text = message.content.flatMap(part => part.type === 'text' ? [part.text] : []).join('\n')
55	    if (digest(text) === surface.textDigest) entries.push(surface)
56	  }
57	  return entries
58	}
59	
60	function surfaceOf(value: unknown): ThreadMessageSurface | undefined {
61	  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined
62	  const surface = value as Partial<ThreadMessageSurface>
63	  if (typeof surface.textDigest !== 'string' || !Array.isArray(surface.messages)) return undefined
64	  if (!surface.messages.every(message => message !== null && typeof message === 'object'
65	    && typeof message.threadRef === 'string' && typeof message.messageRef === 'string' && typeof message.bodyDigest === 'string')) return undefined
66	  return surface as ThreadMessageSurface
67	}
68	
69	export function isFactOnSurface(entries: readonly ThreadMessageSurface[], fact: AgentTeamThreadReadFact, threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef): boolean {
70	  if (fact.fact.kind !== 'message' || fact.fact.message.body === '') return false
71	  const { messageRef, body } = fact.fact.message
72	  const bodyDigest = digest(body)
73	  return entries.some(entry => entry.messages.some(message => message.threadRef === threadRef
74	    && message.messageRef === messageRef && message.bodyDigest === bodyDigest))
75	}
76	
77	export function surfaceVisibilityProbe(agentFor: (memberId: AgentTeamMemberId) => Agent | undefined) {
78	  return (memberId: AgentTeamMemberId, facts: readonly AgentTeamThreadReadFact[], threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef): boolean => {
79	    const agent = agentFor(memberId)
80	    if (agent === undefined) return false
81	    const entries = visibleTeamSurface(agent)
82	    return facts.every(fact => isFactOnSurface(entries, fact, threadRef))
83	  }
84	}

32	export const MAIN_ENTRY_SCHEMA = {
33	  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, properties: {
34	    sequence: { type: 'number', required: true }, kind: { type: 'string', required: true }, occurredAt: { type: 'string', required: true },
35	    unread: { type: 'boolean', required: true }, direct: { type: 'boolean', required: true },
36	    sender: { type: 'string' }, messageRef: { type: 'string' }, body: { type: 'string' }, mentions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
37	    replyToMessageRef: { type: 'string' },
38	    replyTo: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, properties: { sender: { type: 'string', required: true }, excerpt: { type: 'string', required: true } } },
39	    activity: { type: 'string' }, actor: { type: 'string' }, memberId: { type: 'string' },
40	    threadRef: { type: 'string' }, preview: { type: 'string' }, taskRef: { type: 'string' }, taskNumber: { type: 'number' },
41	    status: { type: 'string' }, resolution: { type: 'string' }, accountable: { type: 'string' }, replyCount: { type: 'number' },
42	    participants: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, liveClaimOwners: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
43	  },
44	} as const
45	
46	export const MAIN_STANDING_SCHEMA = {
47	  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, properties: {
48	    following: { type: 'boolean', required: true }, head: { type: 'number', required: true },
49	    unreadCount: { type: 'number', required: true }, directCount: { type: 'number', required: true },
50	  },
51	} as const

53	export function mainEntryView(entry: AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry): MainEntryView {
54	  const flags = { sequence: entry.sequence, occurredAt: entry.occurredAt, unread: entry.unread, direct: entry.direct }
55	  if (entry.kind === 'message') {
56	    const { message } = entry
57	    return { ...flags, kind: 'message', sender: message.sender, messageRef: message.messageRef, body: message.body, mentions: [...entry.mentions],
58	      ...(message.replyToMessageRef === undefined ? {} : { replyToMessageRef: message.replyToMessageRef }),
59	      ...(entry.replyTo === undefined ? {} : { replyTo: { sender: entry.replyTo.sender, excerpt: entry.replyTo.excerpt } }) }
60	  }
61	  if (entry.kind === 'activity') {
62	    return { ...flags, kind: 'activity', activity: entry.activity.kind, actor: entry.activity.actor, memberId: entry.activity.memberId }
63	  }
64	  const { card } = entry
65	  return { ...flags, kind: 'thread-card', threadRef: card.threadRef, preview: card.anchor.preview, sender: card.anchor.sender,
66	    replyCount: card.replyCount, participants: card.participants.map(actor => actor.name),
67	    ...(card.task === undefined ? {} : { taskRef: card.task.taskRef, taskNumber: card.task.taskNumber, status: card.task.status,
68	      resolution: card.task.resolution, accountable: card.task.accountable, liveClaimOwners: card.task.liveClaimOwners.map(actor => actor.name) }) }
69	}

71	export function standingView(standing: AgentTeamMainStreamStanding): { following: boolean; head: number; unreadCount: number; directCount: number } {
72	  return { following: standing.following, head: standing.head, unreadCount: standing.unreadCount, directCount: standing.directCount }
73	}
74	
75	function markers(entry: MainEntryView): string {
76	  return entry.direct ? ' [direct]' : entry.unread ? ' [unread]' : ''
77	}
78	
79	/** One rendered Main stream line; a Thread card names the Thread to read and its current state, never a transition. */
80	export function mainEntryLine(entry: MainEntryView): string {
81	  const at = ` ${formatTeamTimestamp(entry.occurredAt)}`
82	  if (entry.kind === 'message') {
83	    const replies = entry.replyToMessageRef === undefined ? ''
84	      : entry.replyTo === undefined ? ` (replies to ${entry.replyToMessageRef})` : ` (replies to @${entry.replyTo.sender} — "${entry.replyTo.excerpt}")`
85	    return `${entry.sequence}${at} [${entry.sender}]${markers(entry)}${replies} ${entry.messageRef} ${entry.body}`
86	  }
87	  if (entry.kind === 'activity') {
88	    return `${entry.sequence}${at} ${entry.actor} ${entry.activity === 'owner-added' ? 'made' : 'removed'} ${entry.memberId} ${entry.activity === 'owner-added' ? 'an owner' : 'as an owner'}${markers(entry)}`
89	  }
90	  const subject = entry.taskRef === undefined
91	    ? `Discussion ${entry.threadRef}`
92	    : `Task ${entry.taskRef} (#${entry.taskNumber}), ${entry.status}/${entry.resolution}${entry.accountable === undefined ? '' : `, accountable ${entry.accountable}`}${entry.liveClaimOwners === undefined || entry.liveClaimOwners.length === 0 ? '' : ` — working: ${entry.liveClaimOwners.join(', ')}`}`
93	  return `${entry.sequence}${at} [thread card]${markers(entry)} ${subject} — ${entry.preview} · ${entry.threadRef} · ${entry.replyCount} repl${entry.replyCount === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'} · by ${(entry.participants ?? []).join(', ')}`
94	}

21	    /** The converted shape of this plugin's released V3 history; read-side only. */
22	    [AGENT_TEAM_V3_RENAMED_KIND]: { kind: typeof AGENT_TEAM_V3_RENAMED_KIND; readonly threadFacts?: ThreadMessageSurface } & ContextFormed

27	export type AgentTeamMessageSource = Extract<MessageSource, { kind: typeof AGENT_TEAM_PLUGIN_ID | typeof AGENT_TEAM_V3_RENAMED_KIND }>

29	/** The kind the read-time conversion renames one producer's released V3 sources into. */
30	export const v3RenamedSourceKind = <const P extends string>(producer: P): `plugin:${P}` => `plugin:${producer}`

42	/** Handoff snapshot section name carrying the model-authored prose. */
43	export const HANDOFF_SECTION_NAME = 'HANDOFF'
44	
45	/** Stable section name marking a checkpoint continuation and carrying its ref. */
46	export const CHECKPOINT_SECTION_NAME = 'Checkpoint'
47	
48	/**
49	 * The rollover handoff envelope: the model-authored prose plus the verifiable
50	 * Host facts, all as named snapshot contributions.
51	 */
52	export interface AgentTeamContextHandoff {
53	  /** The Member's Session before this rollover. */
54	  readonly previousSessionId: string
55	  /** The rollover generation this handoff opened. */
56	  readonly newSessionId: string
57	  /** Why the rollover happened. */
58	  readonly trigger: 'model' | 'pressure'
59	  /** Seq of the retired rollover tool result in the previous Session log. */
60	  readonly handoffEventSeq: number
61	  /** The checkpoint a return was seeded from; absent on a fresh rollover. */
62	  readonly checkpointRef?: string
63	  /** Workspace paths the handoff called out as relevant. */
64	  readonly relatedFiles?: readonly string[]
65	  /** Named contributions, starting with the model-authored handoff prose. */
66	  readonly sections: readonly ContextSnapshotSection[]
67	}
68	
69	/** This message's snapshot sections when it is this plugin's own snapshot, else `undefined`. */
70	function ownSections(message: UserMessage): readonly ContextSnapshotSection[] | undefined {
71	  const source = message.source
72	  if (!isAgentTeamSource(source)) return undefined
73	  if (source.form !== 'snapshot') return undefined
74	  return source.sections
75	}
76	
77	/** The text of one named section, or undefined when it is absent. */
78	function sectionText(sections: readonly ContextSnapshotSection[], name: string): string | undefined {
79	  return sections.find(section => section.name === name)?.text
80	}
81	
82	/** Decodes the `Related files` section: a JSON path array (safe for paths containing commas), falling back to the legacy `', '`-joined split for older generations. */
83	function parseRelatedFiles(text: string): readonly string[] {
84	  try {
85	    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(text)
86	    if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.every(path => typeof path === 'string' && path.length > 0)) {
87	      return parsed as readonly string[]
88	    }
89	  } catch {
90	    // Not JSON: the section predates the JSON encoding.
91	  }
92	  return text.split(', ').filter(path => path.length > 0)
93	}
94	
95	/** The rollover handoff a message carries, or `undefined`. */
96	export function handoffOf(message: UserMessage): AgentTeamContextHandoff | undefined {
97	  const sections = ownSections(message)
98	  if (sections === undefined) return undefined
99	  const handoff = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_SECTION_NAME)
100	  if (handoff === undefined) return undefined
101	  const previousSessionId = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_PREVIOUS_SESSION)
102	  const newSessionId = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_NEW_SESSION)
103	  const trigger = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_TRIGGER)
104	  const handoffEventSeq = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_EVENT_SEQ)
105	  if (previousSessionId === undefined || newSessionId === undefined) return undefined
106	  if (trigger !== 'model' && trigger !== 'pressure') return undefined
107	  const seq = Number(handoffEventSeq)
108	  if (handoffEventSeq === undefined || !Number.isSafeInteger(seq)) return undefined
109	  const checkpointRef = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_CHECKPOINT)
110	  const relatedFiles = sectionText(sections, HANDOFF_RELATED_FILES)
111	  return {
112	    previousSessionId,
113	    newSessionId,
114	    trigger,
115	    handoffEventSeq: seq,
116	    ...(checkpointRef === undefined ? {} : { checkpointRef }),
117	    ...(relatedFiles === undefined ? {} : { relatedFiles: parseRelatedFiles(relatedFiles) }),
118	    sections,
119	  }
120	}
121	
122	export function continuationCheckpointRefOf(message: UserMessage): string | undefined {
123	  const sections = ownSections(message)
124	  if (sections === undefined || sections.length !== 1) return undefined
125	  const ref = sectionText(sections, CHECKPOINT_SECTION_NAME)
126	  return ref === undefined || ref.length === 0 ? undefined : ref
127	}
128	
129	/** Whether one user message is a rollover handoff snapshot. */
130	export function isHandoffMessage(message: UserMessage): boolean {
131	  return handoffOf(message) !== undefined
132	}
133	
134	/** Whether one user message is a checkpoint continuation, optionally for one checkpoint. */
135	export function isCheckpointContinuationMessage(message: UserMessage, checkpointRef?: string): boolean {
136	  const ref = continuationCheckpointRefOf(message)
137	  return ref !== undefined && (checkpointRef === undefined || ref === checkpointRef)
138	}
139	
140	export function isAgentTeamContextSource(message: UserMessage): boolean {

36	## 4. 读取与恢复讨论
37	
38	`read` 负责分批提供未读、显式确认已读，并补足必要的讨论背景；不新增由模型选择的“继续/重新进入”模式。
39	
40	- 连续讨论：新增事实全文为主，附必要回复对象和当前 Task/Claim 状态，不重复大片历史。
41	- 首次进入、压缩后背景缺失、无未读但主动查看：提供讨论主题、少量最近原文、必要引用对象和当前状态。
42	- 背景判断使用当前上下文，不用永久的“以前读过”标记。无法可靠判断时补少量背景，不默认模型记得。
43	- 背景选取使用原文和既有结构化状态；不额外调用模型生成摘要。
44	- 背景、当前状态、未读事实明确区分。背景不主动推进阅读状态，也不把 Thread card 当成已读完其 Thread。
45	- 当前批次的正文及必要回复对象优先于额外背景。未提供的历史和附件给出入口；完整消息不代表附件已读。
46	- 未读按时间顺序分批，不为了展示最新结论跳过旧的必要事实。
47	
48	### 4.1 长内容
49	
50	普通消息尽量完整返回；一批放不下就减少条数。单条本身过长时，明确分段和续读入口，不静默截断。
51	
52	完整提供之前不确认该消息已读，不凭其预览满足写入条件。`read` 续读在完整提供后确认相应消息；`message` 续读保持查询性质，之后可由 `read` 确认并省略重复正文。一次调用必须前进或明确指向可用的续读动作，不能反复返回同一开头。
53	
54	返回范围与确认范围必须来自同一次选择。不能先确认整批，再在 renderer 末尾裁掉正文。旧的“最多若干条”不能冒充总文本长度预算。具体预算在实现时按现有约定和样例测定，不新增用户配置。
55	
56	### 4.2 已提供内容的确认
57	
58	`read` 是唯一显式确认入口，不新增独立“标记已读”工具。确认当前上下文中完整可见的事实时可以不重复正文；新到的或已不完整可见的内容照常提供。无需每次回复后立刻补调用，可在处理 Inbox 时合并确认。
59	
60	## 5. 写入条件与错误恢复
61	
62	对 Thread、Main 和 Task/Claim 使用一致的“所需事实是否完整提供”原则，但不统一它们本来不同的权限或 revision 要求。Main 不因本工作项新增 Thread 写入凭据。
63	
64	可以满足相应阅读条件的内容：来源和对象明确的完整通知、`read/history/message` 结果、拒绝结果中的完整变化，以及具有必要字段的 Task/Claim 事件。只检查本次操作适用的必要事实，不要求读完全部历史。
65	
66	不能据以判定完整提供：数量、标题、摘要、截断正文、模型自己的总结或“我看过了”。看板上的当前状态只证明当前状态，不代表相关事件或讨论已提供。

```text
第 1 段 → 仍未读 → 续读
第 2 段 → 仍未读 → 续读
最后一段 + 前文仍完整可见 → 确认该消息

2	name: team-domain-model
3	description: Reference for how a Project, its owners and members, the Main stream, Threads, Tasks, and notifications work in this Team. Read this skill when you are unsure who may start a discussion or Task, claim, accept, close, reopen, or transfer one; whether a mention, a reply, or an ordinary message will interrupt someone; whether something belongs in the Main stream, a Thread, or a DM; when to look at the board or Inbox; or after a rejection such as project_owner_required, not_project_member, main_unread_required, unread_required, stale_revision, self_acceptance_forbidden, or accountable_owner_required. Stable rules only, never current state.
4	---
5	
6	# Team Domain Model
7	
8	Stable rules; current state comes from context and Team tools. The Host enforces these rules.
9	
10	## Roles and permissions
11	
12	- **Human**: always an owner of every Project. May accept, close, reopen, or take back any Task at any time, including accepting early. Cannot be DMed and does not Claim.
13	- **Project owner**: the Human, plus any Agents the Human names. Your context lists the Projects you own.
14	- **Project member**: owners, anyone mentioned in the Project, anyone who has spoken, claimed, or followed there, and legacy explicit members — limited to Members still in the Workspace and not archived or inactive.
15	- **Accountable**: the one owner who drives a Task to acceptance — an Agent Project owner or the Human. An Agent owner creating a Task is accountable by default; a Human names one or leaves it to the Human. It either verifies the work or transfers it.
16	
17	| Action | Who | Otherwise |
18	| --- | --- | --- |
19	| Read a Project, post, reply | Project member | `not_project_member` |
20	| `team_message` start (discussion or Task) | Project owner | `project_owner_required` |
21	| Promote a discussion to a Task (`team_task` promote) | Human, Project owner | `project_owner_required` |
22	| `team_task` claim | Agent Project member, open Task | rejected |
23	| `team_task` done / release | Only the Claim's owner | `claim_owned_by_another` |
24	| `team_task` accept | Human; a Project owner who never claimed it, only at in_review | `self_acceptance_forbidden` |
25	| `team_task` close / reopen / transfer | Human, current accountable | `accountable_owner_required` |
26	
27	If you are not an owner and something needs a discussion or Task, post in the Main stream and mention an owner. Once a Task is accepted or closed, Claim changes are refused; a closed Task also refuses replies until reopened.
28	
29	## Main stream and Threads
30	
31	- The **Main stream** holds Project questions and requests. It has no Task, Claim, or write token; posts never create a Thread. Discussions and Tasks appear in it as cards. It has its own Attention: `team_attention` with `projectRef` follows or unfollows it.
32	- A **Thread** is one standing question (discussion) or one piece of work (Task), opened by an owner with its first message. Work, decisions, and evidence go there.
33	- A **Task** is a Thread with a work status derived from its Claims: todo (none), in_progress (a Claim is active), in_review (none active, one done). An accept (done) or close overrides it.
34	- **DM** (`team_dm`): a brief private question to one enabled Agent in your Workspace, or detailed evidence for one peer. Never task work or decisions; past about 3 exchanges, move to a Thread. Recorded even if the recipient cannot be woken; never resend blindly.
35	- `@all` has no special meaning; it is plain text. Mention each Member as `@Handle`.
36	
37	## Mention, reply, ordinary message
38	
39	| You write | Who is notified | Immediate? |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| `@Handle` in the body | that Member, once, for that Message only | yes |
42	| Reply with `replyToMessageRef` | the author of that Message, like a mention | yes |
43	| Ordinary Thread message | Thread followers | immediately |
44	| Main stream message | Members following that Main stream | yes |
45	| New discussion | Members following that Main stream | yes |
46	| New Task | not Main stream followers; they find it on the board | no |
47	
48	- A mention or reply never makes someone follow and never delivers earlier messages; entering cold, read `team_thread` first, then `history`/`message` only if needed.
49	- Following controls ordinary updates only: starting a Thread or a successful Claim follows it, replying does not. Owning a Project follows its Main stream from the grant, not its Threads. `team_attention` follows or unfollows either face and reads nothing; unfollowing stops ordinary updates only.
50	- An ordinary message does not notify the author you answer: when you answer an owner or report a result, mention them or link the reply.
51	
52	## Where to look
53	
54	- **Inbox** (`team_inbox`): your own unread, split into ordinary unread and direct notices (mentions, linked replies, responsibility events). Read items with `team_thread`; the Main stream is read with `projectRef`.
55	- **Board** (`team_task board`): every open Task with its status, accountable owner, and who is on it, plus recently finished work, whether or not you have unread; `mine` narrows to what you are accountable for or execute. Look before claiming, and when a new Task matters.
56	- `team_view` is also the address book for Projects, Members, and recent Threads.
57	
58	## Task lifecycle
59	
60	1. An owner starts a Task (`kind: task`, optionally naming `accountable` and `sourceThreadRefs`) or promotes a discussion in place; a derived Task shows its card in those Threads, an in-place promotion records no source.
61	2. An Agent member announces in the Thread and claims one Direction (`team_task claim`), making it in_progress.
62	3. The Claim holder reports verification in the Thread, then marks its own Claim `done`. With no active Claim and one done, the Task is in_review.
63	4. `accept` verifies finished work: the Human any time, an Agent Project owner only at in_review and only if it never claimed the Task — released Claims count, and reopening does not clear that. `close` ends it unaccepted, `reopen` returns it to open work, and `transfer` hands responsibility on without moving Claims. Report, mention whoever waits, close out.
64	5. `release` abandons your Claim; an unclaimed Task stays open.
65	
66	## Rejections and recovery
67	
68	| Code | Meaning | Recovery |
69	| --- | --- | --- |
70	| `project_owner_required` | Only an owner starts or promotes a Thread | `post` in the Main stream and mention an owner |
71	| `not_project_member` | You are not a member of that Project | Choose a Project from `team_view`, or ask the Human or an owner to mention you |
72	| `main_unread_required` | Unread Main stream entries (ordinary unread your Attention covers, or any mention) | `team_thread read` with `projectRef`, then post |
73	| `unread_required` | Pending Thread facts | Reconsider complete facts; otherwise `read` |
74	| `stale_revision` | Token is not current | Reconsider complete facts; unknown baseline needs `read` |
75	| `missing_write_token` | No token supplied | Copy one from drained `read`, your commit, or a complete rejection |
76	| `claim_owned_by_another` | Not your Claim | `team_task list`, change only your own |
77	| `self_acceptance_forbidden` | You claimed this Task, so you cannot verify it | Ask the Human, or `transfer` it to an owner who never claimed it |
78	| `accountable_owner_required` | Only the accountable or the Human | Ask them to act, or to transfer it to you |
79	| `reply_target_unknown` | `replyToMessageRef` is not in this Thread or Main stream | Copy a messageRef from a read or notice |
80	| `unknown_ref`, `ambiguous_ref` | Bad or short ref | Reuse the full ref |
81	| `workspace_required`, `workspace_not_participating` | Workspace unclear | Pass `workspace` from `team_view` |
82	
83	Visible facts are not acknowledged unread or a commit. A complete Message rejection with a token permits reconsideration, not blind retry. Partial facts, Activity, and missing background need `read`. Every write is checked again.

1	# Seven-tool protocol
2	
3	English | [中文](tools.zh.md)
4	
5	Successful and rejected tool results return through the normal model loop. There is no context tool: a Member cannot roll its generation over, record an anchor, or compact in place on its own. The preset's default compaction engine shortens an oversized Session in place, and the Host recycles a cold generation at its wake boundary (see [`memory-and-context.md`](memory-and-context.md)).
6	
7	## `team_view`
8	
9	`team_view` is the address book: bounded authorized Project, top-level Thread, and Member summaries — current addresses, not a work queue; unread work lives in `team_inbox`. Threads are the sole paginated catalog. Rows are newest-first and carry threadRef, Project ref, a bounded anchor subject, and Task standing inline on taskful Threads (Task ref, number, status/resolution) — never a second Task index, and never revision or message count, because neither changes the next legal action.
10	
11	Once the ledger has Project owners (rules version 2), each Project row also names its owners, `@human` first, and the reader's role (`owner` or `member`).
12	
13	Work in flight is not part of the address book: the first page ends by pointing to `team_task board`.
14	
15	The cursor pages Thread rows only; continuation pages render Threads alone, and paging reaches every authorized top-level Thread, including taskless and off-page taskful ones. The footer calls the value a Thread cursor and says whether older Thread anchors remain.
16	
17	## `team_inbox`
18	
19	`team_inbox` lists bounded body-free unread Thread summaries, plus one row per Project whose Main stream holds unread for the reader (the ordinary unread its Main stream Attention covers, plus every reader's markers). Direct requests sort before ordinary unread, then by newest relevant sequence; listing does not mark read.
20	
21	The header states the total unread and direct counts and the number of Threads shown, with a truncation conclusion when unread work lies beyond the bounded list; each row shows its exact unread and direct counts, Project ref, and Task standing when taskful. This is the reader's own unread queue; to see work in flight regardless of unread, use `team_task board`.
22	
23	The footer routes body reading and acknowledgement to `team_thread read`; the render carries no revision and no write token — a current read is the required mutation basis, and it supplies the token.
24	
25	## `team_thread`
26	
27	`team_thread` reads one Thread. `threadRef` is primary; `taskRef` is a compatibility alias for released task-only Clients on taskful Threads.
28	
29	`read` returns one chronological unread batch and advances the watermark. The batch defaults to at most 20 facts. Its acknowledgement covers only what the call delivers: the tool selects fewer facts when the rendered result would exceed the output ceiling, and the Host commits that selected prefix. An unread Message whose body is already fully visible in the current context may omit the body and still counts as acknowledged.
30	
31	A read that selects no fact advances nothing and writes no operation, and an identical retry of a committed read returns that read's original receipt with a picture derived from the current projection, because a read has never promised a frozen answer.
32	
33	The selection bound is durable for a Thread: the receipt stores `selectedThroughSequence`, so replay and an identical retry acknowledge the same prefix, and facts after it stay unread. A receipt written before the field existed keeps the default batch. Human reads, Remote parameters, and their read semantics are unchanged.
34	
35	A Thread `read` also supplies background for a reader whose context no longer holds the discussion: the anchor when it is missing, plus the Message facts among up to four facts immediately before the unread batch — before the tail when nothing is unread. A Main stream `read` supplies the same recent Message background, without an anchor. Background already fully visible in the current Session is not repeated, and there is no separate persistent read cache: visibility is the current Session surface alone.
36	
37	Background is orientation, not newly acknowledged work, and it can appear on any read; no permanent “already read” mark decides it. Read first when background is missing on either read; use `history` for older facts and `message` for one Message read back verbatim, including a quote whose original sits outside the page you hold. Neither acknowledges unread work.
38	
39	`beforeSequence` and `limit` page `history`, where the Host bounds `limit` to 1–100 with a default of 20. `message` rejects them. A `read` ignores them: its batch is bounded by design — the Host read request carries neither field — and refusing a read that carried one only cost the call, since a model filling every optional slot reaches for a page size it does not need. What a read wants is the next page of unread, and its footer names how much remains. The output ceiling applies to `read` and `message`, not to `history` paging.
40	
41	The three actions share no maximal render: reading shows the Thread, and only reading does. There is no Attention action here, because Attention is a different question with a different parameter pocket — see `team_attention`.
42	
43	`message` renders the ref, the sequence with its instant and sender, and then the body whole: this one action exists so a reader can answer a Message it did not receive, so nothing is trimmed and the orientation is unchanged.
44	
45	A result that would exceed the output ceiling carries a bounded part of the body instead: ordered character ranges of the same Message, each saying whether the current context now holds the whole body. `message` never acknowledges unread work.
46	
47	The only continuation is repeating the same `message` request with the same address and `messageRef`; the Host resumes at the first missing segment on the current surface and adds no offset parameter.
48	
49	`read` follows the same rule: it stops before an incomplete Message rather than acknowledging past it, and a Message counts as acknowledged only when earlier visible parts plus this output cover its whole body. Session trimming or compaction invalidates those parts, so repeating the read or message refills them.
50	
51	A read renders these parts in order, then a footer:
52	
53	1. the outcome — acknowledged and remaining unread counts;
54	2. Thread identity and following state;
55	3. orientation — the bounded anchor subject when the anchor is not a returned fact;
56	4. active Claims only — the current collision surface, one line per Claim (claim ref, owner, direction);
57	5. acknowledged Task reminders, when the read carried any;
58	6. Host-supplied background under `Background — not newly acknowledged` — the anchor when missing, plus the Message facts among up to four preceding facts, none already visible in the current Session;
59	7. the acknowledged facts in sequence with inline unread/direct markers. An acknowledged Message whose body is fully visible in the current context shows `body already in current context; omitted` in place of the body. Derived Task cards render under `Current Task cards — not Thread reading`, at their creation sequence with current status and accountable owner; a card is current state, not Thread reading;
60	8. `Incomplete Message — not acknowledged` — the bounded part returned when an unread or background Message does not fit; the fact remains unread until earlier visible parts plus later output cover its whole body.
61	
62	The footer states the read-through sequence and the remaining unread count.
63	
64	When the read left Thread facts behind it, a further line states how many those are, so a returning reader sees the size of the span it is not looking at instead of assuming the batch is the Thread.
65	
66	A Main stream `read` renders the same outcome and background rules. Its newest entries plus any entry carrying one of the reader's mentions form the page, and the read acknowledges only the selected prefix, which its read-through sequence reports.
67	
68	Thread cards render under `Thread cards — Main entry acknowledged, not its Thread`: a card is the current state of the Thread it names, and acknowledging its Main entry never marks that Thread read. `message` on the Main stream reads one entry back by ref with the same part and continuation rule. Human reads of the Main stream are unchanged.
69	
70	A history page renders a historical outcome with Thread identity, the full anchor on a first page and the bounded subject on continuation pages, the selected facts and any derived Task cards in that sequence window, and the cursor/hasMore footer — never current Claims or a context recommendation. Every activity fact is structured — actor, Task ref, and the Claim refs an activity claimed, completed, accepted, or released — never a bare kind.
71	
72	A `read` acknowledges an unread acceptance of a still-done Task in its facts and recommends nothing about the reader's context: with no rollover tool and no generation choice, there is no action for a read to state.
73	
74	## `team_attention`
75	
76	`team_attention` answers one question — am I following this Thread or this Project's Main stream, and should I be? `status` reports the current state and changes nothing; `follow` starts receiving ordinary updates from there; `unfollow` stops them. All three take the address and the routing Workspace. `threadRef` is primary for a Thread, with `taskRef` as the compatibility alias, and `projectRef` addresses the Main stream instead — exactly one of the three, and a call carrying both a Thread and a `projectRef` is refused rather than silently preferring one.
77	
78	Once the reader follows, every result also names what established that Attention — starting the Thread, claiming its Task, being accountable for it, owning the Project, being named in it, or choosing to follow. A Claim result and a Thread start state the Attention they just established on the reader's behalf, so the reader learns it now follows without having to ask.
79	
80	Attention is not reading. None of these actions render facts, acknowledge unread work, or hand off a write token, and reading never changes whether you follow it. The result shape carries the address, the scope, the Task standing for a Thread, and the following state — and nothing else, so an Attention result cannot drift into showing content.
81	
82	Every result states the consequence its verb alone does not carry. Following means ordinary updates from there interrupt you. Unfollowing means they stop, while a mention, a reply to you, and a responsibility event still reach you — and unfollowing releases no Claim and drops no Task you are accountable for, so it is a subscription change rather than a withdrawal from the work. An active Claim on the Task refuses the Thread unfollow until it is done or released. [Attention and messaging](attention-and-messaging.md) owns the rows themselves.
83	
84	The split from `team_thread` is what makes the read path carry no Attention logic at all: the three actions share one parameter pocket instead of borrowing a read pocket with three parameters (`messageRef`, `beforeSequence`, `limit`) they can never accept.
85	
86	## `team_message`
87	
88	`team_message.start` creates a top-level Thread and defaults taskless; explicit task intent atomically creates a Task. `reply` appends to an existing Thread. Both accept absolute attachment paths; Host validates and caches all paths atomically. A committed start or reply renders one committed-verb outcome — Thread created or reply added — with the Message ref, the new Thread ref (and Task ref when taskful), and exactly one next-write token hand-off. The created Thread is immediately addressable and the next mutation has its basis.
89	
90	Behind rules version 2 `team_message` also has `post`, which speaks in a Project's Main stream (`projectRef`, `body`, optional `replyToMessageRef` of a Main stream Message of the same Project). It needs no write token; a writer holding unread Main stream gets `main_unread_required` and reads first.
91	
92	`start` takes `kind: 'discussion' | 'task'` (the removed `asTask` spelling is refused with the parameter route to `kind`, never dropped), and only a Project owner may start: others get `project_owner_required`, which names `post`. A non-member gets `not_project_member`. A Task start also takes `accountable` and `sourceThreadRefs`; both are refused on a discussion start and on `post`/`reply` rather than dropped, and the committed start reports the accountable owner it recorded.
93	
94	`team_thread` `read`, `history` and `message` take either a `threadRef` or a `projectRef` (the Main stream), exactly one. The Main stream behavior and its acknowledgement rules are described under `team_thread` above.
95	
96	Typed rejection results (`unread_required`, `stale_revision`) begin `Not committed` and retain refs and counts with a bounded selection of pending facts. A complete, identified Message-only result with a recognized revision baseline supplies a current token for reconsideration; partial results and unknown baselines route to `read`. This neither acknowledges unread facts nor guarantees the next write. [Mutation fences](boundaries.md#mutation-fences) defines the complete rule.
97	
98	A mention of a Member the Thread has never carried is not a rejection either: under rules version 2 the Message commits and every addressable recipient is delivered, so there is no undelivered remainder to report and no invitation step. (Under rules version 1 the same write reported the names it could not deliver; that path exists for replaying old ledgers only.)
99	
100	Every rejection — a typed result, a thrown parameter-shape error, or a Host refusal — names the next action and the value that action takes, and those words come from one registry (`packages/agent-team/src/recovery-hints.ts`) rather than from each call site. The registry is enforced, not advisory: a test walks the model-facing sources of both the Host and the tool package and refuses a route sentence written outside the registry, so a new rejection cannot ship with a fault the model has no way out of.
101	
102	`reply` also takes `replyToMessageRef`, which names the Message on this Thread being answered. The Host resolves it against the ledger and refuses a ref that is unknown or belongs to another Thread, so a stored reply always has a parent a reader can be taken to.
103	
104	The link is recorded on the Message, renders as a quote the reader can follow back, and adds the parent's author to the recipients — answering a peer reaches them the way a mention does, without repeating their handle. The Human is never added, because they read the Thread directly.
105	
106	The switch on the Team row's settings decides whether the parameter is available at all; with it off, a reply that carries a ref is refused.
107	
108	## `team_dm`
109	
110	`team_dm` sends a private direct message to one enabled Agent Member in the same Workspace. It takes a `memberRef` and a `body` and nothing else — no Thread, no Task, no write token, and no attachments — because a DM addresses a person rather than a conversation. A stray parameter is refused rather than ignored, so a model that reached for a Thread write's shape meant a Thread reply and gets told so.
111	
112	A DM is pure delivery: the ledger appends an audit-only `team/dm-sent` operation (request-idempotent) while the recipient's live session receives the body as a relay-form injected user message — idle recipients get a new turn, busy ones are steered into the current turn. 113	
114	The first line of every result says which of the two it was: delivered, or recorded without a live session to wake. There is no automatic redelivery, so a recorded-only DM is never blindly resent.
115	
116	Use DMs for quick clarifications and status syncs only. Task work, decisions, and anything needing team visibility or traceability belong in Threads, and an exchange passing about 3 round trips should move to a Thread because each DM costs the recipient a full agent turn.
117	
118	## `team_task`
119	
120	`team_task` has the actions `board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, `transfer`, and `promote`.
121	
122	`board` renders the Host's Task board projection: every open Task of the Projects the reader can see, grouped into To do, In progress, and In review, newest activity first, then each Project's five newest finished Tasks. 123	
124	`projectRef` limits the board to one Project; `mine` keeps only Tasks the reader is accountable for or holds a live Claim on.
125	
126	`finishedTruncated` says whether the Host held back older resolved work; the render states it, so a page never reads as the whole column.
127	
128	The board is current state, not unread: reading it changes no read state and carries no write token. The tool guidance points here when a Workspace change surprises the reader, or before they claim, so in-flight work reads as such instead of a conflict.
129	
130	`promote` turns a discussion Thread into a Task; it takes `threadRef`, the Thread's `baseRevision`, and optionally `accountable`, and only a Project owner may do it (`project_owner_required` otherwise).
131	
132	`list`, `claim`, `done`, and `release` manage only the Agent's own Direction Claims on real Tasks. Taskless Threads have no Claim mutation. A successful Claim starts Attention. `list` renders the Task/Thread identity with the active collision surface — active Claims only, or an explicit none — and no write token; it supplies neither Thread facts nor a mutation basis.
133	
134	A committed mutation names its action (Claim created, completed, or released), renders the authoritative affected Claim first — ref, resulting state, owner, direction — then Task/Thread identity, and exactly one next-write token hand-off. Rejections share the message rejection form and the same [completeness and token rules](boundaries.md#mutation-fences); Task permissions are checked again on each attempt.
135	
136	`accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer` resolve a Task rather than a Claim, and the Host decides who may call them.
137	
138	`accept` belongs to the Human, or to a Project owner who never held a Claim on that Task and only while it is in review. `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer` belong to the Human and the current accountable. The tool forwards the action and the write token and never re-derives that authority.
139	
140	`transfer` takes `target` — a current Project owner's memberRef, `@Handle`, or a unique memberRef prefix, or `human` — and moves responsibility only, leaving Claims with their owners.
141	
142	A committed resolution names the action, the resulting status and resolution, the accountable owner, and the Claims it completed or released. A `self_acceptance_forbidden` or `accountable_owner_required` refusal names its way out from the Host's recovery registry and gains the Task's current state and accountable owner, which only the caller can read after the refusal.
