30	## Agent delivery
31	The Host computes delivery from the current Inbox; delivery class is runtime state, not a durable fact on the Message or Activity. There is one delivery class: every unread fact interrupts.
32	
33	| Unread fact | Agent recipient | Delivery |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| Thread mention or reply, responsibility Activity, Main stream marker, or live Task reminder | Any | Immediate |
36	| Thread ordinary fact | A follower of that Thread | Immediate |
37	| Main stream ordinary fact, including a new discussion | A reader whose Attention covers it | Immediate |
38	
39	Attention decides whether ordinary work exists at all, never how fast it travels: an ordinary Thread update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread, and an ordinary Main stream update only because its Attention covers that Main stream. Owning a Project does not choose a slower class, so a reader that follows a Thread is interrupted by its first ordinary update, and a reader that stops following it stops accumulating ordinary unread there.
40	
41	A `covered` signature keeps an unchanged rederivation from spending a second attempt on the same durable facts. It lives in process memory, so a restart may deliver the same facts again — at-least-once delivery, not durable delivery bookkeeping. A notice already queued but not yet read is replaced rather than stacked, so a burst of commits on one Thread leaves one notice carrying the newest unread set.
42	
43	An Activity notice renders the event's immutable fields — actor, object, and the recorded Claim refs or transfer endpoints — never current Task or Claim state. Delivering or reading it is context, not acknowledgment: unread remains until an explicit `team_thread read`. A complete Message body or Activity event rendered in a notice binds exactly that text for a later write; a truncated body, an identity-only line, or an omitted fact adds no binding. For an identity line, the earlier complete text on the surface is what a context check uses.
44	
45	Direct signals rank ahead of ordinary work across every scope. A direct Message or Task/Claim or Project-ownership Activity not yet complete in the Member's Session comes first, newest first across Threads and the Main stream. An ordinary Message never expands here; it appears only in its Thread's count.
46	
47	A direct fact already complete on the Session surface follows as an identity line marked `already in current context; still unread`, which binds nothing further. Delivery intent is not Session output, so a notice queued but not yet read cannot make its own facts visible. Task reminders follow as detail, and ordinary Thread counts and Main stream Thread cards come last.
48	
49	The eight-Thread scope cap and the twenty-detail cap apply only after that rank, so a newer direct signal cannot lose its scope to an older ordinary update. Main stream scopes do not consume the Thread cap, and ordinary count lines do not consume the detail cap.
50	
51	The whole notice, a recovery instruction included, is limited to 32,768 UTF-16 code units, with 2,048 held back for the mandatory omission and next-step routes. When direct signals are dropped, one warning states their total, names up to four scope routes plus a count of any others, and points to `team_inbox` and `team_thread read`; it never expands every route.
52	
53	## Main stream Attention
54	
55	The Main stream carries its own Attention, keyed by Member × Project rather than by a Thread ref: it is a conversation outside every Thread, so giving it a synthetic Thread ref would put it in the Thread indexes. Thread Attention and Main stream Attention are two independent rows for the same Member, each with its own read watermark.
56	
57	| Who | Main stream Attention |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| The Human | Derived, never stored: it starts at the Project's creation, and only the read watermark is stored |
60	| A Member granted Project ownership | Written by the grant itself, starting at the grant sequence — no historical backlog is inherited |
61	| Any other Member | Absent until it follows; then it starts at the current tail |
62	
63	The Human's derived Main stream Attention is mandatory and cannot be unfollowed; it starts with the Project and stores only its read watermark. Agent Members can follow or unfollow their Main stream Attention explicitly.

1	# Agent 工具与上下文呈现：已确认设计
2	
3	**确认日期：2026-10-29。** Human 已确认目标、具体行为和六段完整流程；本稿将讨论整理为实施依据。同日另行授权推进实施；进度见 README。本稿不描述当前产品行为，现行行为仍以源码、测试和正式文档为准。
4	
5	## 1. 目标与范围
6	
7	首要目标是 Agent 正确理解当前状态并完成协作；其次是减少重复上下文、重复读取和无效重试。不以整体压缩比例驱动改造，不因文字缩短就判定成功。
8	
9	范围覆盖七个 Team 工具、Agent 通知、Member 动态 context、persona 与 core skills。有证据的行为问题可以修正，但行为变化与文案整理分别验证。保留七个工具的职责、权限、Attention 和 Task/Claim 语义；不改 Human Web Client 交互、不改 Harness 仓库、agent loop 或 shipped defaults。
10	
11	工程细节由实施者决定：优先复用现有能力，选能够长期保留的最简单实现，不为假设需求引入通用框架、配置开关、备用实现或独立事实数据库。
12	
13	## 2. 三个不同的状态
14	
15	| 状态 | 含义 | 不意味着什么 |
16	| --- | --- | --- |
17	| 当前上下文已提供某事实 | 来源和对象明确，必要内容完整出现在本次模型可用的上下文中 | 不等于模型理解正确，不等于持久已读 |
18	| 已确认已读 | 显式 `read` 确认的事实，由 Host 写入既有阅读状态 | 不等于事项完成，不改变 Attention |
19	| 操作已提交 | Host 按当前权限、状态及并发条件提交操作 | 不等于通知送达，不顺带清除未读 |
20	
21	收到通知、发回复、`history`、`message` 查询和自动背景补充都不主动确认已读。`read` 可以省略当前上下文里已经完整提供的正文，但必须明确确认了哪些内容、哪些正文被省略、还有多少未读。
22	
23	历史已读不会因压缩而撤销；压缩可能导致 Agent 缺少工作背景，需要重新提供。当前上下文中的完整性只是本次阅读条件的依据，不建立第二套持久未读状态。
24	
25	## 3. Member 背景与记忆
26	
27	- 新会话或上下文缺少起步背景时，提供当前身份、Project ownership、Workspace 参与及路径、预算内完整 memory 索引。
28	- 没有变化时不追加重复内容。
29	- 自己修改 `memory.md` 后，只提供简短更新提示，明确先前副本不再代表最新文件；不强迫立即读取刚写过的文件。
30	- 身份、ownership、Workspace 分别更新；ownership 和 Workspace 变化提供各自完整当前列表，包含撤销为空或从多个参与缩为一个的情况。
31	- 不因责任变化重发 memory，不因 memory 更新重发身份和 Workspace。
32	- memory 删除、不可读或超过既有预算时，明确异常及读取/维护入口，不继续把旧副本当成当前索引。
33	- 压缩后按当前实际缺失的类别补足背景；不能因为还残留一条 memory 更新提示，就假定完整索引仍在。
34	- 记忆是可能过时的参考，不覆盖 Human 输入、Workspace 指令和 Team durable facts。
35	
36	## 4. 读取与恢复讨论
37	
38	`read` 负责分批提供未读、显式确认已读，并补足必要的讨论背景；不新增由模型选择的“继续/重新进入”模式。
39	
40	- 连续讨论：新增事实全文为主，附必要回复对象和当前 Task/Claim 状态，不重复大片历史。
41	- 首次进入、压缩后背景缺失、无未读但主动查看：提供讨论主题、少量最近原文、必要引用对象和当前状态。
42	- 背景判断使用当前上下文，不用永久的“以前读过”标记。无法可靠判断时补少量背景，不默认模型记得。
43	- 背景选取使用原文和既有结构化状态；不额外调用模型生成摘要。
44	- 背景、当前状态、未读事实明确区分。背景不主动推进阅读状态，也不把 Thread card 当成已读完其 Thread。
45	- 当前批次的正文及必要回复对象优先于额外背景。未提供的历史和附件给出入口；完整消息不代表附件已读。
46	- 未读按时间顺序分批，不为了展示最新结论跳过旧的必要事实。
47	
48	### 4.1 长内容
49	
50	普通消息尽量完整返回；一批放不下就减少条数。单条本身过长时，明确分段和续读入口，不静默截断。
51	
52	完整提供之前不确认该消息已读，不凭其预览满足写入条件。`read` 续读在完整提供后确认相应消息；`message` 续读保持查询性质，之后可由 `read` 确认并省略重复正文。一次调用必须前进或明确指向可用的续读动作，不能反复返回同一开头。
53	
54	返回范围与确认范围必须来自同一次选择。不能先确认整批，再在 renderer 末尾裁掉正文。旧的“最多若干条”不能冒充总文本长度预算。具体预算在实现时按现有约定和样例测定，不新增用户配置。
55	
56	### 4.2 已提供内容的确认
57	
58	`read` 是唯一显式确认入口，不新增独立“标记已读”工具。确认当前上下文中完整可见的事实时可以不重复正文；新到的或已不完整可见的内容照常提供。无需每次回复后立刻补调用，可在处理 Inbox 时合并确认。
59	
60	## 5. 写入条件与错误恢复
61	
62	对 Thread、Main 和 Task/Claim 使用一致的“所需事实是否完整提供”原则，但不统一它们本来不同的权限或 revision 要求。Main 不因本工作项新增 Thread 写入凭据。
63	
64	可以满足相应阅读条件的内容：来源和对象明确的完整通知、`read/history/message` 结果、拒绝结果中的完整变化，以及具有必要字段的 Task/Claim 事件。只检查本次操作适用的必要事实，不要求读完全部历史。
65	
66	不能据以判定完整提供：数量、标题、摘要、截断正文、模型自己的总结或“我看过了”。看板上的当前状态只证明当前状态，不代表相关事件或讨论已提供。
67	
68	- 拒绝结果完整补齐必要事实后，允许 Agent 重新考虑并提交，不强制重复读取相同内容。
69	- 结果未补齐时，明确缺失与读取入口，不提供暗示可直接写的凭据或恢复句。
70	- 凭据不保证成功。提交时仍检查最新未读、权限、Thread revision 和 Task 状态。
71	- 仅满足写入条件不写持久已读、不消费未读标记。
72	- 不保留正文子串匹配作为备用判断。必须对应具体事实及实际可见内容，短消息不能因别处出现 `ok` 而误命中。
73	
74	## 6. 通知
75	
76	| 类型 | 默认内容 |
77	| --- | --- |
78	| 直接提及或回复通知 | 发送者、原文、所属讨论、消息定位、必要回复背景 |
79	| 普通更新 | Thread/Main 入口及未读数量，不复制正文 |
80	| Task/Claim 变化 | 操作者、对象、实际变化、变化后状态和与读者的关系；不猜原因 |
81	| ownership 变化 | 新增或撤销的责任，不顺带重发全部背景 |
82	| DM | 发送者和原文；不虚构 Thread、不计入 Inbox |
83	
84	同批合并；直接提及和责任变化优先于普通计数。重要内容被省略时明确说明还有直接信号未展开，并给入口。既有已通知正文不得反复挤占新变化；重启/恢复保留既有可重派生投递语义，不新增投递数据库。
85	
86	通知预算约束整体输出，包含外层说明和读取入口。正文截断与其完整性判断一致。已提供必要事实时，不统一追加“必须先 read”；是否需要读取按当前缺失决定。通知不确认已读。
87	
88	通知派发性能由并行工作项负责；本工作项不另写派发器。实施通知票前核实那条线的最新实现，避免覆盖其改动。
89	
90	## 7. 工具结果与规则放置
91	
92	### 7.1 操作结果
93	
94	明确区分：已提交、未提交、已记录但未送达，以及确实无法确认的提交结果。
95	
96	- 成功给本次变化、必要对象标识和后续凭据，不重放全部正文或规则；没有必要下一步时不硬加建议。
97	- 部分投递失败不冒充操作未提交，不诱导重发已写入的内容。
98	- 拒绝说明原因及当前可执行恢复；需要重新判断时不说“原样重试”。
99	- 只有实际证据不足以判定提交结果时才说“不确定”；不用通用 catch 把所有错误改成不确定，也不为此前未遇到的错误增加完整重试框架。
100	
101	### 7.2 七工具职责
102	
103	`team_view` 提供地址目录，`team_inbox` 提供未读入口，`team_attention` 管关注，`team_thread` 提供读取和显式已读确认，`team_message` 管公开发言，`team_dm` 管直接投递，`team_task` 管工作状态。目录、看板和关注结果不扩张成正文读取或第二套写入依据。
104	
105	### 7.3 规则
106	
107	规则统一定义，但允许使用位置的必要短提醒：persona 放跨工具规则，工具说明放选择及调用所需契约，参数说明保留必要格式，结果说明本次状态和恢复，core skill 放详细方法和少见情况。不得为了去重让基本调用先依赖读教程。
108	
109	## 8. 工程落点
110	
111	Host module 保有事实、权限、阅读提交与写入检查的 interface；tool module 负责参数、Agent 结果和文本。Client 不解析这些文本。共享的内部 module 只承担当前真实重复的完整性判断或渲染，不建通用 Agent-facing 语义框架。
112	
113	实施依据和 Harness interface 核对见 [工程核对](materials/2026-10-29-implementation-notes.md)。尤其注意：canonical 工具结果不自动持久化；当前 surface 中的最终文本才参与判断；裁剪后 `meta` 可能原样留下，不能只信 `meta`。复用 Session 记录，不建独立的已读事实库。
114	
115	读取批次与确认需要在 Host 中协调。必要时增加窄的 Agent-owned 读取 interface，复用既有 Host 提交；不让 Session 可见性成为 ledger 重放的输入，不从 Agent renderer 更改 Human 读取行为。既有持久记录保持可重放，不为文案优化改变旧 operation 的解释。
116	
117	现有公开 seam 不足时先记录具体限制再决定；不访问私有字段、不修改 Harness、不虚构已经存在的承诺。结构选择、字段、预算和内部测试由实施者决定，无需逐项交 Human 拍板。
118	
119	## 9. 完整流程与验收
120	
121	[六段完整流程](materials/2026-10-29-accepted-flows.md)是行为验收入口，不是仅比较措辞的 snapshot。
122	
123	1. 起步、记忆更新、责任变化、压缩后恢复。
124	2. 普通更新、读取、理解当前分工、领取工作。
125	3. 直接提及、无需重复正文即可回复、稍后显式确认已读。
126	4. 旧状态写入被拒、收到完整变化、修改行动后提交。
127	5. 压缩后进入旧讨论、无未读也能恢复背景。
128	6. 长消息分段、可继续读取、完整后按动作性质确认。
129	
130	实现检查使用真实累计的 Session surface；覆盖裁剪、压缩、重启、短正文、跨 Thread 同文、旧凭据、新消息并发、memory 异常及通知上限。只覆盖现实生命周期与公开输入，不为类型已保证的内部值叠防御测试。
131	
132	模型评测复用既有 harness，使用隔离的合成场景，不上传个人会话语料；接入模型前核实本轮可用且获授权的配置，不复用归档中的凭据。关键指标是目标完成、根据新事实改行动、误调用与恢复次数，其后才是上下文 token/字符、总调用数与耗时。比较同一版本窗口和场景，重复运行并报告样本及波动，不承诺未测的成本比例。
133	
134	## 10. 实施与完成条件
135	
136	当前可开始的实施票为 01、02；其后按 [README 的依赖顺序](README.md#实施顺序)推进。每票包含行为、可见输出、测试及受影响正式文档，不先搭横向框架再等最后集成。
137	
138	完成要求：六段流程成立；关键新事实不丢失；无无效凭据指引、错误确认或重复读取循环；模型评测不出现未解释的正确性回退；相关旧路径与矛盾规则删除；双语正式文档和 CHANGELOG 同步；仅在影响 assembled Web/Remote 等面时运行相应浏览器检查。
139	
140	最初仅批准设计整理；2026-10-29 Human 随后授权推进生产实现，允许 subagent 实施、主线程审查。模型付费调用、提交和发布仍需另行授权。设计检查通过不等于上述实现验收通过。
141

**范围**：`packages/tool-agent-team`、`packages/client-agent-team`、`packages/agent-team/preset`、`core-skills`，以及 ticket 07 当前交付；设计依据 spec.md §3/§6/§8/§11 与 issues/06、07、08。\n- 唤醒 fan-out 缺失\n普通 Main stream 消息与新讨论 Thread **不会唤醒发帖人以外的 owner**。\n- `affectedMembersOf` 只向 inbox-delta 接收者和 Thread follower 扩散；`team/main-message-posted`、`team/thread-started` 既不为新 Thread 贡献 mention，正好掩盖了这个缺口。**这是最有价值的一条：测试的覆盖形状决定了缺陷能否存活。\n- 修法：为这两类操作补 `projectOwnerIds(projectRef)`（排除操作者）。\n\n## 三、SHOULD-FIX：预算与重放\n- **通知预算漏发**：`summarizedThrough` 对每个持有待投递 fact 的 Thread 都推进，但 `notificationText` 只渲染前 8 条、预算超限时静默丢弃整段——某 Thread 的普通更新可能被**从未提及它的通知「总结」掉**。修法：仅对实际追加段落推进 `summarizedThrough`，或输出省略计数。\n- **v1 回复重放不一致**：规则 v1→v2 采纳后，对 v1 回复做 requestId 重放会用**当前**规则版本重算 recipients，早于 会写进成员派生——等于可自助获得 Project 成员身份**，且拒绝时不带 recovery 码。这是\"读写两侧校验强度不对称\"的典型：所有读侧入口都要与写侧共用同一个成员判定。\n\n## 五、文档/文案漂移（v2 切换后未同步）\n- 看板页签仍在 `view.hasMore` 时渲染「加载更早消息」，对**投影看板无效**。\n- v2 下 tool 描述仍声称 `@all` 触达整个 Project（`@all` 在 rules version 2 是普通文本，不产生收件人与 marker）；`attention-and-messaging.md`、`domain-model.md` 同源矛盾。\n- v2 下仍保留 v1 的邀请流程文案与 throw。\n- `thread-and-composer.md` / `memory-and-context.md` / 2	name: distill-memory
3	description: Recognize breakthrough moments, blocking resolutions, and design decisions worth preserving. Detect high-value insights that save future time. Suggest distillation at valuable moments, not routine work.
4	---
5	
6	# Distill Memory
7	
8	Save proactively when the conversation produces a durable fact, preference, decision, plan, procedure, learning, event, or important context. Do not wait to be asked.
9	
10	## When to Suggest (Moment Detection)
11	
12	**Breakthrough:** Extended debugging resolves, user relief ("Finally!", "Aha!"), root cause found
13	
14	**Decision:** Compared options, chose with rationale, trade-off resolved
15	
16	**Research:** Investigated multiple approaches, conclusion reached, optimal path determined
17	
18	**Twist:** Unexpected cause-effect, counterintuitive solution, assumption challenged
19	
20	**Lesson:** "Next time do X", preventive measure, pattern recognized
21	
22	**Skip:** Routine fixes, work in progress, simple Q&A, generic info
23	
24	## Memory Quality
25	
26	**Good (atomic + actionable):**
27	
28	- "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused leaks."
29	- "PostgreSQL over MongoDB: ACID needed for transactions."
30	
31	**Poor:** Vague "Fixed bugs", conversation transcript
32	
33	## Tool Usage
34	
35	Use `nmem` CLI to create memories:
36	
37	```bash
38	nmem m add "Insight + context for future use" \
39	  -t "Searchable title (50-60 chars)" \
40	  -i 0.8
41	```
42	
43	Add `--unit-type fact|preference|decision|plan|procedure|learning|context|event` when the type is clear.
44	
45	If an existing memory already captures the same decision, workflow, or preference and the new information refines it, update that memory instead of creating a duplicate:
46	
47	```bash
48	nmem m update <id> -t "Updated title"
49	```
50	
51	**Content:** Outcome/insight focus, include "why", enough context
52	
53	**Importance:** 0.8-1.0 major | 0.5-0.7 useful | 0.3-0.4 minor
54	
55	**Note:** For programmatic use, add `--json` flag to get JSON response
56	
57	**Examples:**
58	
59	```bash
60	# High-value insight
61	nmem m add "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused memory leaks in event listeners." \
62	  -t "React Hooks Cleanup Pattern" \
63	  -i 0.9
64	
65	# Decision with context
66	nmem m add "Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for ACID compliance and complex queries" \
67	  -t "Database: PostgreSQL" \
68	  -i 0.9
69	```
70	
71	## Suggestion
72	
73	**Timing:** After resolution/decision, when user pauses
74	
75	**Pattern:** "This [type] seems valuable - [essence]. Distill into memory?"
76	
77	**Frequency:** 1-3 per session typical, quality over quantity
78	
79	## Troubleshooting
80	
81	If `nmem` is not in PATH: `pip install nmem-cli`, or on Arch Linux `yay -S nmem-cli` / `paru -S nmem-cli`
82	
83	For remote servers: run `nmem config client set url https://...` and `nmem config client set api-key ...` once on this machine.
84	
85	Run `/status` to check server connection.

51	**检查**：通知无普通正文；第一次 read 足以看到需求和当前分工；不重复 anchor；claim 结果不重放读到的正文；普通 Agent 不因 Team 改动获得这些工具或提示。
52	
53	## F3 直接提及、直接回复、稍后确认已读
54	
55	以 Main 为例。Thread 仍要求其既有写入凭据，不从通知猜数字。
56	
57	```text
58	直接通知
59	  项目 P / Main，消息 M，@B：@A Linux 回归完成了吗？
60	
61	前提
62	  当前上下文已有所需背景，没有其他缺失的必要事实。
63	
64	A post 回复
65	  回归已完成，结果通过。
66	  工具：已提交，新消息 N，回复 M。
67	  M 未因通知或回复被确认已读。
68	
69	稍后 read
70	  确认 M 已读；正文已在当前上下文中，不重复。
71	  如有新增 O，正常提供 O。
72	  说明剩余未读。
73	```
74	
75	**检查**：post 不要求重新读取同一正文；没有写入后自动确认；未读可通过 read 清理且不重复正文；期间到达新消息不被顺带跳过。
76	
77	## F4 旧状态写入被拒、重新判断、提交
78	
79	```text
80	A 读完 Thread，准备留言“可以发布”。
81	B 随后发言：Windows 安装失败，先不要发布。
82	
83	A 用旧凭据提交
84	  未提交，展示 B 的完整变化。
85	  相关变化已完整提供；要求重新考虑，给相应写入凭据。
86	
87	A 修改行动
88	  先暂停发布。我来复现 Windows 安装问题。
89	  提交成功；无需再 read 同一句话。
90	
91	稍后 read
92	  明确确认对应事实，已完整可见正文不重复。
93	```
94	
95	**检查**：Agent 修改行动而非机械重试；结果与恢复句不冲突；拒绝只展示部分事实时要求继续读取；并发新消息仍重新检查；相同短正文、不同 Thread 不能误判；既有权限和关闭状态仍约束写入。
96	
97	## F5 压缩后进入旧讨论，无未读也能恢复
98	
99	```text
100	用户：继续处理那个安装问题。
101	A 定位 Thread 后 read。
102	
103	没有未读，本次不改变未读状态。
104	主题：Windows 安装失败。
105	Task 进行中；A 负责复现；B 负责发布包。
106	近期原文：
107	  A：路径包含空格时失败。
108	  B：新版包已生成，等待复测。
109	更早历史未展示，可通过 history 读取。
110	
111	A 根据需要直接复测，或查询原复现步骤。
112	```
113	
114	**检查**：不因历史已读而只返空结果；不重放全部历史；不额外调用模型摘要；没有新已读 operation；背景查询不改变 Attention；再次 read 且背景仍在时不继续堆副本。
115	
116	## F6 长消息、分段续读、确认范围一致
117	
118	```text
119	通知
120	  B 提及 A，正文较长；当前只给预览和读取入口。
121	
122	read 或 message
123	  消息 M 第 1 段，未完整提供，给续读入口。
124	  M 尚未因本段被确认已读。
125	
126	连续续读
127	  每次前进到下一段；最后一段明确结束。
128	
129	read 流程
130	  完整交付后确认相应消息已读。
131	
132	message 查询流程
133	  提供全文但不确认；后续 read 可确认并省略已可见正文。
134	```
135	
136	**检查**：跨多字节字符不丢正文；预算包含包裹文本和下一步入口；中断、裁剪或压缩导致缺段时不误确认；普通长度一次全文；末段不等于附件已读；有多条未读时不能越过未完整提供的一条推进连续水位。
137	
138	## 结果表达补充
139	
140	- DM 已记录但无可投递会话：说明已记录、未送达，不建议盲目重发。
141	- Host 明确拒绝：说明未提交，不称“可能提交”。
142	- 实际中断且缺乏提交证据：说明结果尚不确定，给现有核实入口，不新增通用重试系统。
143	- 已提交但某通知失败：说明已提交及通知状态，不引导重复写入。
144	
145	## 验收矩阵
146	
147	| 流程 | 主要票据 | 确定性检查 | 模型行为检查 |
148	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
149	| F1 | 01 | 连续 Session 注入、分类撤销、压缩恢复 | 继续工作时使用当前责任和记忆 |
150	| F2 | 03、06、07 | 通知→read→claim、状态与正文一致 | 理解需求且不重复领取已有方向 |
151	| F3 | 03、05、06 | Main 通知→post→read、水位不提前动 | 无额外读正文即可回答，稍后正确清理 Inbox |
152	| F4 | 02、05、07 | 真实写入检查及恢复、并发变化 | 根据新事实修改行动，不只换凭据 |
153	| F5 | 03、07 | 压缩后无未读 read、背景无额外确认 | 能恢复工作，需要时主动补历史 |
154	| F6 | 04 | 分段完整性、连续确认、不会卡同一页 | 跟随续读入口，不误称全文已读 |
155	
156	先在相同合成场景上确定性验证，再运行获授权的真实模型评测；重复样本并报告波动。模型成功不能替代水位和提交检查，绿色单测也不能证明模型真的理解。

1	import type { AgentTeamProjectRef, AgentTeamThreadReadFact, AgentTeamThreadRef } from './types/entities.ts'
2	import type { AgentTeamInboxItem, AgentTeamInboxReminder, AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry } from './types/requests-results.ts'
3	
4	/**
5	 * Every unread fact interrupts: there is one delivery class. An ordinary Thread
6	 * update reaches a reader only because it follows that Thread, a mention or a
7	 * reply carries a direct marker, and a responsibility Activity or live Task
8	 * reminder arrives through its own marker — so what decides whether ordinary
9	 * work exists at all is Attention, never how fast it travels. No identity
10	 * chooses a slower class here. `covered` is what keeps an unchanged
11	 * rederivation from spending a second attempt on the same durable facts.
12	 */
13	export type InboxDelivery = 'immediate'
14	
15	/** The reader's role in one notice scope, as the notice states it. */
16	export type InboxScopeRole = 'follower' | 'member'
17	
18	export interface InboxThreadUnread {
19	  readonly item: AgentTeamInboxItem
20	  readonly facts: readonly AgentTeamThreadReadFact[]
21	  readonly reminders?: readonly AgentTeamInboxReminder[]
22	}
23	
24	export interface InboxMainUnread {
25	  readonly projectRef: AgentTeamProjectRef
26	  readonly entries: readonly AgentTeamMainTimelineEntry[]
27	}
28	
29	export interface InboxDeliveryInput {
30	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadUnread[]
31	  readonly main: readonly InboxMainUnread[]
32	  /** Signature of the immediate facts the last delivery attempt answered. */
33	  readonly covered: string | undefined
34	  /**
35	   * Threads the last notice could not render, so its facts were never delivered.
36	   * Their facts still enter this signature — otherwise an unchanged
37	   * rederivation would look identical to the delivered one — but the facts the
38	   * last attempt actually answered are the ones `covered` may match.
39	   */
40	  readonly undelivered?: readonly AgentTeamThreadRef[] | undefined
41	}
42	
43	export interface InboxThreadPlan {
44	  readonly threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef
45	  readonly role: InboxScopeRole
46	  readonly delivery: InboxDelivery
47	}
48	
49	export interface InboxDeliveryPlan {
50	  /** Why a notice goes out now, or `undefined` when nothing may interrupt the reader. */
51	  readonly trigger: InboxDelivery | undefined
52	  readonly signature: string
53	  /** The signature the next rederivation compares `covered` against: everything the notice can actually render. */
54	  readonly delivered: string
55	  readonly threads: readonly InboxThreadPlan[]
56	}
57	
58	export function planInboxDelivery(input: InboxDeliveryInput): InboxDeliveryPlan {
59	  const immediate: (string | number)[][] = []
60	  const delivered: (string | number)[][] = []
61	  const threads: InboxThreadPlan[] = []
62	  const undelivered = new Set(input.undelivered ?? [])
63	  for (const { item, facts, reminders = [] } of input.threads) {
64	    const threadRef = item.thread.threadRef
65	    // A reminder is always delivered: it is the whole reason the notice exists
66	    // when the Thread holds no ordinary unread.
67	    if (reminders.length > 0) {
68	      const reminderFacts = [threadRef, 'reminder', ...reminders.map(reminder => `${reminder.kind}:${reminder.baselineSequence}`)]
69	      immediate.push(reminderFacts)
70	      delivered.push(reminderFacts)
71	    }
72	    const now = facts.map(entry => entry.fact.sequence)
73	    if (now.length > 0) immediate.push([threadRef, ...now])
74	    // A Thread the notice cannot render is not delivered by this attempt, so its
75	    // facts are not what `covered` records: an unchanged rederivation still sees
76	    // them as owed and re-attempts instead of standing down.
77	    if (now.length > 0 && !undelivered.has(threadRef)) delivered.push([threadRef, ...now])
78	    threads.push(Object.freeze({ threadRef, role: item.attention === undefined ? 'member' : 'follower', delivery: 'immediate' as const }))
79	  }
80	  for (const { projectRef, entries } of input.main) {
81	    if (entries.length > 0) { immediate.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]); delivered.push([projectRef, ...entries.map(entry => entry.sequence)]) }
82	  }
83	  const signature = immediate.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(immediate)
84	  const covered = delivered.length === 0 ? '' : JSON.stringify(delivered)
85	  const trigger = signature !== '' && covered !== input.covered ? 'immediate' : undefined
86	  return Object.freeze({ trigger, signature, delivered: covered, threads: Object.freeze(threads) })
87	}

30	- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.
31	
32	**Changed**
33	
34	- Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original discussion context even after compaction with no unread. Already-visible Message bodies are explicitly omitted while the read acknowledges the same chronological batch; background, Main stream Thread cards, and current Task cards remain separate from newly acknowledged facts. Human reads and historical read receipts are unchanged.
35	- Agent `read` and `message` results share one output ceiling: the tool selects fewer facts, an oversized Message body returns in ordered parts, a read acknowledges only the prefix it can deliver and never crosses an incomplete Message, and repeating the same request resumes at the first missing segment of the current Session surface. A Thread read receipt records the selected bound, while receipts written before it keep the default batch; there is no offset parameter.
36	- Complete Thread Message rejections provide the facts and current token needed to reconsider a write without a mandatory extra read. The Host verifies exact Team source, Thread/Message identity, and the actual Session text; summaries and truncated results cannot satisfy the check. Partial rejections supply no token, and neither notifications nor rejections acknowledge unread work.
37	- Task and Claim Activities follow the same context rule as Messages. A notice, read/history result, or rejection binds the immutable event — actor, object, and recorded Claim refs or transfer endpoints — never current Task or Claim state; a complete mixed Message/Activity rejection supplies the Thread token, while partial facts do not. A Main stream post has no token and accepts complete pending entries from the current Session or an explicit read, and new unread entries, revision, permissions, and Task state are checked again.
38	- An Activity already fully visible in the current context is acknowledged by identity only, with its event marked as already present; the repeated identity does not bind a second time. An Activity is one line and cannot be split, so one beyond the output ceiling acknowledges nothing and reports that limit instead of offering continuation.
39	- Agent notices rank missing direct signals ahead of ordinary work. Direct Messages and Task/Claim or Project-ownership Activities not yet complete in the Session come first, newest first across Threads and the Main stream; a fact already complete on the Session surface appears only as an identity marked `already in current context; still unread`, without a second binding, and a queued but unread notice does not make its facts visible. Reminders follow, and ordinary counts and Main stream Thread cards come last. The Thread-scope and detail caps apply after that rank, the whole notice including a recovery instruction stays within one character budget, and dropped direct signals produce one warning with up to four routes instead of an unbounded list. Unread counts and markers, complete versus truncated binding, and delivery retries are unchanged.
40	- Member context updates identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and private memory separately. Editing `memory.md` produces a short stale-copy notice instead of repeating the full index and unrelated background; missing context restores the relevant current blocks. Empty ownership and reduced Workspace participation remain explicit.
41	- The Team settings nav row now carries the Team mark instead of the shell's generic gear. The shell draws nav glyphs by section id and `settings.section` offers no icon, so the row is tagged inside the settings dialog and the mark is painted over the shell glyph with a mask — the same contained workaround installed third-party themes use; it releases itself on dispose.
42	- The composer's mention picker is rebuilt on the version 2 model instead of the retired version 1 one. Its order no longer claims to rank how directly a pick reaches a Member — every mention is now a durable direct marker delivered identically whether or not the recipient follows, and the invitation step that once made a non-follower slower is gone. Rows are grouped by relation on `data-mention-group`: Project owners first (pinned, so the Members who decide are always at hand), then this Thread's followers, then the rest of the Project, then Workspace peers a pick would enroll into the Project — because a mention of a non-member is a Project-membership fact, and the recipient notice now names those Members as joining before the send. Within a group the order is online first, then handle, so it no longer drifts with the roster's arrival order. An offline Member is no longer dropped — a durable mention waits for them — so only lifecycle (`inactive`/`archived`) ends eligibility. A typed query now matches a handle substring or a description keyword, and an empty result shows a 「没有匹配的成员」 line instead of closing the popup.
43	- The Client drops its version 1 paths: the old Project feed, `@all` expansion, and the invitation confirmation flow are gone. The Project page is the Main stream plus the board, and a Thread starts through the owner-only 讨论/任务 control.

# 07 验收核对

2026-10-30。01–05 已提交；06 在最终检查和提交阶段。此文件是后续实施入口，不代表模型验收通过。

## 完成检查

- 逐项核实七工具盘点中的问题，只修改已证实的矛盾和重复说明。
- 复用真实 Session、Host、工具调用组合；不以自行拼接的 messages 数组代替实际上下文。
- F1–F6 的确定性验证与模型理解验证分别报告。
- 保持普通 Session 隔离、Human Remote、历史 ledger 重放与通知投递语义。
- 指标区分当前 surface 文本、单次新增输出、累计输出、完整模型请求；字符不是 token 或费用。
- 模型评测未获本轮配置和费用授权，不执行、不复制归档凭据。

## 已有确定性流程

以下定位已重新核对源码，提交后的联合验证还需执行。

| 流程 | 当前测试 | 检查范围 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | `member-context-integration.spec.ts` | 分类注入、memory 修改、撤销为空、压缩与真实 Session restore、普通 Agent 无注入 |
| F2 | `thread-read-context.spec.ts` 中 discussion→board→claim | 原文、Task/Claim 分工和领取结果；普通通知无正文由通知测试补充 |
| F3 | `main-read-context.spec.ts` 中完整direct→post→read | 无重复读取即可post，不自动确认，之后read省略正文并确认 |
| F4 | `surface-rejection-recovery.spec.ts`、`activity-tool-recovery.spec.ts` | 完整变化→修改回复→提交，新增事实仍拦截，不完整拒绝不给直接写入依据 |
| F5 | `thread-read-context.spec.ts`、`main-read-context.spec.ts` | 压缩后无未读仍提供最近原文，重复read不堆副本，不新增确认 |
| F6 | `thread-read-context.spec.ts`、`main-read-context.spec.ts`、`surface-probe.spec.ts` | 长消息续读、缺段恢复、未完整消息阻止后续确认、查询不确认、restore与裁剪 |

这些测试通过 ScriptedAdapter 固定模型行为，证明接口和状态条件，不能证明真实模型理解或行动正确。

## 评测工具限制

归档 `team-tools-model-eval/harness/live-eval.mts` 第177–220行自行维护 `messages`，直接执行 `tool.execute` 和 `tool.output.render`，没有真实 Session 的 call/result provenance 或 presentationMeta。它能测参数形状，不能直接用于01–06的完整事实识别与压缩恢复验收。

后续复用其合成场景和指标分类，但执行应使用既有 `realHarness` 与真实 Agent loop。无需复制一套工具循环或修改 Harness。评测模型配置必须在运行前由 Human 确认。

`harness/context-volume.mjs` 是历史日志累计输出统计，默认扫描本机个人日志；不能把它当当前 surface 或模型请求成本。07需要改成显式输入并明确统计对象，不修改历史研究数字。

## 07 只读盘点待核实

- 工具结果仍带 v1 `undeliveredMentions` 说明；若删除模型出口，保留历史ledger解释，不顺带移除重放。
- 双语 tools 文档提及 reply ref 设置开关，需以配置和代码查证是否存在。
- Thread地址与Main地址互斥；同一Thread的threadRef/taskRef当前可共存，说明不能泛称三者只能一个。message动作不接受只有taskRef。
- recovery registry 文档不能宣称所有错误均有下一步；无可执行恢复不硬加建议。
- DM body说明不应暗示正文提及Human可以向Human投递。
- team_attention 使用位置补 active Claim 拒绝unfollow的规则。
- persona、工具、参数、结果与core skill的重复说明可精简，但基本调用契约、动作选择与真实恢复入口必须保留。

## 当前量测

2026-10-30重跑既有合成Member场景，与基线deaa671对比：memory修改单次新增8242→355个UTF-16代码单元；ownership修改8301→154。初始分类包装8242→8455，压缩后恢复8301→8514。没有变化的步骤均无新注入。

这些是固定合成输入的字符数；当前surface与单次新增分别记录，未测token、真实请求费用或真实模型目标完成率。原始输出在`.scratch/local/agent-context-implementation/context-scenario-notification.json`。

74	A history page renders a historical outcome with Thread identity, the full anchor on a first page and the bounded subject on continuation pages, the selected facts and any derived Task cards in that sequence window, and the cursor/hasMore footer — never current Claims or a context recommendation. Every activity fact is structured from that event alone — its activity ref, actor, Task and Thread refs, and the Claim refs or transfer endpoints the activity recorded — never a bare kind and never current Task or Claim state.
75	
76	A `read` acknowledges an unread acceptance of a still-done Task in its facts and recommends nothing about the reader's context: with no rollover tool and no generation choice, there is no action for a read to state.
77	
78	## `team_attention`
79	
80	`team_attention` answers one question — am I following this Thread or this Project's Main stream, and should I be? `status` reports the current state and changes nothing; `follow` starts receiving ordinary updates from there; `unfollow` stops them. All three take the address and the routing Workspace. `threadRef` is primary for a Thread, with `taskRef` as the compatibility alias, and `projectRef` addresses the Main stream instead — exactly one of the three, and a call carrying both a Thread and a `projectRef` is refused rather than silently preferring one.
81	
82	Once the reader follows, every result also names what established that Attention — starting the Thread, claiming its Task, being accountable for it, owning the Project, being named in it, or choosing to follow. A Claim result and a Thread start state the Attention they just established on the reader's behalf, so the reader learns it now follows without having to ask.
83	
84	Attention is not reading. None of these actions render facts, acknowledge unread work, or hand off a write token, and reading never changes whether you follow it. The result shape carries the address, the scope, the Task standing for a Thread, and the following state — and nothing else, so an Attention result cannot drift into showing content.
85	
86	Every result states the consequence its verb alone does not carry. Following means ordinary updates from there interrupt you. Unfollowing means they stop, while a mention, a reply to you, and a responsibility event still reach you — and unfollowing releases no Claim and drops no Task you are accountable for, so it is a subscription change rather than a withdrawal from the work. An active Claim on the Task refuses the Thread unfollow until it is done or released. [Attention and messaging](attention-and-messaging.md) owns the rows themselves.
87	
88	The split from `team_thread` is what makes the read path carry no Attention logic at all: the three actions share one parameter pocket instead of borrowing a read pocket with three parameters (`messageRef`, `beforeSequence`, `limit`) they can never accept.
89	
90	## `team_message`
91	
92	`team_message.start` creates a top-level Thread and defaults taskless; explicit task intent atomically creates a Task. `reply` appends to an existing Thread. Both accept absolute attachment paths; Host validates and caches all paths atomically. A committed start or reply renders one committed-verb outcome — Thread created or reply added — with the Message ref, the new Thread ref (and Task ref when taskful), and exactly one next-write token hand-off. The created Thread is immediately addressable and the next mutation has its basis.
93	
94	Behind rules version 2 `team_message` also has `post`, which speaks in a Project's Main stream (`projectRef`, `body`, optional `replyToMessageRef` of a Main stream Message of the same Project). It needs no write token. A writer holding unread Main stream entries must instead hold every one of them complete in the current context — as a Team notice or a tool result that binds the actual rendered Message or Activity — or explicitly read with `projectRef`; otherwise it gets `main_unread_required`.
95	
96	`start` takes `kind: 'discussion' | 'task'` (the removed `asTask` spelling is refused with the parameter route to `kind`, never dropped), and only a Project owner may start: others get `project_owner_required`, which names `post`. A non-member gets `not_project_member`. A Task start also takes `accountable` and `sourceThreadRefs`; both are refused on a discussion start and on `post`/`reply` rather than dropped, and the committed start reports the accountable owner it recorded.
97	
98	`team_thread` `read`, `history` and `message` take either a `threadRef` or a `projectRef` (the Main stream), exactly one. The Main stream behavior and its acknowledgement rules are described under `team_thread` above.
99	
100	Typed rejection results (`unread_required`, `stale_revision`, `main_unread_required`) begin `Not committed` and retain refs and counts with a bounded selection of pending facts. A complete Message and Activity result with a recognized revision baseline supplies a token for reconsideration; a Main stream result supplies none (it has no token). Partial results and unknown baselines route to `read`. This neither acknowledges unread facts nor guarantees the next write. [Mutation fences](boundaries.md#mutation-fences) defines the complete rule.
101	
102	A mention of a Member the Thread has never carried is not a rejection either: under rules version 2 the Message commits and every addressable recipient is delivered, so there is no undelivered remainder to report and no invitation step. (Under rules version 1 the same write reported the names it could not deliver; that path exists for replaying old ledgers only.)
103	
104	Every rejection — a typed result, a thrown parameter-shape error, or a Host refusal — names the next action and the value that action takes, and those words come from one registry (`packages/agent-team/src/recovery-hints.ts`) rather than from each call site. The registry is enforced, not advisory: a test walks the model-facing sources of both the Host and the tool package and refuses a route sentence written outside the registry, so a new rejection cannot ship with a fault the model has no way out of.
105	
106	`reply` also takes `replyToMessageRef`, which names the Message on this Thread being answered. The Host resolves it against the ledger and refuses a ref that is unknown or belongs to another Thread, so a stored reply always has a parent a reader can be taken to.
107	
108	The link is recorded on the Message, renders as a quote the reader can follow back, and adds the parent's author to the recipients — answering a peer reaches them the way a mention does, without repeating their handle. The Human is never added, because they read the Thread directly.
109	
110	The switch on the Team row's settings decides whether the parameter is available at all; with it off, a reply that carries a ref is refused.
111	
112	## `team_dm`
113	
114	`team_dm` sends a private direct message to one enabled Agent Member in the same Workspace. It takes a `memberRef` and a `body` and nothing else — no Thread, no Task, no write token, and no attachments — because a DM addresses a person rather than a conversation. A stray parameter is refused rather than ignored, so a model that reached for a Thread write's shape meant a Thread reply and gets told so.
115	
116	A DM is pure delivery: the ledger appends an audit-only `team/dm-sent` operation (request-idempotent) while the recipient's live session receives the body as a relay-form injected user message — idle recipients get a new turn, busy ones are steered into the current turn. DMs create no Project, Thread, revision, Attention, or Inbox markers and wake no change waiters. The Human cannot be DMed.
117	
118	The first line of every result says which of the two it was: delivered, or recorded without a live session to wake. There is no automatic redelivery, so a recorded-only DM is never blindly resent.
119	
120	Use DMs for quick clarifications and status syncs only. Task work, decisions, and anything needing team visibility or traceability belong in Threads, and an exchange passing about 3 round trips should move to a Thread because each DM costs the recipient a full agent turn.
121	
122	## `team_task`
123	
124	`team_task` has the actions `board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, `transfer`, and `promote`.
125	
126	`board` renders the Host's Task board projection: every open Task of the Projects the reader can see, grouped into To do, In progress, and In review, newest activity first, then each Project's five newest finished Tasks. Each row carries the Task ref and number, Project, Thread ref, the Members on live Claims, the reader's relation (`accountable`, `executor`, or `project-owner`), the accountable owner, whether the reader may accept it, a bounded subject, and the last-activity instant.
127	
128	`projectRef` limits the board to one Project; `mine` keeps only Tasks the reader is accountable for or holds a live Claim on.
129	
130	`finishedTruncated` says whether the Host held back older resolved work; the render states it, so a page never reads as the whole column.
131	
132	The board is current state, not unread: reading it changes no read state and carries no write token. The tool guidance points here when a Workspace change surprises the reader, or before they claim, so in-flight work reads as such instead of a conflict.
133	
134	`promote` turns a discussion Thread into a Task; it takes `threadRef`, the Thread's `baseRevision`, and optionally `accountable`, and only a Project owner may do it (`project_owner_required` otherwise).
135	
136	`list`, `claim`, `done`, and `release` manage only the Agent's own Direction Claims on real Tasks. Taskless Threads have no Claim mutation. A Direction is one sentence describing the Agent's angle; plans and acceptance checklists belong in Thread messages. A successful Claim starts Attention. `list` renders the Task/Thread identity with the active collision surface — active Claims only, or an explicit none — and no write token; it supplies neither Thread facts nor a mutation basis.
137	
138	A committed mutation names its action (Claim created, completed, or released), renders the authoritative affected Claim first — ref, resulting state, owner, direction — then Task/Thread identity, and exactly one next-write token hand-off. Rejections share the message rejection form and the same [completeness and token rules](boundaries.md#mutation-fences); Task permissions are checked again on each attempt.
139	
140	`accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer` resolve a Task rather than a Claim, and the Host decides who may call them.
141	
142	`accept` belongs to the Human, or to a Project owner who never held a Claim on that Task and only while it is in review. `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer` belong to the Human and the current accountable. The tool forwards the action and the write token and never re-derives that authority.
143	
144	`transfer` takes `target` — a current Project owner's memberRef, `@Handle`, or a unique memberRef prefix, or `human` — and moves responsibility only, leaving Claims with their owners.
145	
146	A committed resolution names the action, the resulting status and resolution, the accountable owner, and the Claims it completed or released. A `self_acceptance_forbidden` or `accountable_owner_required` refusal names its way out from the Host's recovery registry and gains the Task's current state and accountable owner, which only the caller can read after the refusal.
147

3	DeepSeek Harness is an all-plugin Cordis agent harness. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.
4	
5	## Pre-stable APIs and released Session data
6	
7	Public APIs are pre-stable; update every consumer. Follow [version/status](docs/session-format-status.md) and [type acknowledgements](docs/cookbook/reviewing-persistence-type-changes.md). [Adjacent migration](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-31-released-session-format-migrations.md) may add a version-named successor but never move, overwrite, or delete committed generations; predecessors imply neither fallback nor downgrade support. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
8	
9	Acknowledge [declared persistence-type changes](docs/cookbook/reviewing-persistence-type-changes.md).
10	
11	Record each externally perceptible breaking change immediately in an [upgrade guide](.agents/skills/dsh-create-upgrade-guide/SKILL.md).
12	
13	**Application launch.** Only `dsh` profiles launch supported Node apps; package bins, demos, and public SDK argv escapes are forbidden ([rule](docs/architecture.md#application-launch)).

109	### Host sandbox failures
110	
111	If a required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator command fails because the sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass test failures or the product sandbox.
112	
113	### Run relevant checks locally
114	
115	Before pushing, follow [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.
116	
117	- Match evidence to the surface: focused behavior tests, model/user-output snapshots, `doc-sync` for docs, built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for providers.
118	- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
119	- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).
120	- Develop with `build:artifacts`; before claiming completion, run `build:check` after the latest `build:artifacts`, or `build` ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
121	- **Web browser automation and GIF recording:** launch with `pnpm dsh web --patch apps/web/tests/pin-browse-picker.overlay.yml` to use the [in-page directory picker](apps/web/tests/pin-browse-picker.overlay.yml); omit this override only when testing native picker behavior explicitly.
122	
123	## Secrets / .env
124	
125	Windows packaging/signing: [required reading](apps/desktop/windows-signing/README.md).
126	
127	Real-API tests/demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

1	# Sessions
2	
3	English | [中文](session.zh.md)
4	
5	The in-memory, event-sourced model of [dsh-session](../../packages/core/session). A `Session` is an **append-only log** of typed `SessionEvent`s — the single source of truth for an agent's whole interaction history. The LLM message history is *derived* from the log, never stored separately; replay is re-derivation from the same events. How the log is made **durable** (the persistence seam, backends, crash recovery) is the sibling concern on [persistence.md](persistence.md).
6	
7	Source: [`packages/core/session/src/types.ts`](../../packages/core/session/src/types.ts)
8	
9	## `SessionEventMap` — the event vocabulary
10	
11	The append-only event types. Merge-extensible: a plugin declares extra event types via declaration merging — e.g. the [compaction seam](compaction.md) adds `compaction/start` / `compaction/summary` / `compaction/end`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hook-protocol` adds log-only `hook/invoked` / `hook/result` records for a hook bridge. Like `compaction/*`, these are NOT `SurfaceEventType`s (no `surfaceOp`). The generated [persistence log event catalog](../persistence-catalog.md) enumerates every member — core and merged — with its payload, surface badge, and declaration site.

14	/** A user-role specialization of the shared message representation. */
15	interface UserMessage extends MessageBase {
16	  readonly role: 'user'
17	}
18	```

20	```ts type-equiv
21	/**
22	 * The merge-extensible, append-only source of truth for an agent interaction.
23	 * Message history is derived from this log. Every event is lossless JSON and
24	 * sequence numbers stay contiguous. Assistant attempt events embed their exact
25	 * compact raw streams so persistence stores one durable settlement per attempt.
26	 */
27	interface SessionEventMap {
28	  /**
29	   * Opens turn `turn` before the loop claims queued input or runs pre-step.
30	   * Rejection, empty input, cancellation, or failure may close it with no
31	   * step; otherwise the following identified `user/message` event or batch
32	   * records the messages entering the step.
33	   */
34	  'turn/start': { turn: number }
35	  /**
36	   * Closes turn `turn` with the {@link TurnEndReason} that ended it. A turn
37	   * with no entered step has no `step/start` or `step/end`. The loop does not await a
38	   * flush at turn boundaries: `dsh-session-checkpoint-policy` owns the
39	   * per-request durability checkpoint, and consumers that read storage after
40	   * `whenIdle()` flush themselves. Success commits the turn; rejection is
41	   * reported live and does not prevent later work.
42	   */
43	  'turn/end': { turn: number; reason: TurnEndReason }
44	  /** Opens step `step` of turn `turn` — one model call plus the tool executions it requested. */
45	  'step/start': { turn: number; step: number }
46	  /** Closes step `step` of turn `turn`. */
47	  'step/end': { turn: number; step: number }
48	  /**
49	   * A user-role message on the model-visible surface: a direct human prompt
50	   * (the queued message claimed for this turn), a synthetic `agent.inject()`
51	   * context (file-change notices, subdir AGENTS.md, skill content, cron
52	   * notifications, …), or an entered goal continuation round. All three
53	   * project their `content` verbatim; `source` tells them apart.
54	   */
55	  'user/message': UserMessage
56	  /** An incremental agent session change admitted at the named turn and step. */
57	  'developer/message': {
58	    turn: number
59	    step: number
60	    message: DeveloperMessage
61	    /** Earlier request/header defining every tool addition; required exactly when additions are present. */
62	    headerSeq?: SessionSeq
63	  }
64	  /**
65	   * The rendered system prompt on the model-visible surface. The loop appends
66	   * the first one as surface node 0 before the step's first `user/message`.
67	   * A prepared in-history route can append nonempty changes in a continuing
68	   * series. An incapable route or new series normalizes text to the first system
69	   * node. Normalization empties nonempty later nodes, then rewrites the head if
70	   * needed, through logged per-node replacements. An empty rendering always
71	   * clears all active system nodes, leaving no older instructions model-visible.
72	   * Empty later nodes are dormant and project to no message; an empty head with
73	   * no active later node records "no system prompt". Restored nonempty text follows
74	   * the same route and series rule; empty nodes never restore older text.
75	   */
76	  'system/message': { turn: number; step: number; message: SystemMessage }
77	  /**
78	   * Assembled assistant message for one step (derived history uses this).
79	   * Carries the step's `usage` when the adapter reported token accounting, so
80	   * the model output and its accounting travel together (there is no separate
81	   * usage record). `usage` is absent when the adapter reported none. A turn
82	   * cancelled mid-stream finalizes its delivered text/reasoning prefix as this
83	   * event with `interrupted: true`; undispatched tool calls are absent. The
84	   * marker distinguishes that prefix without re-deriving interruption from turn
85	   * boundaries. An aborted turn with no such event streamed no visible content.
86	   */
87	  'assistant/message': {
88	    turn: number
89	    step: number
90	    message: AssistantMessage
91	    /** Exact timed model stream, compacted without joining delta boundaries. */
92	    stream: AssistantStreamRecord[]
93	    usage?: TokenUsage
94	    interrupted?: true
95	  }
96	  /**

1	# Agent Note: Deprecate synchronous reads of arbitrary Session events
2	
3	Status: implemented
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-09-deprecate-synchronous-session-event-reads.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Synchronous access to arbitrary event positions makes consumers depend on the complete Session event sequence being immediately available in memory. The storage direction is to stop retaining that complete sequence in memory. Once historical events require storage I/O, the runtime cannot preserve the same synchronous read guarantee without retaining the history or blocking on storage.
10	
11	New callers increase that dependency even when they read only one old event. Repeated history scans after resume also make ordinary domain logic depend on historical storage instead of the state it actually needs.
12	
13	## Decision
14	
15	All operations that synchronously read arbitrary positions or ranges of Session event history are deprecated, including `Session.eventAt()`, `Session.snapshotEvents()`, and `Session.ownEvents()`. Existing logic may remain unmigrated for now, but new calls are prohibited. New aliases or wrappers that expose the same synchronous historical access are prohibited as well.
16	
17	The three methods carry this rule in `@deprecated` JSDoc. This is an API-use decision; the current Session implementation still retains the complete event sequence in memory.
18	
19	Repository test files, including `scripts/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}`, may call these three readers to inspect emitted events and exercise Session history behavior. The test-file lint override allows `snapshotEvents`, `eventAt`, and `ownEvents`; all other deprecated names remain errors. This allowance also covers unrelated declarations with the same three names under the current linter. It does not apply to production source or non-test repository scripts.
20	
21	### State needed after resume
22	
23	Design durable event fields and Session projections together so each domain can reconstruct the state its consumers need. Restore that state during resume, then maintain it incrementally from newly committed events. After resume, ordinary logic reads the projection or processes the delivered current event instead of looking back through historical events. Reading already-maintained projection state synchronously does not require arbitrary access to the event log.
24	
25	Historical content presented on demand uses explicit asynchronous pagination and progressive loading, with each read limited to the requested window. Loading the complete sequence behind a synchronous helper preserves the dependency this decision removes.
26	
27	### Operations that require complete history
28	
29	Fork and a small number of operations may genuinely need a complete historical sequence or inherited prefix. Their need for those records remains valid and requires an explicit storage read. It does not require the whole sequence to remain resident or grant an exception for new calls to deprecated synchronous readers. Each such consumer must establish why its result requires the complete sequence rather than projected state or a limited historical window.
30	
31	## Alternatives considered
32	
33	**Keep synchronous single-event reads while deprecating only full snapshots.** A single requested event may also be absent from memory. Restricting the result size does not remove the storage dependency, and helpers such as `ownEvents()` retain the same assumption for a suffix.
34	
35	**Keep the complete sequence resident to preserve the read APIs.** This lets consumer convenience dictate Session memory retention and prevents the intended storage design. Projections preserve required state, while explicit historical reads preserve access to the records themselves.
36	
37	**Require every existing caller to migrate immediately.** Existing logic may defer migration under this decision. Preventing new dependencies bounds the remaining work without making every existing consumer part of the same change.
38	
39	**Disable deprecation lint throughout test files or exempt production readers by name.** Tests only need the three reader names; other deprecated APIs must remain errors. Production code retains the prohibition on new synchronous reads.
40	
41	**Add a separate test-only reader API.** The three existing readers already expose the observations these tests need. Wrapping them adds an API and production-import checks without changing those observations.
42	
43	## Consequences
44	
45	New domain behavior must make its event data and projected state sufficient for resumed execution. User-requested history may still load progressively, and genuine full-history operations still have a storage path to design. This decision does not claim that resume or fork already avoids loading the complete log.
46	
47	Calls outside test files carry line-scoped `typescript/no-deprecated` waivers that identify deferred migration or delegation between deprecated readers. Remove a waiver when its deprecated call is removed; copying a waiver to a new production call violates this policy. The executable lint check accepts test reads and existing waived reads, rejects unwaived production reads, and rejects unrelated deprecated APIs in tests. Documentation checks verify the source-equivalent API declarations and bilingual records.
48	
49	## Related decisions
50	
51	The [session immutability decision](2026-06-11-dev-invariants-over-deep-readonly.md) continues to own event ownership and freezing; this decision supersedes its recommendation to use synchronous historical readers. The [required projection reader decision](2026-08-19-session-projection-mandatory-seam.md) continues to own missing-state failures and typed state reads. The [recallable compaction proposal](../../proposed/feature/2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.md) retains its recall design while replacing its proposed synchronous history access with paged reads.
52

import { afterEach, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { createUserMessage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'

import { cleanups, realHarness, requestId, ScriptedAdapter, textResponse, toolCallResponse, waitFor } from '../../../../packages/agent-team/tests/helpers/member-harness.ts'

afterEach(async () => { await Promise.all(cleanups.splice(0).map(cleanup => cleanup())) })

it('exports real Session checkpoints for direct reply, acknowledgment, compaction and continuation', async () => {
  const adapter = new ScriptedAdapter()
  const { ctx, workspaceId } = await realHarness(adapter)
  const project = await ctx.agentTeam.createProject({ requestId: requestId('project'), workspaceId,
    name: 'Synthetic release checks', description: 'Isolated context acceptance scenario' })
  const projectRef = project.project.projectRef
  const member = await ctx.agentTeam.addMember({ requestId: requestId('member'), workspaceId,
    handle: 'builder', description: 'Checks signed packages', presetId: 'team-member', projectRefs: [projectRef] })
  const agent = ctx.agents.get(member.status.member.sessionId)!
  const snapshots: unknown[] = []
  function checkpoint(stage: string) {
    snapshots.push({ stage, sessionId: agent.session.id, header: agent.session.header,
      events: agent.session.snapshotEvents(), requests: adapter.requests.map(request => ({ messages: request.messages, tools: request.tools })) })
  }
  async function call(name: string, args: object) {
    const before = adapter.requests.length
    adapter.enqueue(toolCallResponse(`call-${before}`, name, args))
    adapter.enqueue(textResponse('Checks recorded.'))
    agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Continue the package checks.' }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
    await waitFor(() => adapter.requests.length === before + 2 ? true : undefined)
    await agent.whenIdle()
    const result = agent.session.deriveMessages().filter(message => message.role === 'tool').at(-1)!
    expect(result.isError).not.toBe(true)
    return result.content.flatMap(part => part.type === 'text' ? [part.text] : []).join('\n')
  }
  function standing() { return ctx.agentTeam.mainStreamHistoryForAgent(agent, { workspaceId, projectRef }).standing }
  adapter.enqueue(textResponse('The direct request is available.'))
  const direct = await ctx.agentTeam.postMainMessage({ requestId: requestId('direct'), workspaceId, projectRef,
    body: '@builder Verify the signed package in a path containing spaces.' })
  if (direct.kind !== 'committed') throw new Error('Direct setup failed')
  await waitFor(() => adapter.requests.length === 1 ? true : undefined)
  await agent.whenIdle()
  checkpoint('F3-direct-notice')
  expect(await call('team_message', { action: 'post', projectRef, body: 'The signed package passed the path-with-spaces check.', replyToMessageRef: direct.message.messageRef }))
    .toContain('Committed — Main stream message posted.')
  expect(standing()).toMatchObject({ unreadCount: 1, directCount: 1 })
  checkpoint('F3-reply-without-read')
  const read = await call('team_thread', { action: 'read', projectRef })
  expect(read).toContain('acknowledged 1 unread update(s)')
  expect(read).not.toContain(direct.message.body)
  expect(standing().unreadCount).toBe(0)
  checkpoint('F3-explicit-read')

  const operationCount = ctx.agentTeam.status().operationCount
  const nodes = agent.session.surface.nodes.slice(1)
  agent.session.append('user/message', createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Summary: continue package verification.' }], source: { kind: 'user' } }), {
    surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', startSeq: SessionSeq(nodes[0]!), endSeq: SessionSeq(nodes.at(-1)!) }, sourceEventSeqs: [...nodes],
  })
  checkpoint('F5-compacted')
  expect(await call('team_thread', { action: 'read', projectRef })).toContain(direct.message.body)
  expect(ctx.agentTeam.status().operationCount).toBe(operationCount)
  checkpoint('F5-background-restored')
  expect(await call('team_thread', { action: 'read', projectRef })).not.toContain(direct.message.body)
  expect(ctx.agentTeam.status().operationCount).toBe(operationCount)
  checkpoint('F5-background-not-repeated')

  await ctx.agentTeam.readMainStream({ requestId: requestId('human-read'), workspaceId, projectRef })
  const body = '@builder ' + '安装路径🙂保留空格。'.repeat(5200) + '完整检查结束。'
  adapter.enqueue(textResponse('A long check arrived.'))
  const before = adapter.requests.length
  const long = await ctx.agentTeam.postMainMessage({ requestId: requestId('long'), workspaceId, projectRef, body })
  if (long.kind !== 'committed') throw new Error('Long setup failed')
  await waitFor(() => adapter.requests.length === before + 1 ? true : undefined)
  await agent.whenIdle()
  checkpoint('F6-truncated-notice')
  const pieces: string[] = []
  for (let index = 0; index < 5; index += 1) {
    const text = await call('team_thread', { action: 'message', projectRef, messageRef: long.message.messageRef })
    expect(text.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(32768)
    pieces.push(...[...text.matchAll(/<message-part[^>]*>\n([\s\S]*?)\n<\/message-part>/g)].map(match => match[1]!))
    expect(standing()).toMatchObject({ unreadCount: 1, directCount: 1 })
    checkpoint(`F6-message-part-${index + 1}`)
    if (text.includes('complete in current context')) break
  }
  expect(pieces.join('')).toBe(body)
  const acknowledged = await call('team_thread', { action: 'read', projectRef })
  expect(acknowledged).toContain('acknowledged 1 unread update(s)')
  expect(acknowledged).not.toContain('安装路径')
  expect(standing().unreadCount).toBe(0)
  checkpoint('F6-explicit-read')
  const output = resolve('.scratch/local/agent-context-implementation/context-snapshots.json')
  await mkdir(resolve(output, '..'), { recursive: true })
  await writeFile(output, JSON.stringify({ format: 'team-context-snapshots-v1', snapshots }, null, 2))
})

# 合成场景与上下文量测

当前行为以 packages 源码与测试为准；本目录为工作项的验收工具，不读取个人 Session，也不调用真实模型。

## 当前组合场景

从仓库根运行：

```bash
npx vitest run --config .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/vitest.config.ts --project context-scenarios
```

使用既有 realHarness、ScriptedAdapter 和真实 Agent loop，在同一 Session 中依次验证 F3（direct→post→read）、F5（压缩→无未读背景恢复→不重复）与 F6（长通知→message续读→显式确认），同时检查 Host 未读状态。F1、F2、F4 与更多边界复用 packages 下现有集成测试，定位见 `../materials/2026-10-30-acceptance-plan.md`。

输出 `.scratch/local/agent-context-implementation/context-snapshots.json`。它是合成场景快照，不是 Session 存储文件格式；不要传入个人日志。

## 当前量测

```bash
node --import tsx .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/context-volume.mts .scratch/local/agent-context-implementation/context-snapshots.json
```

必须显式指定输入，不会默认扫描本机目录。可以传多个合成快照文件，分别列出文件数量、Session 数量及每个阶段。

- `cumulativeLog`：截至该检查点的全部已记录文本，按工具动作与 Member 背景类别分别计数。包括已经离开当前上下文的内容。
- `currentSurface`：通过 Harness 的 Session 投影得到的当前模型上下文文本。
- `requests`：真实 Agent loop 交给 ScriptedAdapter 的每次 GenerateOptions；文本、消息 JSON 和工具 schema JSON 分开计数。不是 provider 网络请求字节数。
- `partBindings` / `wholeMessageBindings`：输出中记录的分段／全文绑定次数，不代表唯一内容量或当前仍可见的内容量。

所有长度都是 UTF-16 代码单元，不是 token、费用或模型理解质量。每个检查点在自身 Session 内累计，不可把连续检查点相加。该工具通过实际 Session 的恢复验证事件和 surface，不从 metadata 单独推断可见事实。

## Member 分类更新对比

```bash
node --import tsx .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/member-context-scenario.mts
```

固定合成 memory 与责任变化，对比基线 `deaa671` 和当前实现。每个版本独立 Session，分别输出单步注入、完整索引副本和当前 surface 字符数。

## 历史工具

`member-context-resend.mjs` 与 `member-context-triggers.mjs` 是旧个人日志研究入口，不属于当前验收命令，不应默认重跑。原 `context-volume.mjs` 的自动扫描实现已由上述显式合成输入工具替代；历史材料中的数字和命令保留原记录，不更新成新结果。

## 真实模型

ScriptedAdapter 固定行为，只证明组合和状态规则，不证明模型会正确理解。旧 `team-tools-model-eval` runner 自行拼 messages、直接 execute/render，适合历史参数形状评测，但不能验证本工作项的 Session 上下文恢复。真实模型验收应继续复用真实 Agent loop；运行前确认本轮模型配置和费用授权，不复制归档配置或凭据。

84	`team_message.start` 创建 Project 顶层 Thread。默认 taskless，也接受明确 task intent 以原子创建 Task。`team_message.reply` 向既有 Thread 追加明确的 reply。二者都接受 `attachments` 中的可选 absolute file paths。Host 验证每个 path，把 bytes 复制到 attachment cache。收件人看到 thumbnails/chips 与一行 cached path。任一 path 验证失败都会拒绝整个 send。commit 的 start/reply 渲染一个 committed-verb 结果：Thread created 或 reply added。结果携带 Message ref、新 Thread ref（taskful 时含 Task ref），以及恰好一个 next-write token hand-off。新建 Thread 立即可寻址，下一次变更也拿到了基础。
85	
86	规则版本 2 起，`team_message` 还有 `post`，在 Project 的 Main stream 发言（`projectRef`、`body`，可选 `replyToMessageRef`，须为同一 Project 的 Main stream Message）。它不需要写入 token。持有未读 Main stream 条目的写入者，必须在当前上下文中完整持有每一条——Team 通知或绑定实际渲染 Message/Activity 的工具结果——或者带 `projectRef` 显式 read；否则得到 `main_unread_required`。
87	
88	`start` 带 `kind: 'discussion' | 'task'`（已移除的 `asTask` 写法会被拒绝并指回 `kind`，绝不静默丢弃），只有 Project owner 能开：其他人得到 `project_owner_required`，提示改用 `post`；非 member 得到 `not_project_member`。Task start 另接受 `accountable` 与 `sourceThreadRefs`；两者在讨论 start 与 `post`/`reply` 上都被拒绝而非丢弃，commit 的 start 回报实际记录的负责人。
89	
90	`team_thread` 的 `read`、`history`、`message` 只寻址一个 scope：Thread 用 `threadRef`（该 Thread 有 Task 时也可用别名 `taskRef`），Main stream 用 `projectRef`；同时给两个 scope 会被拒绝。`message` 必须带 `threadRef` 或 `projectRef`，只有 `taskRef` 不能读回一条 Message。Main stream 的行为与确认规则见上文 `team_thread` 一节。
91	
92	类型化拒绝（`unread_required`、`stale_revision`、`main_unread_required`）以 `Not committed` 开头，保留 refs、计数和有界的待处理事实。Message 与 Activity 结果完整，且 revision 基线可识别时，会提供令牌供重新考虑；Main stream 结果不提供令牌（它本来就没有）。部分结果与未知基线指向 `read`。这既不确认未读，也不保证下一次写入成功。完整规则见 [Mutation fences](boundaries.zh.md#mutation-fences)。

102	## `team_dm`
103	
104	`team_dm` 向同一 Workspace 内一个 enabled Agent Member 发送私有 direct message。它只接受 `memberRef` 与 `body`，别无其他——没有 Thread、没有 Task、没有写令牌、没有附件——因为 DM 寻址的是人，不是会话。多带的参数会被拒绝而不是被忽略，因此伸手去拿 Thread 写入形状的模型会被告知：你想要的其实是 Thread reply。
105	
106	DM 是纯送达。ledger 追加一个 audit-only 的 `team/dm-sent` operation，requestId 幂等。收件人的 live session 以 relay-form 注入的 user message 收到正文。idle 收件人开新 turn，busy 收件人 steer 进当前 turn。DM 不创建 Project、Thread、revision、Attention 或 Inbox markers，也不唤醒任何 change waiters。Human 不能被 DM。
107	
108	每条结果的第一行都说明它是哪一种：已送达，还是只记录在案、没有可唤醒的 live session。没有自动重投，因此只记录在案的 DM 绝不被盲目重发。

70	## `team_attention`
71	
72	`team_attention` 只回答是否关注这个 Thread 或这个 Project 的 Main stream，以及该不该继续关注。`status` 报告当前状态且不改变任何东西；`follow` 开始接收来自那里的普通更新；`unfollow` 停止接收。三者参数完全相同：地址与路由 Workspace。Thread 用 `threadRef` 作 primary identity，`taskRef` 是 compatibility alias，两者只有在指向同一个 Thread 时才能同时出现；`projectRef` 改指 Main stream，与任一 Thread 字段同时出现都会被拒绝，而不是静默取其中一个。
73	
74	读者已关注时，每个结果还会说出这份 Attention 由什么建立——开了这个 Thread、领了它的 Task、是它的 accountable、拥有这个 Project、在里面被点名，或自己选择关注。Claim 的结果与 Thread start 会说明它们代读者刚建立的 Attention，因此读者不必再问就知道自己现在关注了。
75	
76	Attention 不是 reading。这三个 action 都不渲染 facts、不确认未读、不交写令牌；读也从不改变你是否关注。结果形状只携带地址、scope、Thread 的 Task standing 与 following 状态，别无其他，因此 Attention 结果不可能漂移成展示内容。
77	
78	每条结果都说出动词本身不携带的那个后果。follow 意味着来自那里的普通更新会打断你。unfollow 意味着它们停止，而点名你的 mention、对你的回复和需要你处理的责任事件仍然到达——并且 unfollow 不释放任何 Claim、不放下你 accountable 的 Task，所以它是订阅变化，不是退出工作。该 Task 上持有 active Claim 时会拒绝 Thread 的 unfollow，直到它 done 或 released。行本身的归属见 [Attention 与消息](attention-and-messaging.zh.md)。
79	
80	与 `team_thread` 的拆分正是让读路径完全不带 Attention 逻辑的原因：三个 action 共享同一个参数口袋，而不是借用读的口袋——那里有 `messageRef`、`beforeSequence`、`limit` 三个它们永远用不上的参数。

1	import type { ToolDefinition } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
2	import { apply } from '../src/index.ts'
3	
4	/**
5	 * Shared render-spec harness: registers the Team tools into a throwaway
6	 * registry and renders one structured value to text, because renders are the
7	 * only channel a tool result reaches the model through. Asserting on this
8	 * text — not the schema — is what locks the model-visible contract.
9	 */
10	export function teamTools(): Map<string, ToolDefinition> {
11	  const registered = new Map<string, ToolDefinition>()
12	  apply({ tools: { register: (tool: unknown) => {
13	    const definition = tool as ToolDefinition
14	    registered.set(definition.name, definition)
15	  } } } as never)
16	  return registered
17	}
18	
19	export function renderText(tool: ToolDefinition, args: Record<string, unknown>, value: unknown): string {
20	  const blocks = tool.output.render(args, value as never)
21	  return blocks.map(block => block.type === 'text' ? block.text : '').join('\n')
22	}

24	/** Count how many times a label appears — the "exactly one" discipline for token hand-offs. */
25	export function occurrences(text: string, needle: string): number {
26	  return text.split(needle).length - 1

1	# Start and checks
2	
3	English | [中文](start-and-checks.zh.md)
4	
5	## Scope
6	This document records maintenance workflows for the repository. Exact command definitions remain authoritative in the root `package.json`, package manifests, and `scripts/`; update configuration first when a command changes, then update this document.
7	
8	## Start developing
9	This repository is an independent external DSH bundle. End users install the published package; local development and real Web verification require the adjacent `../deepseek-harness` checkout.
10	
11	```text
12	../
13	├── deepseek-harness/
14	└── dsh-agent-team/
15	```
16	
17	Install dependencies with the command specified by the root README:
18	
19	```sh
20	corepack pnpm install
21	```
22	
23	`pnpm-workspace.yaml` does not declare `packages/*` as workspace members: the repository publishes one root npm package and its three `packages/*` directories are build targets of that one workspace, not independently installable packages. The file is still load-bearing — it disables automatic peer installation and carries the build-approval and release-age settings this repository relies on — so do not change or remove it because a directory lacks its own manifest. The root `node_modules` and adjacent Harness checkout provide the packages and source mappings needed for local development.
24	
25	## Verification gradient
26	Run the smallest sufficient checks for the change:
27	
28	```sh
29	npm run generate:typert
30	npm run typecheck
31	npm run check:docs
32	npm run check:core-skills
33	npm run check:boundaries
34	npm run check:versions
35	npm run check:facades
36	npm test
37	npm run build
38	npm run lint
39	npm run duplication
40	npm pack --dry-run
41	npm run check:artifact
42	npm run check:public-baseline
43	git diff --check HEAD
44	```
45	
46	Their responsibilities are:
47	
48	- `generate:typert` emits Typert Host/Remote artifacts from the Host face in `packages/agent-team/src/`.
49	- `typecheck` regenerates Typert and checks Host, tools, and Client sources.
50	- `check:docs` mechanically enforces the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md): bilingual pairing with a working switcher, a shared heading outline per pair (the same headings at the same levels), relative links, `#fragment` heading anchors, the per-file longest-block ceiling recorded in the script, and both indexes naming exactly the documents that exist. It covers the four README pairs as well — the repository root and one per package — plus the root contributing pair, each set with its own switcher wording. Run it on its own for a documentation-only change.
51	  - `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --budgets` prints the per-file longest-block table instead of deciding.
52	- `check:core-skills` mechanically enforces the shipped skill contract under `packages/agent-team/core-skills/`: the front matter names the skill after its directory and its description names real triggers, the whole skill stays inside the reviewed budget in `scripts/check-core-skills.mjs`, every relative link stays inside the skill directory (an installer copies that directory alone), and every file under `references/` is linked from `SKILL.md`.
53	- `check:boundaries` mechanically enforces the package seams described below: no file under `packages/*/src/` may reach another package by a relative specifier that escapes its own package directory. `import type` is exempt because it is erased before runtime, and test files are out of scope because they deliberately wire directories together. Declared subpaths such as `@contexera/dsh-agent-team/remote` are the supported way to cross a seam.
54	- `check:versions` mechanically enforces the certified-version consistency rule: the CI tag, the setup tag, the development guide, the READMEs, the architecture doc, the compatibility baseline, and the bug-report placeholder must all state the same DSH baseline (in both languages). That baseline must also be the lower bound of every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range. It asserts mutual agreement, never a hardcoded version, so it passes unchanged on every release lane. Run it on its own after touching any version string.
55	- `check:comments` mechanically enforces two comment rules over `packages/*/src` and `scripts/`, excluding `vendor/`. First, a per-scope comment-line budget recorded in the script (see its header). Second, a comment may not cite `.scratch/`, a work-item number, or an acceptance criterion: none of those resolve for a reader of the published package, and work history is not an authority. A bare `issue #<n>` is fine — it resolves to a real GitHub issue — and so is `Task #<n>`, a documented Team entity.
56	- `check:facades` writes nothing: it recomputes the path facades from the adjacent Harness checkout and refuses a committed `tsconfig*.json` or `.generated-harness` marker that differs from the generated output, so a subpath added to `scripts/sync-paths.mjs` cannot land without its regenerated facades. `npm test` runs it, which is why a fresh clone regenerates the facades first (see [`environments-and-install.md`](./environments-and-install.md)).
57	- `test` regenerates Typert, runs `check:facades`, `check:docs`, `check:core-skills`, `check:boundaries`, `check:versions`, and `check:comments`, then runs Vitest. `scripts/isolate-dsh-home.setup.ts` gives each test file an isolated `DSH_HOME`; tests needing a particular home must save and restore it. Startup does not prune ledger-unknown Member directories; explicit Member removal removes that Member's private memory.
58	- The suite pins one time zone (`Asia/Shanghai`, in `vitest.config.ts`), because time rendering is zone-dependent by contract: a seat states the reader's own clock, so the same expectation otherwise reads as a different hour on every runner — UTC in CI, UTC+8 where this is maintained. The pinned zone is deliberately not UTC, which keeps the assertion sharp: a formatter that reaches for `getUTCHours` renders an hour that is not the reader's and fails here. A date-sensitive test may therefore assert a literal clock time rather than read the runner's zone for its expectation.
59	- The Client bench (`packages/client-agent-team/tests/harness.tsx`) fails a spec whose rendered shipped slot entry crashed: the shipped error boundary contains the throw and reports it only through `console.error`, so an unguarded run stays green while the surface is gone. That bench also supplies what jsdom lacks (`ResizeObserver`, `document.fonts`) and the whole `conversation` service face — an absent observable member is not a missing method but a `WeakMap.set(undefined)` throw in the renderer's hook cache.
60	- `build` uses the restricted Node cleaner to clear package `lib/` directories, regenerates Typert, builds all three source trees, and uses Harness `tsdown` for the Client bundle. The published artifact remains one root npm package.
61	- `lint` runs oxlint.
62	- `duplication` runs jscpd over `packages` and `scripts` using `.jscpd.json`; treat its output as a place to look, never as a verdict, because it reports moved and restructured code as readily as copied code.
63	- `pack --dry-run` checks the root bundle's published contents; `prepack` runs the full build first, so it is a release prerequisite rather than an everyday check.
64	- `check:artifact` reads back what `npm pack` would actually ship and refuses an artifact that would ship broken: stray `.ts`/`.tsx` sources, a missing `cordis.patch.yml`, or a runtime relative import whose target is not inside the tarball. That last one is invisible to every local check, because the working tree has every file. Run it after `build` and before publishing.
65	- `check:public-baseline` compares the certified DSH baseline declared by the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers against every public surface that restates it by hand — both READMEs and the pinned compatibility discussion in the Harness repository. A surface it cannot parse is a failure, never a skip, so rewording a README cannot quietly drop it out of coverage. It needs `gh`; `--offline` skips the discussion read and is for local iteration only.
66	
67	Both gates are publish-time checks rather than everyday ones; [`release-runbook.md`](../release-runbook.md) places them in the order a release runs them.
68	
69	Changes affecting browser bundles, Client modules, slots, Remote activation, bundle manifests, or visible UI must also run:
70	
71	```sh
72	npm run test:browser
73	```
74	
75	Visible UI changes touching Team controls or surfaces additionally run the mechanical design-language audit (shipped-reference tripwires included):
76	
77	```sh
78	node scripts/audit-ui-parity.mjs
79	```
80	
81	The audit compares Team Client CSS/TSX against the design-language contract in `docs/frontend-design/principles-and-language.md`: focus visibility, control rhythm, icon semantics, hardcoded colors, and shipped-reference presence. Run it after any visible-UI change and after every DSH upgrade.
82	
83	This builds first, copies built packages into a temporary profile, starts the official Harness Web scaffold, and runs the real journey with `/usr/bin/google-chrome` (override with `CHROME_PATH`). The sandbox setup provisions Playwright's own chromium at that path when the base image ships no browser. It cleans the temporary profile and Harness test files afterward.
84	
85	There are three explicit preview/verification paths:
86	
87	```sh
88	npm run preview:ui                         # keyless Team fixture
89	npm run test:browser                       # repeatable keyless browser acceptance
90	DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... npm run preview       # real model interaction
91	```
92	
93	`preview` and `preview:ui` use temporary profiles and storage and clean up on `Ctrl+C`. `preview` always uses the real DeepSeek adapter and fails when credentials are missing; it does not silently switch to replay. `preview:ui` uses a keyless route-only adapter whose fixture does not call a model; an accidental model request fails explicitly.
94	
95	All three lanes stage this bundle and its declared dependency closure into a temporary profile, then name that staged copy as a profile package — the shape `dsh plugin add` leaves behind: a `file:` dependency, a link under the profile's own `node_modules`, and an entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The scaffold resolves plugin imports from a computed generation built out of `profile.layers`, so only a staged copy named there contributes the Team rows, and they come from the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.
96	
97	A command-line overlay is not an equivalent mount. The Host row's Human-profile form is written to the profile document, and the config editor rejects that write while a later layer (a home patch or a command-line overlay) declares the same row — `overridden by a home patch or command-line overlay` — so the form stays unwritable. A staged bundle the scaffold never names resolves neither its own rows nor its dependency closure: every Team row reports `failed to import` with no module-resolution error to read, and the keyless fixture then fails on an `undefined` `ctx.agentTeam`.
98	
99	`test:browser` does not cover the two preview lanes, so boot them by hand after any change to scaffold composition or profile resolution.
100	
101	The browser journey uses a deterministic keyless Host/Client driver. It covers Agent Inbox reading/replying, Human Project and Thread navigation, persistence after reload, and restoration of the ordinary DSH surface after leaving Team mode.
